nodes.desc: Forces the dev overlay off whether or not it's currently showing - unlike the overlay node itself, which toggles.
nodes.desc_short: Forces the dev overlay off whether or not it's currently showing - unlike the overlay node itself, which...

nodes.title: Easy Debug: Is Overlay On?
nodes.desc: Reports whether the dev overlay panel is currently up. A pure read - it changes nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Reports whether the dev overlay panel is currently up.

returns.name: on
returns.desc: True while the overlay panel is showing.

nodes.title: Easy Debug: Dev Overlay
nodes.desc: Toggles a live panel that follows you around showing the things you constantly need while building a mod: your exact world position and yaw (the number you keep needing to paste into spawn and teleport calls), what your crosshair is on with its name, faction and distance, whether you're on foot or in a vehicle, your health, and how many people and vehicles are nearby. Call it again to hide it. There's deliberately no FPS readout - this refreshes on a timer, so any framerate it printed would be a confidently wrong number.
nodes.desc_short: Toggles a live panel that follows you around showing the things you constantly need while building a mod:...

params.name: opts
params.desc: All optional: x and y (where the panel sits on screen, default 20 and 40), interval (how often it refreshes in seconds, 0.2), radius (how far the nearby-count scan reaches, 40), i (player slot).

returns.name: panel
returns.desc: The panel widget - or nothing at all when the call toggled it back off.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Hide Markers
nodes.desc: Clears the floating coloured icons from over your followers' heads, along with any ground ring showing where you last sent them. It only removes markers this system placed, never anyone else's.
nodes.desc_short: Clears the floating coloured icons from over your followers' heads, along with any ground ring showing where...

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Attack
nodes.desc: Every follower on your roster breaks off and goes after one target. The moment it dies they automatically fall back in behind you - no second order needed.
nodes.desc_short: Every follower on your roster breaks off and goes after one target.

params.name: target
params.desc: Who they attack. The default is whatever your crosshair is resting on right now - aim, then fire this node. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out to the roster.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Board a Vehicle
nodes.desc: Your followers pile into a vehicle. The role defaults to driver rather than passenger on purpose: a follower in the driver's seat keeps taking every later order you give (move, attack, guard) and drives the vehicle there, through the same guid you already hold. Confirmed live - when that order finishes they climb back out and go back to following on foot, exactly like any other order.
nodes.desc_short: Your followers pile into a vehicle.

params.name: vehicleGuid
params.desc: The vehicle to board. The default is whatever you're sitting in right now; wire in the guid a summon or spawn node handed you instead.

params.name: role
params.desc: driver, passenger or gunner. Keep driver if you want to keep steering the vehicle by ordering the follower. A passenger or gunner is still yours to command - they just aren't the vehicle.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out to the roster.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Guard a Spot
nodes.desc: The whole roster digs in around a spot and fights anything that enters it. Guarding has no natural end - they stay there until you order something else.
nodes.desc_short: The whole roster digs in around a spot and fights anything that enters it.

params.name: at
params.desc: The ground to hold, as {x, y, z}. The default { Ess.Player.pose(0) } means right where you're standing.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out to the roster.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Patrol
nodes.desc: The whole roster walks a repeating beat between the points you list, instead of trailing behind you.
nodes.desc_short: The whole roster walks a repeating beat between the points you list, instead of trailing behind you.

params.name: points
params.desc: The route, as a list of {x, y, z} waypoints. Switch on Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read real coordinates off the screen.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out to the roster.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Recruit
nodes.desc: Turns any character in the world into your follower - they fall in behind you and tag along, climbing into vehicles with you on their own, using the game's real recruit mechanic. Once recruited they answer to every Easy Followers order, and they take themselves off the roster automatically when they die.
nodes.desc_short: Turns any character in the world into your follower - they fall in behind you and tag along, climbing into...

params.name: guid
params.desc: Who to recruit. The default is whoever your crosshair is resting on - aim at someone and fire this node. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if they were recruited onto the roster.

nodes.title: Easy Followers: Show Markers
nodes.desc: Puts a floating icon over every follower's head, each one a different colour, and drops a white ground ring wherever you last ordered them - so you can see at a glance who is yours and where you just sent them. Anyone you recruit later gets a marker too.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a floating icon over every follower's head, each one a different colour, and drops a white ground ring...

nodes.title: Easy Fun: Technoviking Dance
nodes.desc: Your character breaks into the technoviking dance on the spot. Pure easter egg - nothing to configure, nothing to undo.
nodes.desc_short: Your character breaks into the technoviking dance on the spot.

nodes.title: Easy Fun: Victory Fanfare
nodes.desc: Plays the game's own mission-complete music sting - or the mission-failed one. The right way to punctuate the end of something you built.
nodes.desc_short: Plays the game's own mission-complete music sting - or the mission-failed one.

params.name: bWin
params.desc: true plays the victory sting, false plays the failure sting.

nodes.title: Easy Human: Give a Weapon
nodes.desc: Puts a weapon straight into someone's hands by name - nothing spawns, nothing has to be walked over. Confirmed to genuinely ADD a weapon to their inventory rather than just re-equip something they already carry. (For a pickup lying on the ground instead, use Easy Spawn: Weapon Pickup.)
nodes.desc_short: Puts a weapon straight into someone's hands by name - nothing spawns, nothing has to be walked over.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: Who gets the weapon. Ess.Player.character(0) is you; wire in any character guid instead.

params.name: sTemplateName
params.desc: The weapon's in-game name, e.g. Grenade Launcher, RPG, Sniper Rifle, Assault Rifle, Minigun, Shotgun, C4, Anti-Material Rifle, Pistol. A name the game doesn't know is refused safely and written to the log.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if that weapon name was found and equipped.

nodes.title: Easy Impulse: Knockback
nodes.desc: Blasts something directly away from a source with a little upward lift - the sent-them-flying feel of an explosion. Mass-scaled, so it looks right on a person or a truck. GOTCHA: unlike Launch and Speed Boost this one has no fallback - with no target guid the call is refused and nothing moves at all.
nodes.desc_short: Blasts something directly away from a source with a little upward lift - the sent-them-flying feel of an...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: Who gets thrown. Required - there's no fallback. The default is whatever your crosshair is on. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

params.name: fromGuid
params.desc: What they get thrown away FROM. Defaults to you, so they fly straight backwards from where you're standing. Point it at an explosion's location instead for a proper blast-wave shove.

params.name: strength
params.desc: How hard the shove is. Default 10 - a few units is a stumble, well past 10 is a full ragdoll launch.

nodes.title: Easy Impulse: Launch Upward
nodes.desc: Pops something straight up into the air - a little hop or a car-flipping launch, depending on the strength you give it.
nodes.desc_short: Pops something straight up into the air - a little hop or a car-flipping launch, depending on the strength...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: What to launch. The default is you. (In hand-written Lua, leaving this out entirely picks the vehicle you're driving, or you on foot.)

params.name: strength
params.desc: The upward kick. Default 12 - try 4 for a hop, 30 for something ridiculous.

nodes.title: Easy Impulse: Speed Boost
nodes.desc: Slams whatever it is forward - the Spy Hunter effect. Mass-scaled, so it feels the same in a bike or a tank.
nodes.desc_short: Slams whatever it is forward - the Spy Hunter effect.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: What to boost. The default is the vehicle you're driving; if you're on foot it quietly falls back to boosting you.

params.name: strength
params.desc: How hard. Default 8 - the original Spy Hunter script used 6 to 8.

nodes.title: Easy Mark: Enemy
nodes.desc: Tags a hostile so they show up on your radar and in your PDA - deliberately with NO floating world icon, matching how the game's own wave-defense script marks enemies (an icon over every enemy clutters the whole screen).
nodes.desc_short: Tags a hostile so they show up on your radar and in your PDA - deliberately with NO floating world icon,...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: Who to mark. The default is whatever your crosshair is on. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: The marker handle - hand it to Ess.Mark.clear to take the mark off again.

nodes.title: Easy Mark: Objective
nodes.desc: Marks something as a real mission objective on all three surfaces at once - radar, PDA, and a floating icon in the world - the same way the game's own contracts mark their targets.
nodes.desc_short: Marks something as a real mission objective on all three surfaces at once - radar, PDA, and a floating icon...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: What to mark as the objective. The default is whatever your crosshair is on. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: The marker handle - hand it to Ess.Mark.clear to take the mark off again.

nodes.title: Easy Mark: Zone Ring
nodes.desc: Draws a glowing ring on the ground at a spot - the go-here disc, with no radar or PDA clutter added.
nodes.desc_short: Draws a glowing ring on the ground at a spot - the go-here disc, with no radar or PDA clutter added.

params.name: x
params.desc: World X of the ring's centre. Use Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read coordinates off the screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: World Y (ground level) of the ring's centre.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z of the ring's centre.

params.name: r
params.desc: The ring's radius in world units. About 8 is a comfortable you-are-here size; go bigger to circle a whole compound.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: The marker handle - hand it to Ess.Mark.clear to remove the ring.

nodes.title: Easy UI: Menu
nodes.desc: Opens a menu on screen right now - one flat list of labelled actions, nothing to configure. Picking an entry runs your function.
nodes.desc_short: Opens a menu on screen right now - one flat list of labelled actions, nothing to configure.

params.name: title
params.desc: The heading across the top of the menu.

params.name: entries
params.default: { {"Summon a car", function() Ess.Easy.Vehicle.summon("Veyron") end}, {"Big boom", function() Ess.Easy.Spawn.explosion() end} }
params.desc: The choices, as {label, action} pairs in the order you want them listed. One flat level only - for nested sub-menus use Ess.UI.Menu directly instead.

returns.name: menu
returns.desc: The open menu object.

nodes.title: Easy Objective: Counted Goal
nodes.desc: Puts a counted goal on the HUD objective line - Collect the intel 0/5 - that ticks up each time you advance it and fires your callback the moment it's met. This is the MANUAL kind: nothing moves it but your own script. For goals that watch the world themselves, use the reach, destroy, clear or survive variants.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a counted goal on the HUD objective line - Collect the intel 0/5 - that ticks up each time you advance...

params.name: label
params.desc: The text shown on the HUD objective line.

params.name: target
params.desc: How many times it has to be advanced before it counts as done. This is a COUNT, not a thing in the world. 1 makes it a plain do-this-once goal; anything above 1 shows a running counter on the HUD.

params.name: onComplete
params.desc: Runs the moment the count is reached.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live objective - call advance on it to tick it up, or complete / cancel to end it early.

nodes.title: Easy Objective: Clear the Area
nodes.desc: The eliminate-everyone-here goal. It rings the area on the ground, counts the enemies inside it, and updates the HUD line as they drop (Clear the area   4 left), completing when the last one falls. It works by counting the area's population once a second - the engine has no clean per-kill event, so this is the honest way to detect area cleared, bundled up for you.
nodes.desc_short: The eliminate-everyone-here goal.

params.name: x
params.desc: World X of the area's centre. Use Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read coordinates off the screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: World Y (ground level) of the area's centre.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z of the area's centre.

params.name: r
params.desc: How wide the area is, in world units. Default 40 - roughly a compound.

params.name: faction
params.desc: Which side to count, e.g. VZ, Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate. Leave it out to count every human inside the radius no matter whose side they're on.

params.name: label
params.desc: The HUD text. The live count is appended to it automatically.

params.name: onDone
params.desc: Runs when the last one inside the ring is dead.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live objective - cancel it if the mission moves on before the area is cleared.

nodes.title: Easy Objective: Destroy Target
nodes.desc: A destroy-this goal wired to one specific object you already hold: it marks the target on radar, PDA and in the world, and completes the instant that object dies - cleaning its own marker up afterwards.
nodes.desc_short: A destroy-this goal wired to one specific object you already hold: it marks the target on radar, PDA and in...

params.name: guid
params.desc: The object that has to die. The default is whatever your crosshair is on; normally you wire in the guid a spawn node handed you. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

params.name: label
params.desc: The text shown on the HUD objective line.

params.name: onDone
params.desc: Runs the moment the target is destroyed.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live objective - cancel it if the mission moves on first.

nodes.title: Easy Objective: Reach a Point
nodes.desc: A go-here goal in one node: it drops a glowing ring on the ground so the player can see where, puts the label on the HUD, and completes the moment they walk inside it - then clears its own marker. One node instead of hand-wiring an area trigger, a marker, a goal and its teardown.
nodes.desc_short: A go-here goal in one node: it drops a glowing ring on the ground so the player can see where, puts the label...

params.name: x
params.desc: World X of the destination. Use Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read coordinates off the screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: World Y (ground level) of the destination.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z of the destination.

params.name: r
params.desc: How close counts as arrived, in world units. Default 8 - a comfortable you're-here radius.

params.name: label
params.desc: The text shown on the HUD objective line.

params.name: onDone
params.desc: Runs the moment the player steps inside the ring.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live objective - cancel it if the mission moves on first.

nodes.title: Easy Objective: Survive N Seconds
nodes.desc: A live countdown on the HUD objective line (Survive   12s) that completes when it runs out - and FAILS if the local player dies before it does. The player watches the clock without you building any extra HUD.
nodes.desc_short: A live countdown on the HUD objective line (Survive 12s) that completes when it runs out - and FAILS if the...

params.name: seconds
params.desc: How long they have to last, in seconds. Default 30; anything under 1 is clamped up to 1.

params.name: label
params.desc: The HUD text. The remaining seconds are appended to it automatically.

params.name: onDone
params.desc: Runs when the timer runs out with the player still alive.

params.name: onFail
params.desc: Runs instead if the player dies before the clock does.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live objective - cancel it to stop the clock early.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Free Support
nodes.desc: Switches off every stock count and unlock requirement on the airstrike and support menu, so you can call anything in, as often as you like, for nothing. This is the game's own cheat-menu function.
nodes.desc_short: Switches off every stock count and unlock requirement on the airstrike and support menu, so you can call...

params.name: bOn
params.desc: true makes support free, false puts the normal stock and unlock rules back.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Ghost Mode
nodes.desc: Stealth mode - drops your AI detectability to the engine's own floor so enemy perception mostly stops noticing you, and toasts on screen to confirm. Calling it again (or passing false) restores your original value EXACTLY, because it remembers the number it replaced. Honest limit: flooring detectability is confirmed reversible in game, but whether it makes AI genuinely blind or merely very short-sighted hasn't been measured yet.
nodes.desc_short: Stealth mode - drops your AI detectability to the engine's own floor so enemy perception mostly stops...

params.name: bOn
params.desc: true to go dark, false to restore your original detectability exactly. (In hand-written Lua, calling it with no argument at all toggles.)

params.name: i
params.desc: Player slot: 0 is you (the local player), 1 is your co-op partner.

returns.name: on
returns.desc: Whether ghost mode is on after this call.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Give All Rewards
nodes.desc: Dispenses every unlock reward in the game at once - the same cheat-menu function the game itself uses.
nodes.desc_short: Dispenses every unlock reward in the game at once - the same cheat-menu function the game itself uses.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Give Grappling Hook
nodes.desc: Unlocks the grappling hook and puts it on your character right now.
nodes.desc_short: Unlocks the grappling hook and puts it on your character right now.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Change Skin
nodes.desc: Swaps your character's entire look for another figure in the game - be Fiona, a VZ soldier, a beach civilian, a police officer. GOTCHAS: it's whole-figure only (individual body parts don't work), a level reload puts your normal look back, and a freshly skinned model's bones aren't ready for about a third of a second, so wait a beat before gluing bone effects onto a just-skinned character.
nodes.desc_short: Swaps your character's entire look for another figure in the game - be Fiona, a VZ soldier, a beach civilian,...

params.name: sCode
params.desc: The model code. Confirmed ones include pmc_hum_fiona, pmc_hum_eva, pmc_hum_diablo, vz_hum_solano, al_hum_boss, ch_hum_boss, gr_hum_boss, civ_hum_beachfemale_a and police_hum_officer_b - around thirty more exist.

params.name: i
params.desc: Player slot to re-skin: 0 is you (the local player), 1 is your co-op partner.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Unlock All HQs
nodes.desc: Unlocks every HQ and outpost on the map at once.
nodes.desc_short: Unlocks every HQ and outpost on the map at once.

nodes.title: Easy Player: Unlock Fast Travel
nodes.desc: Unlocks every landing zone, so you can fast-travel anywhere on the map immediately.
nodes.desc_short: Unlocks every landing zone, so you can fast-travel anywhere on the map immediately.

nodes.title: Easy Quest: Linear Mission
nodes.desc: A whole linear mission in one node: an ordered list of goals, shown one at a time on the HUD objective line. Steps can wire themselves to the world (arrive somewhere, blow something up, clear an area) or be manual ones you finish yourself. Lighter than a full contract, far more than a bare HUD line.
nodes.desc_short: A whole linear mission in one node: an ordered list of goals, shown one at a time on the HUD objective line.

params.name: steps
params.desc: The mission, in order. Each step is either { reach = {x,y,z,radius}, label = ... }, { destroy = someGuid, label = ... } or { clear = {x,y,z,radius,"VZ"}, label = ... } to complete itself off a world event, or just a plain string for a manual step you finish by calling advance on the quest.

params.name: onComplete
params.desc: Runs when the last step is done. The default plays the victory sting.

returns.name: quest
returns.desc: The running quest - advance, skip or cancel it, or ask which step it's on.

nodes.title: Easy Relations: Make Allies
nodes.desc: Every faction in your list becomes allied with every other one in it - they stop shooting each other and fight side by side. GUARDRAIL: this Easy tier keeps exactly ONE relation set alive at a time, so calling any Easy Relations node again first puts the previous one back. It can't leak or stack. Use Ess.Relations directly if you need several sets at once.
nodes.desc_short: Every faction in your list becomes allied with every other one in it - they stop shooting each other and...

params.name: factionList
params.desc: The factions to pair up, as a list of names. Valid names: Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ and PMC (PMC is you).

nodes.title: Easy Relations: Make Hostile to You
nodes.desc: Every faction you list turns on YOU - on PMC - and the change is registered properly so the HUD's attitude display reflects it. One node and half the map wants you dead. GUARDRAIL: only one Easy relation set is alive at a time; calling another Easy Relations node first restores this one.
nodes.desc_short: Every faction you list turns on YOU - on PMC - and the change is registered properly so the HUD's attitude...

params.name: factionList
params.desc: Who turns on you, as a list of faction names. Valid names: Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ.

nodes.title: Easy Relations: Restore
nodes.desc: Puts faction relations back exactly as they were before your last Easy Relations call. Safe to fire at any time - if no Easy relation set is active it simply does nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Puts faction relations back exactly as they were before your last Easy Relations call.

nodes.title: Easy Relations: Side With
nodes.desc: Picks your side in one node: you ally with one faction, go hostile to the other, and set those two at war with each other. The whole stance for I'm helping this lot crush that lot - e.g. side with China against the Allies and back their assault on the Allied refinery.
nodes.desc_short: Picks your side in one node: you ally with one faction, go hostile to the other, and set those two at war...

params.name: friend
params.desc: The faction you're backing. One of Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ.

params.name: foe
params.desc: The faction you're both turning on. One of Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ.

nodes.title: Easy Relations: Start a War
nodes.desc: Sets two factions at each other's throats with you left out of it entirely - a firefight you can stand back and watch. This is the case Make Hostile can't express, because Make Hostile always means hostile to you.
nodes.desc_short: Sets two factions at each other's throats with you left out of it entirely - a firefight you can stand back...

params.name: a
params.desc: One side of the war. One of Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ.

params.name: b
params.desc: The other side. One of Allied, China, Guerilla, OC, Pirate, VZ.

nodes.title: Easy Sandbox: Begin Arena
nodes.desc: Walls off a temporary playground with every protection on at once: your cash is banked away and restored exactly afterwards, the support menu is isolated, faction relations are snapshotted, world layers are managed - and SAVING IS BLOCKED for the whole duration, so a crash mid-arena just leaves your normal game untouched. Everything is guaranteed restored by Easy Sandbox: Done.
nodes.desc_short: Walls off a temporary playground with every protection on at once: your cash is banked away and restored...

params.name: id
params.desc: A name for this sandbox - pass the same one to Easy Sandbox: Done to end it. Beginning an id that's already running does nothing.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Optional: startCash (what your wallet holds inside the arena - your real balance is restored on finish either way) and relations (a list of {factionA, factionB, stance} to apply only for the arena).

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: False if that id was already running, or if nothing could actually be isolated (a typo'd provider name).

nodes.title: Easy Sandbox: Done
nodes.desc: Ends the arena and restores everything it touched - your cash, the support menu, faction relations, layers - and lets the game save again.
nodes.desc_short: Ends the arena and restores everything it touched - your cash, the support menu, faction relations, layers -...

params.name: id
params.desc: The same name you gave Easy Sandbox: Begin Arena.

nodes.title: Easy Sound: Play a Cue
nodes.desc: Fires a one-shot sound effect straight at the player with no world position - the UI beep, alert or sting case. (For a sound coming out of an object in the world, use Ess.Sound.cue with its guid.)
nodes.desc_short: Fires a one-shot sound effect straight at the player with no world position - the UI beep, alert or sting case.

params.name: sCueName
params.desc: The game's internal name for the sound cue. The framework confirms no cue names of its own, so you need a real one from the game's sound bank - see the string catalog at wiki.mercs2.tools/reference.html. An empty or unknown name is ignored safely and written to the log.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Shell On My Head
nodes.desc: Drops a live artillery shell out of the sky onto your own position from 250 units up - the classic sandbox gag. It's real, impact-fused, lethal ordnance and it is aimed squarely at you.
nodes.desc_short: Drops a live artillery shell out of the sky onto your own position from 250 units up - the classic sandbox gag.

params.name: sRound
params.desc: Which round falls. Confirmed: Artillery Shell (default), Gunship Shell, Cluster Bomb Projectile, Cruise Missile Projectile, Bomb.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Supply Crate
nodes.desc: A supply crate parachutes down just in front of you - spawned high on purpose so it drifts in under its chute exactly the way the game's own bounty crates do.
nodes.desc_short: A supply crate parachutes down just in front of you - spawned high on purpose so it drifts in under its chute...

params.name: sType
params.desc: Which crate falls. Confirmed types: Supply Drop (Light MG) (default), Supply Drop (Blueprints), Supply Drop (Treasure).

returns.name: crate
returns.desc: The crate that appeared - wire it into other nodes. Nothing comes back if the template name was wrong.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Enemy Squad
nodes.desc: A squad of hostiles drops in a short way ahead of you and immediately comes at you - an instant firefight in one node. It hands back their guids so you can keep ordering or tracking them afterwards.
nodes.desc_short: A squad of hostiles drops in a short way ahead of you and immediately comes at you - an instant firefight in...

params.name: nCount
params.desc: How many spawn. They're laid out three to a row, so 3 is a line abreast and 6 is two ranks. Default 3.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Optional: template (who spawns - VZ Soldier is the confirmed one), dist (how far ahead of you, 14), spread (how far apart, 3), attack (set false and they just stand there instead of charging you), target (who they go for; you by default).

returns.name: guids
returns.desc: A Lua list of the units that spawned - wire it into an AI Orders node to command them further.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Explosion
nodes.desc: A real explosion goes off about ten units in front of you - placed ahead rather than in your face so it's dramatic without instantly killing you. These are genuine, damaging blasts; don't stand in them.
nodes.desc_short: A real explosion goes off about ten units in front of you - placed ahead rather than in your face so it's...

params.name: sType
params.desc: How big a bang. Confirmed types: Explosion (Grenade) (default), Explosion (C4), Explosion (MOAB), Explosion (Rocket Artillery), fx_Explosion_Huge.

returns.name: guid
returns.desc: The spawned explosion object. Nothing comes back if the template name was wrong.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Effect at a Point
nodes.desc: Puts a particle effect at a world position. One-shot effects clean themselves up when they finish; ambient ones like a smoke plume keep going until you remove them yourself with Ess.Object.remove.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a particle effect at a world position.

params.name: sTemplate
params.desc: Which effect. Confirmed names: fx_Explosion_Huge, global_particle_explosion_c4, global_particle_env_smokeplume_distance_tall, plus the whole Explosion (...) family.

params.name: x
params.desc: World X to put it. Use Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read coordinates off the screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: World Y (height) to put it.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z to put it.

returns.name: guid
returns.desc: The spawned effect. Nothing comes back if the template name was wrong.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Effect on an Object
nodes.desc: Sticks an effect on an object. Give it a bone name and the effect is GLUED there and travels with them - smoke pouring off a running man. Leave the bone out and it's a one-shot fired at wherever they happen to be standing, which will NOT follow them. You have to supply the bone name yourself, since only you know your model's bones: a character's real bones work, vehicle hardpoints don't bind at all.
nodes.desc_short: Sticks an effect on an object.

params.name: sTemplate
params.desc: Which effect. Confirmed names: fx_Explosion_Huge, global_particle_explosion_c4, global_particle_env_smokeplume_distance_tall, plus the whole Explosion (...) family.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: What to put the effect on. Ess.Player.character(0) is you.

params.name: sBone
params.desc: The bone to glue it to, e.g. Bone_Chest on a character - the effect then follows them around. Leave it out entirely for a one-shot at their current position that stays behind. Remove a glued one with Ess.Bones.detachFX.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: The effect handle - pass a glued one to Ess.Bones.detachFX to take it off again.

nodes.title: Easy Spawn: Weapon Pickup
nodes.desc: Drops a weapon pickup on the ground just in front of you - walk over it to grab it. (To put one straight into someone's hands instead, use Easy Human: Give a Weapon.)
nodes.desc_short: Drops a weapon pickup on the ground just in front of you - walk over it to grab it.

params.name: sName
params.desc: Which weapon. Confirmed names: RPG (default), Sniper Rifle, Assault Rifle, Minigun, Shotgun, Grenade Launcher, C4, Anti-Material Rifle, Pistol.

returns.name: pickup
returns.desc: The pickup lying on the ground. Nothing comes back if the template name was wrong.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Assign Role
nodes.desc: Tags one squad member with a role. Roles are just labels and nothing enforces them - but Mount Up reads them: whoever you tag as driver claims the driver's seat before anyone else can take it.
nodes.desc_short: Tags one squad member with a role.

params.name: guid
params.desc: Which member to tag. The default is whoever your crosshair is on. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

params.name: roleType
params.desc: A free-form label. driver is the one the framework actually acts on; anything else (heavy, medic, gunner) is purely yours to read back later.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the role was recorded.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Cancel Queue
nodes.desc: Aborts a team's running step sequence part-way through and drops them straight back to following you - the safe fallback.
nodes.desc_short: Aborts a team's running step sequence part-way through and drops them straight back to following you - the...

params.name: teamName
params.desc: The team whose plan you're calling off - the same name you gave Create Team.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if a queue was found and cancelled.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Clear Formation
nodes.desc: Stops holding a formation. The squad simply stays wherever they were standing when you called it - nothing marches them back.
nodes.desc_short: Stops holding a formation.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: The team to release - the same name you gave Create Team.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the formation was stopped.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Create Team
nodes.desc: Carves a named team out of your followers so you can order that group on its own instead of the whole roster. GOTCHA: only units already recruited as followers make it in - anyone else in your list is silently dropped. Teams look after themselves: a member who dies or is dismissed falls out of the team automatically.
nodes.desc_short: Carves a named team out of your followers so you can order that group on its own instead of the whole roster.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: What to call this team. You use this name in every other Easy Squad node. (The name __all__ is reserved and will be refused.)

params.name: guids
params.desc: The members, as a Lua list of guids. Ess.Followers.list() is everyone you currently have; wire in a subset to split your roster into two teams.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the team was defined.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Dismount and Secure
nodes.desc: The team piles out of whatever they're riding and sets up a defensive perimeter on the spot. A gotcha the framework already handles for you: the engine's own deploy only ejects PASSENGERS - the driver stays glued to the wheel - so this explicitly kicks the driver out too, then waits two seconds for everyone to actually get clear before the defend order lands.
nodes.desc_short: The team piles out of whatever they're riding and sets up a defensive perimeter on the spot.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: The team to disgorge - the same name you gave Create Team.

params.name: atPos
params.desc: Where the perimeter goes, as {x, y, z}. The default { Ess.Player.pose(0) } means right where you're standing.

params.name: radius
params.desc: How wide a perimeter they hold, in world units. Default 15.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the team had anyone to dismount.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Mount Up
nodes.desc: The whole team boards one vehicle, in the right order: anyone you tagged with the driver role gets in first so nobody else steals the wheel, and everyone else piles in as passengers. If the vehicle is full or the way is blocked it quietly gives up after about 20 seconds - a real, expected outcome here, not an error.
nodes.desc_short: The whole team boards one vehicle, in the right order: anyone you tagged with the driver role gets in first...

params.name: vehGuid
params.desc: The vehicle they board. The default is whatever you're sitting in; wire in the guid a summon or spawn node handed you instead.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: The team to load - the same name you gave Create Team. (A raw Lua list of guids works here too.)

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the boarding orders went out.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Team Attack
nodes.desc: Just this team peels off to attack a target - your other teams carry on doing whatever they were already doing. When the target dies, this team falls back in behind you on its own.
nodes.desc_short: Just this team peels off to attack a target - your other teams carry on doing whatever they were already doing.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team goes in - the same name you gave Create Team.

params.name: target
params.desc: Who they attack. The default is whatever your crosshair is on - aim, then fire this node. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out. False if the team is empty or unknown.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Team Follow
nodes.desc: Sends one team back to following you. Vehicle-aware, and that matters: a member who's currently DRIVING gets an escort route instead of being told to climb out and follow on foot, and passengers and gunners are left completely alone. This is the fix for the gunner jumps out the instant an order finishes problem.
nodes.desc_short: Sends one team back to following you.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team comes back to you - the same name you gave Create Team.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out. False if the team is empty or unknown.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Team Guard
nodes.desc: This team digs in at a spot and fights anything that enters it, while your other teams keep their own orders. Guarding never finishes on its own - they hold until you order something else.
nodes.desc_short: This team digs in at a spot and fights anything that enters it, while your other teams keep their own orders.

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team holds the ground - the same name you gave Create Team.

params.name: at
params.desc: The ground to hold, as {x, y, z}. The default { Ess.Player.pose(0) } means right where you're standing.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out. False if the team is empty or unknown.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Team Patrol
nodes.desc: This team walks a repeating route between your waypoints while the rest of your followers get on with their own orders.
nodes.desc_short: This team walks a repeating route between your waypoints while the rest of your followers get on with their...

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team walks the beat - the same name you gave Create Team.

params.name: points
params.desc: The route, as a list of {x, y, z} waypoints. Switch on Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read real coordinates off the screen.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the order went out. False if the team is empty or unknown.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Queue a Plan
nodes.desc: Runs a team through a multi-step plan, waiting for each step to genuinely finish before starting the next: board the truck, wait until everyone's seated, drive to the LZ, wait for arrival, pile out. Every step also carries a watchdog (30 seconds unless you say otherwise) so one stuck unit or blocked path can never freeze the sequence forever. HONEST LIMIT: only move, non-looping patrol, attack and enter have real completion signals - a guard or hold step just runs out its timeout before the plan moves on.
nodes.desc_short: Runs a team through a multi-step plan, waiting for each step to genuinely finish before starting the next:...

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team runs the plan - the same name you gave Create Team. (A raw Lua list of guids works here too.)

params.name: steps
params.default: { { behavior = "move", opts = { at = { Ess.Player.pose(0) } } }, { behavior = "defend", opts = { at = { Ess.Player.pose(0) }, radius = 15 } } }
params.desc: The plan in order, as a list of { behavior = ..., opts = { ... }, timeout = seconds }. Behaviors are the AI order names: move, attack, patrol, defend, hold, enter, deploy, follow, face, flee, animate. The default is come to me, then hold this ground.

params.name: onComplete
params.desc: Runs once the last step is done. (For an onCancel handler or per-step timeouts, drop to Ess.Squad.queue directly.)

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the plan started.

nodes.title: Easy Squad: Set Formation
nodes.desc: The team spreads into a shape around you and holds it as you move - a wedge fanned out ahead, single file in a column, a flat line, or a diamond ringing you completely. It's visual sugar rather than a precision tactical system: underneath, it's units walking to waypoints that get recomputed every tick as you move.
nodes.desc_short: The team spreads into a shape around you and holds it as you move - a wedge fanned out ahead, single file in...

params.name: teamName
params.desc: Which team forms up - the same name you gave Create Team.

params.name: formationType
params.desc: wedge (a V opening forward, the default), column (single file behind you), line (a flat wall abreast) or diamond (a full 360-degree ring around you).

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the formation took hold.

nodes.title: Easy Time: Slow Motion
nodes.desc: Drops the game into bullet time and puts it back by itself a few seconds later - the finisher-moment beat you want right on an explosion. The countdown to the restore runs in REAL seconds, deliberately not slowed itself, so it always comes back exactly when you expect.
nodes.desc_short: Drops the game into bullet time and puts it back by itself a few seconds later - the finisher-moment beat you...

params.name: n
params.desc: How slow, as a multiplier of normal speed. Default 0.2 (one fifth speed); 0.5 is a gentle sag, 0.05 is nearly frozen.

params.name: seconds
params.desc: How long the slow motion lasts, in real seconds. Default 2.

nodes.title: Easy UI: Toast
nodes.desc: Flashes a short notification on screen and forgets about it. The simplest possible way to prove your script actually ran.
nodes.desc_short: Flashes a short notification on screen and forgets about it.

params.name: msg
params.desc: The line of text to flash up. Anything you pass is turned into text for you.

nodes.title: Easy Triggers: After N Seconds
nodes.desc: Waits, then runs your code once. The whole do-this-in-a-moment thought in one node - a delayed explosion, a reinforcement wave, a line of dialogue after a beat.
nodes.desc_short: Waits, then runs your code once.

params.name: seconds
params.desc: How long to wait before firing, in seconds.

params.name: fn
params.desc: The code that runs when the time is up. It fires once and the trigger is done.

returns.name: cancel
returns.desc: Call it to disarm the timer before it ever fires.

nodes.title: Easy Triggers: On Death
nodes.desc: Watches one object and runs your code the moment it's destroyed - the enemy commander drops and the gates open. Fires once.
nodes.desc_short: Watches one object and runs your code the moment it's destroyed - the enemy commander drops and the gates open.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: What to watch. The default is whatever your crosshair is on; normally you wire in the guid a spawn node handed you. (The wrapping parentheses matter: they trim the extra values that call returns.)

params.name: fn
params.desc: The code that runs the instant it dies.

returns.name: cancel
returns.desc: Call it to disarm the trigger before it ever fires.

nodes.title: Easy Triggers: On Player Near
nodes.desc: Arms an invisible tripwire at a spot: the moment the player comes within the radius, your code runs. The ambush-when-they-arrive node.
nodes.desc_short: Arms an invisible tripwire at a spot: the moment the player comes within the radius, your code runs.

params.name: x
params.desc: World X of the tripwire's centre. Use Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay() in game to read coordinates off the screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: World Y (ground level) of the tripwire's centre.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z of the tripwire's centre.

params.name: r
params.desc: How close the player has to get before it fires, in world units. Nothing is drawn on screen - add Easy Mark: Zone Ring if you want them to see it.

params.name: fn
params.desc: The code that runs when they walk in. The default drops an ambush squad on them.

returns.name: cancel
returns.desc: Call it to disarm the tripwire before it ever fires.

nodes.title: Easy Vehicle: Summon
nodes.desc: The one-liner this whole namespace exists for: a vehicle appears a short way in front of you and you're already in the driver's seat. It spawns slightly airborne on purpose, so a helicopter is hovering the instant you have the controls and a ground vehicle just drops and settles. A template name the game doesn't know spawns nothing and logs which name failed.
nodes.desc_short: The one-liner this whole namespace exists for: a vehicle appears a short way in front of you and you're...

params.name: sTemplate
params.desc: The vehicle's in-game name, e.g. UH1 Transport (a helicopter you're flying immediately), AH1Z (Full) (a fully armed attack helicopter) or Veyron (a supercar).

params.name: opts
params.desc: Optional: dist (how far ahead it appears, default 18), height (how high above the ground, 10), useView = true to put it where you're LOOKING rather than where your body is turned.

returns.name: vehicle
returns.desc: The vehicle that appeared - wire it into other nodes. Nothing comes back if the template name was wrong.

nodes.title: Easy World: Brightness
nodes.desc: Turns the world's light level up or down. It STICKS: crossing into a new zone would normally reset the lighting, so a small keeper watches for that and snaps your setting straight back - it survives driving right across the map until you call Reset Atmosphere. REGION-GATED: it only shows while you're standing in a real map region, not inside the HQ.
nodes.desc_short: Turns the world's light level up or down.

params.name: n
params.desc: The light level. 1 is normal daylight, 0.05 is near-black, above 1 blows the picture out. Try 0.15 for a blackout.

nodes.title: Easy World: Clear Wanted Level
nodes.desc: Every police and faction pursuit on you drops instantly - you go from hunted to cold in one node. This is a one-shot clear, though: fresh heat can start building again straight away. Use Easy World: No Pursuit if you want to stay cold.
nodes.desc_short: Every police and faction pursuit on you drops instantly - you go from hunted to cold in one node.

nodes.title: Easy World: Day
nodes.desc: Makes it daytime and holds it there, undoing a night lock in one node. Same honest warning as Easy World: Night - parts of the map paint their own sky and simply ignore the clock, so the look can change on you at a boundary. Release it with Easy World: Unlock Time Of Day.
nodes.desc_short: Makes it daytime and holds it there, undoing a night lock in one node.

nodes.title: Easy World: Freeze Time
nodes.desc: Stops the day/night clock dead, so the lighting holds wherever it is now instead of drifting. THIS IS THE RELIABLE ONE: unlike forcing it to be night, freezing genuinely works across the whole map - the speed of the day is global and the map's own sky presets leave it alone, verified live across a region boundary with nothing re-applying it. It is usually what you actually wanted anyway: keeping the light steady through a scripted sequence so a cutscene or a timed objective does not wander into dusk halfway through. Two notes - it holds whatever time is on screen rather than choosing one for you, and there is no undo, because the game's original pace cannot be read back (reload the level to get it).
nodes.desc_short: Stops the day/night clock dead, so the lighting holds wherever it is now instead of drifting.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the cycle was frozen.

nodes.title: Easy World: Hellscape
nodes.desc: The world goes dark and blood-red in one node - the ready-made preset. It sticks across zone changes, and Easy World: Reset Atmosphere puts it back. REGION-GATED: it only shows while you're standing in a real map region, not inside the HQ.
nodes.desc_short: The world goes dark and blood-red in one node - the ready-made preset.

nodes.title: Easy World: Lock Time Of Day
nodes.desc: Pins the time of day at any point you like and holds it there: it freezes the cycle, sets the time, then quietly re-sets it ten times a second so the world cannot drag it away. It deliberately hammers away even mid-change - an earlier version politely waited, which handed the engine a full second of uncontested daylight followed by a jarring snap back, while re-pinning constantly makes crossing a boundary barely noticeable. It still is not truly map-wide: a part of the map with its own authored sky overrides the clock entirely and no amount of re-asserting can win, because the clock is not what is being contested. Release it with Easy World: Unlock Time Of Day.
nodes.desc_short: Pins the time of day at any point you like and holds it there: it freezes the cycle, sets the time, then...

params.name: n
params.desc: Where in the day to pin the clock, as a fraction from 0 to 1 rather than an hour. 0.95 reads as night, 0.30 as daytime. Leave it empty and you get night.

nodes.title: Easy World: Night
nodes.desc: Makes it night and holds it there - one node, no setup. It parks the clock at night, stops it moving, and quietly keeps re-setting it so it stays put. Honest warning, because this one surprises people: it is not reliably map-wide. Parts of the map have their own authored sky that ignores the clock entirely, so driving into one can hand you full daylight back. It holds fine in the large stretches between them. If what you really wanted was 'stop the light changing', use Easy World: Freeze Time instead - that one genuinely works everywhere.
nodes.desc_short: Makes it night and holds it there - one node, no setup.

nodes.title: Easy World: No Pursuit
nodes.desc: Kills the chase you're in AND keeps new heat from building, so you stay cold - the whole thought in one node. Pass false to hand normal pursuit behaviour back. Note it only blocks heat the world generates on its own; a pursuit a script starts deliberately was never blocked either way.
nodes.desc_short: Kills the chase you're in AND keeps new heat from building, so you stay cold - the whole thought in one node.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: true stops the current chase and keeps new heat off, false restores normal pursuit behaviour.

nodes.title: Easy World: Remove Map Boundary
nodes.desc: Tears down the invisible wall that fences you into the story-unlocked part of the map, along with Fiona's warning and the screen static. Drive anywhere. GOTCHAS: there's no clean way to put it back, and it's host-authoritative - it works in single-player and for a co-op HOST but does nothing at all on a co-op CLIENT (use Ess.Player.removeBoundaries there instead).
nodes.desc_short: Tears down the invisible wall that fences you into the story-unlocked part of the map, along with Fiona's...

nodes.title: Easy World: Reset Atmosphere
nodes.desc: Stops the keeper and lets the world's own natural lighting and colour come back, undoing any tint, brightness change or hellscape you applied.
nodes.desc_short: Stops the keeper and lets the world's own natural lighting and colour come back, undoing any tint, brightness...

nodes.title: Easy World: Set Time Speed
nodes.desc: Speeds up or slows down the day/night cycle - a fast-forward knob for the sky, with 0 stopping it entirely. Like Easy World: Freeze Time this is the dependable half of time control and holds map-wide, unlike forcing a particular time of day. There is no undo: the engine will let you set the speed but never tells you what it was, so the game's own pace is gone until you reload the level.
nodes.desc_short: Speeds up or slows down the day/night cycle - a fast-forward knob for the sky, with 0 stopping it entirely.

params.name: n
params.desc: How fast the day runs. 0 stops it. Do not read 1 as 'normal' - it is far faster than the game's own pace, a full day in a few seconds, so a natural-looking cycle means a much smaller number found by experiment.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the speed was applied. False only if you gave it something that was not a number.

nodes.title: Easy World: Tint
nodes.desc: Washes the whole world in a colour. It STICKS across zone changes - a keeper re-applies it the instant a new zone tries to overwrite it - until you call Reset Atmosphere. REGION-GATED: it only shows while you're standing in a real map region, not inside the HQ.
nodes.desc_short: Washes the whole world in a colour.

params.name: r
params.desc: Red, from 0 to 255. Default 220.

params.name: g
params.desc: Green, from 0 to 255. Default 30.

params.name: b
params.desc: Blue, from 0 to 255. Default 30 - the three defaults together give the deep red used by the hellscape preset.

nodes.title: Easy World: Unlock Time Of Day
nodes.desc: Releases a time lock set by Easy World: Night, Day or Lock Time Of Day, stopping the little keeper that was holding the sky in place. By design it leaves the sky exactly where it is rather than snapping anywhere. It deliberately will NOT guess a 'back to normal' speed for you: the engine can set the speed of the day but offers no way to read what it was, so the original pace cannot be recovered - and 1 is emphatically not normal, it is a whole day in a few seconds. If you need the game's real pace back, reload the level.
nodes.desc_short: Releases a time lock set by Easy World: Night, Day or Lock Time Of Day, stopping the little keeper that was...

params.name: nSpeed
params.desc: The speed to restart the day/night cycle at. Leave it at 0, or leave the socket empty, and the sky simply stays frozen where the lock left it. Put a number above 0 here to get the cycle moving again - start well below 1, since 1 races a whole day past in seconds.

nodes.title: Event: Unhook
nodes.desc: Deletes a hook made by Event: Hook Engine Event. Engine hooks are never cleaned up for you, so every hook a feature makes needs one of these when the feature ends - or a tracker doing it for you.
nodes.desc_short: Deletes a hook made by Event: Hook Engine Event.

params.name: handle
params.desc: The handle the hook node handed back. Wire it in; an empty one just does nothing.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if a hook was actually deleted. False means the handle was empty or already gone - harmless, but a sign you are unhooking twice.

nodes.title: Event: Hook Engine Event
nodes.desc:
Wires an action to a raw engine event, for the cases the On: nodes do not cover. This is the low-level door, so it is easy to get wrong.

THE TRAP: if the arguments do not match the shape that event expects, nothing errors and nothing is logged - the hook simply never fires. When a handler seems dead, it is almost always this, not your action.
nodes.desc_short: Wires an action to a raw engine event, for the cases the On: nodes do not cover.

params.name: eventType
params.desc: The engine's event constant, typed as code and NOT in quotes - Event.ObjectDeath, Event.TimerRelative, and so on. Quoting it gives you a hook that never fires.

params.name: args
params.desc: The arguments that event expects, as a Lua list. Every event wants its own shape and getting it wrong fails silently - check the event's wiki page rather than guessing.

params.name: cb
params.desc: What to run when it fires. What it is handed depends on the event.

params.name: tracker
params.desc: Optional. Wire in a tracker from Track: New and this hook is torn down with everything else in that bin, instead of you having to remember it separately.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: The hook's handle, or nothing if it could not be created (that failure IS logged). Keep it and pass it to Event: Unhook, or you have no way to turn this off.

nodes.title: Followers: Current Waypoint (debug)
nodes.desc: A live-map diagnostic. When a follower is escorting you as a vehicle driver, or catching back up to you on foot after an order, the system walks them toward an invisible marker post that it repositions every second. This hands you that post, so you can watch where a unit is ACTUALLY being sent right now - which is what makes a stuck escort obvious instead of a unit standing still with no visible explanation. Empty when this follower is not in one of those loops.
nodes.desc_short: A live-map diagnostic.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The follower to inspect.

returns.name: anchor
returns.desc: The invisible waypoint object this follower is currently being walked toward, or nothing if they are not escorting or catching up right now.

nodes.title: Followers: Count
nodes.desc: How many followers you have right now. It reads the same live, self-cleaning roster, so units that have been killed are never counted.
nodes.desc_short: How many followers you have right now.

returns.name: n
returns.desc: The number of followers currently on your roster. 0 if you have none.

nodes.title: Followers: Dismiss
nodes.desc: Releases one follower. They stop following, get their ordinary background life back, lose their marker, and drop off your roster - any escort or catch-up loop running for them is stopped too. Dismissing somebody who was never recruited is a safe no-op. This same thing runs automatically when a follower is killed, which is why dead units never linger on your roster.
nodes.desc_short: Releases one follower.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The follower to release. The default picks the first person you recruited.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if they were on the roster and have now been released. False if they were not a follower in the first place.

nodes.title: Followers: Dismiss Everyone
nodes.desc: Releases every follower at once. Your whole roster goes back to being ordinary game characters and the roster is left empty. Good as a reset while you are testing, or at the end of a mission.
nodes.desc_short: Releases every follower at once.

nodes.title: Followers: Is One Of Mine
nodes.desc: Asks whether a particular character is on your roster right now. Useful as a gate before ordering somebody about, or to check a unit is still with you. Anyone who has died or been dismissed reads false.
nodes.desc_short: Asks whether a particular character is on your roster right now.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The character to check.

returns.name: bool
returns.desc: True if they are currently one of your followers.

nodes.title: Followers: Roster
nodes.desc: Hands you your current roster: everybody following you right now, oldest recruit first. It is self-cleaning - anyone who died or was dismissed is pruned as this is read, so what you get back is always live. Feed it straight into Create Team to turn your whole roster into a named team.
nodes.desc_short: Hands you your current roster: everybody following you right now, oldest recruit first.

returns.name: guids
returns.desc: A list of your follower handles, in recruit order. Empty if you have nobody.

nodes.title: Followers: Markers Showing?
nodes.desc: Tells you whether the follower markers are currently showing. They start ON, so this reads true until you turn them off.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether the follower markers are currently showing.

returns.name: bool
returns.desc: True if follower markers are on.

nodes.title: Followers: On Event
nodes.desc: Runs your own code whenever something happens to your followers - no checking every frame, it just fires. Events today: "onRecruit" (their handle) when somebody joins, "onDismiss" (their handle, and true if they were killed) when somebody leaves for any reason, and "onFollowerDown" (their handle) when one is killed. Squad's own events travel on this same bus, so the Squad On Event node is the identical mechanism. An event name nobody ever fires is harmless - your code simply never runs.
nodes.desc_short: Runs your own code whenever something happens to your followers - no checking every frame, it just fires.

params.name: eventName
params.desc: Which event to listen for: "onRecruit", "onDismiss" or "onFollowerDown".

params.name: fn
params.desc: Your code, run each time that event fires. It receives whatever that event sends - onRecruit and onFollowerDown send the character; onDismiss sends the character plus true/false for whether they were killed.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Call this to stop listening. Keep hold of it if you might ever want to unsubscribe.

nodes.title: Followers: Order Everyone
nodes.desc: Gives one command to your WHOLE roster at once - the real payoff of having followers. Pick from 11 behaviours: follow, move, face, hold, defend, attack, patrol, flee, enter, deploy, animate. They keep doing it until you say otherwise, with three exceptions that finish by themselves and hand control back: an attack ends when its target dies, and a move or a one-shot patrol ends once everyone arrives - after which they automatically go back to following you. Guard, hold and a looping patrol have no natural finish, so order 'follow' yourself when you want them back. Confirmed live: a follower who is DRIVING a vehicle is still commanded through their OWN character handle, never the vehicle's - order 'move' and the car drives there. While markers are on, the spot you just ordered them to also gets a white ring on the ground.
nodes.desc_short: Gives one command to your WHOLE roster at once - the real payoff of having followers.

params.name: behavior
params.desc: Which order to give: "follow", "move", "face", "hold", "defend", "attack", "patrol", "flee", "enter", "deploy" or "animate".

params.name: opts
params.desc: The details for that order: { at = {x,y,z} for move/face/defend, points = { {x,y,z}, ... } for patrol, loop = false to make a patrol run once instead of forever, target = <enemy handle> for attack or <vehicle handle> for enter, radius for defend, role = "driver" / "passenger" / "gunner" for enter, action = "Cower" for animate, speed, priority }. "follow", "hold" and "deploy" need nothing at all.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the order has been handed over. It is optimistic - the command actually fires about 1.5 seconds later, which is the settle time confirmed necessary for a follower to accept a new order.

nodes.title: Followers: Recruit
nodes.desc: Makes a character join you. From that moment they are one of YOUR units: they follow you around, ride along in vehicles, and answer to every order you give the roster. A follower is a real game character who keeps doing whatever you last told them until you tell them something else. Recruiting the same person twice is harmless. If they are already sitting in a vehicle that is handled properly - a driver keeps the wheel and escorts you instead of climbing out. If they die they drop off your roster on their own, no cleanup needed. Markers are ON by default, so a new follower gets their own coloured icon floating over their head.
nodes.desc_short: Makes a character join you.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The character to recruit. Wire in someone you spawned or picked out of the world - pointing this at yourself does nothing useful.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Optional settings: { target = <who they follow, defaults to you>, minDistance = 2, maxDistance = 30, moveDistance = 4, speed = <number>, escortMinDistance / escortMaxDistance = <how close they trail you while DRIVING a vehicle> }. Leave it empty for the confirmed-good defaults.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if they are now on your roster - also true if they already were. False if no character was given, or the game refused the join sequence.

nodes.title: Followers: Show Markers
nodes.desc: Turns the floating follower markers on or off. They are ON by default: every current AND future follower wears their own coloured icon above their head, each a distinctly different colour, and the place you last ordered them to gets a white ground ring that clears when a new order replaces it. Turning them on also marks everybody you already have; turning them off clears only the markers this system placed, never anyone else's.
nodes.desc_short: Turns the floating follower markers on or off.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to show markers, false to hide them. Setting it to what it already is does nothing.

nodes.title: Gfx: Call Movie Function
nodes.desc: Reach into a Flash widget from Lua and run one of the movie's own functions -- this is how text and numbers get into a custom UI, e.g. calling its SetTitle to change the header text on screen. The function name and its arguments must match what your .gfx movie actually defines; a wrong name quietly does nothing rather than crashing.
nodes.desc_short: Reach into a Flash widget from Lua and run one of the movie's own functions -- this is how text and numbers...

params.name: widget
params.desc: The widget handle from Gfx: Create Widget.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Name of the function inside the movie to run.

params.name: args
params.desc: The values to hand that movie function, in order. Leave it as {} for a movie function that takes none -- if you skip this entirely an empty list is used.

returns.desc: True if the call reached the movie.
returns.name: ok

nodes.title: Gfx: Drive Menu With Arrow Keys
nodes.desc: A HUD Flash widget receives no keyboard input of its own, so this watches the keys on its behalf: Up and Down tell the movie to move its highlight, Enter tells it to pick the highlighted row. The movie owns the selection and all the visuals -- Lua only ever says "up", "down" or "choose". Your movie must define Move and Choose functions or nothing happens. Keep the returned stop function and call it when you're done, or it keeps polling forever.
nodes.desc_short: A HUD Flash widget receives no keyboard input of its own, so this watches the keys on its behalf: Up and Down...

params.name: widget
params.desc: The widget handle from Gfx: Create Widget.

params.name: keys
params.desc: Which key codes count as up / down / enter. Defaults to the arrow keys and Enter.

returns.desc: Call it with no arguments to stop watching the keys.
returns.name: stop

nodes.title: Gfx: On Movie Event
nodes.desc: Listen for something the Flash movie sends back to Lua -- typically the player clicking or picking something inside your custom UI. Your handler simply receives the value the movie sent; this node hides the awkward native shape (a mandatory two-argument callback plus a mandatory trailing empty table) that is very easy to get subtly wrong by hand. The event name has to match exactly what your .gfx movie broadcasts.
nodes.desc_short: Listen for something the Flash movie sends back to Lua -- typically the player clicking or picking something...

params.name: widget
params.desc: The widget handle from Gfx: Create Widget.

params.name: name
params.desc: The event name your movie broadcasts, e.g. "choose" or "close".

params.name: cb
params.desc: What to run when the movie fires that event. It receives the value the movie sent.

returns.desc: True if the listener was registered.
returns.name: ok

nodes.title: Gfx: Show Or Hide Widget
nodes.desc: Turn a Flash widget on or off on screen. TRAP THIS FIXES: there is no IsVisible() on these widgets -- the real getter is GetVisible(), and calling the wrong name fails silently so a hand-written toggle just never flips. Worse, GetVisible() answers with 1 or 0 rather than true/false, and 0 is not falsy in Lua, so even the correct name breaks a naive toggle. Never read the engine back: this node records the state on the handle itself as widget.shown, so check that instead.
nodes.desc_short: Turn a Flash widget on or off on screen.

params.name: widget
params.desc: The widget handle from Gfx: Create Widget.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to show it, false to hide it.

nodes.title: Gfx: Repaint After Load
nodes.desc: Loading a .gfx movie is asynchronous, so text you push into a widget in the same instant you build it can silently vanish -- the movie had not finished loading yet, and you are left staring at an empty box wondering why. This re-runs your repaint step several more times over the next fraction of a second (8 times, one every 0.05s, by default) so at least one of them lands after the movie is genuinely ready. Put whatever re-sends your widget's text inside the repaint step.
nodes.desc_short: Loading a .gfx movie is asynchronous, so text you push into a widget in the same instant you build it can...

params.name: rt
params.desc: Your repaint step: a no-argument function that re-sends everything the widget needs to display. Swap the placeholder for your own Gfx: Call Movie Function calls.

params.name: ticks
params.desc: How many extra repaints to fire, one every 0.05 seconds. Defaults to 8.

nodes.title: Gfx: Create Widget
nodes.desc: Put a Flash (.gfx) movie on screen at a position and size, and hand back a handle the other Graphics nodes use. Nothing appears unless that .gfx file is actually deployed with your mod -- the stock game does not ship the Ess UI movies. Positions are on a fixed 640x480 virtual canvas that the game stretches to whatever resolution the player runs. TRAP THIS FIXES: the raw engine call wants CORNER coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2), NOT width and height. You pass plain x/y/width/height here and the corner maths is done for you -- getting it wrong renders the widget slightly too small instead of erroring, which is exactly why it goes unnoticed.
nodes.desc_short: Put a Flash (.gfx) movie on screen at a position and size, and hand back a handle the other Graphics nodes use.

params.name: file
params.desc: Name of the deployed .gfx movie file to show.

params.name: x
params.desc: Left edge, on the 640-wide virtual screen.

params.name: y
params.desc: Top edge, on the 480-tall virtual screen.

params.name: w
params.desc: Width in virtual pixels (this node converts it to a corner for you).

params.name: h
params.desc: Height in virtual pixels (this node converts it to a corner for you).

returns.desc: The widget handle ({ raw = <FlashWidget>, shown = false }) -- feed it into the other Graphics nodes. Nothing comes back if the movie could not be built.
returns.name: result

nodes.title: GPS: Clear Beacon
nodes.desc: Removes the beacon, both halves of it. It calls the engine's real clear, which wipes a waypoint the PLAYER dropped on the PDA map, and it deletes the drawn marker, which is all a script-placed beacon ever was. Safe to run when there is no beacon at all - it just quietly does nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Removes the beacon, both halves of it.

nodes.title: GPS: Distance To Beacon
nodes.desc: How far a player is from the beacon, in world units. It measures flat across the ground and ignores height deliberately: the beacon has no height of its own, so counting the player's altitude in would only add error to the answer. You get nothing back if there is no beacon, or that player cannot be found.
nodes.desc_short: How far a player is from the beacon, in world units.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player to measure from: 0 is you (the local player), 1 is your co-op partner. Leave it alone to measure from yourself.

returns.name: distance
returns.desc: Flat ground distance from that player to the beacon, in world units. Nothing at all when there is no beacon to measure to.

nodes.title: GPS: Beacon Position
nodes.desc: Tells you where the beacon currently is, or nothing when there is none. It is exact once the game has reported any beacon being set or cleared, because this listens for those from the moment it loads. Before it has heard one it falls back on the PDA's own stored numbers, which lag behind reality - measured still reporting a beacon at 3008 after the player had already cleared it. So a 'no beacon' answer is always trustworthy, but a position read before any beacon activity could be the ghost of one already gone.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you where the beacon currently is, or nothing when there is none.

returns.name: x
returns.desc: World X of the beacon, or nothing at all if there is no beacon.

returns.name: z
returns.desc: World Z of the beacon. There is no height to read - the beacon genuinely does not have one.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: GPS: On Beacon Cleared
nodes.desc: Runs your code every time the player clears their beacon. Your code is handed nothing at all, and that is not an oversight - the game's clear message genuinely carries no coordinates, measured empty. If you need to know where the beacon WAS, remember it yourself from the GPS: On Beacon Set node.
nodes.desc_short: Runs your code every time the player clears their beacon.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Your code, run each time the player clears their beacon. It takes no arguments.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Call this to stop listening. Keep hold of it if the reaction should ever be switched off again.

nodes.title: GPS: On Beacon Set
nodes.desc: Runs your code every time the PLAYER drops a beacon on the PDA map, and tells you where they put it. Note what it does not hear: a beacon placed by the GPS: Set Beacon node draws its marker directly and does NOT fire this. One trap already handled for you - the game's own message labels its second number wrongly, calling a Z coordinate a Y, and this node untangles that before your code ever sees it.
nodes.desc_short: Runs your code every time the PLAYER drops a beacon on the PDA map, and tells you where they put it.

params.name: fn
params.default: function(x, z) Ess.Easy.Toast("Beacon at " .. x .. ", " .. z) end
params.desc: Your code, run each time the player sets a beacon. It is handed two numbers: the beacon's world X and its world Z.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Call this to stop listening. Keep hold of it if the reaction should ever be switched off again.

nodes.title: GPS: Set Beacon
nodes.desc: Drops the GPS waypoint marker on the map at a spot you choose. Be clear about what you are getting: despite the name there is no routing here - no path, no route line, no directions - the whole GPS feature is this single marker. And because the engine gives scripts no way to set the player's real destination, a beacon placed by this node is COSMETIC. It draws correctly on the minimap, but the game does not treat it as where the player is headed. It does use the game's own reserved beacon name, so it replaces a beacon the player placed rather than stacking a second one beside it.
nodes.desc_short: Drops the GPS waypoint marker on the map at a spot you choose.

params.name: x
params.desc: World X of the spot to mark. Must be a number or the whole call is refused and logged.

params.name: z
params.desc: World Z of the spot to mark. There is no height to fill in, on purpose - the map is drawn from directly above, and the game's own beacon passes zero for height too.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Optional look of the marker: rgb = {r, g, b} tints it (default white, matching the game's), nSize sets the icon size (default the game's own 10.666667) and sTexture swaps the icon for another. Careful with a custom icon - it draws fine on your own screen but silently fails to appear for a co-op partner, because only the game's listed icons survive being sent over the network.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the marker was drawn. False means the coordinates were not numbers, or drawing it failed.

nodes.title: Find By Name
nodes.desc: Looks something up in the level by name and hands back the live handle that every other node wants. Names come from the level's own placed objects, and faction names like China, Allied or PMC work too. A typo just gives you nothing back in silence - that is one of the most common beginner dead ends, and turning debug on (a Lua line reading Ess.DEBUG = true) makes it say so.
nodes.desc_short: Looks something up in the level by name and hands back the live handle that every other node wants.

params.name: name
params.desc: The exact name to look up. Spelling and capitals matter.

returns.name: uGuid
returns.desc: The live handle for that name, or nothing at all if no such name exists in this level.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Add Meter
nodes.desc: Puts a faction meter on the HUD - one of the labelled gauges the game uses to show how a faction feels about you. Do not treat it as a panel you own: a meter slides away by itself about five seconds after its last update and CANNOT be pinned open (holding one there was built, measured and found not to work). Think of it as a flash of feedback, and use the Countdown Timer or Pursuit Gauge nodes when you need one held for a known length of time.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a faction meter on the HUD - one of the labelled gauges the game uses to show how a faction feels about...

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Which faction's meter, given as the game's short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ. Blank or non-text is refused and logged. Every node in this group takes the same code.

params.name: sTexture
params.desc: The small marker icon drawn beside the meter. The game passes each faction's own marker texture here; leave it blank if you have nothing particular in mind.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code was usable and the call went out. It does not confirm the meter is on screen.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Hide Meter
nodes.desc: Takes one faction meter off the screen. This is the genuine teardown: the engine's own 'remove meter' and 'remove all meters' functions are EMPTY - they are callable, they return quietly, and they do absolutely nothing - so this is the node that actually works.
nodes.desc_short: Takes one faction meter off the screen.

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Which meter to take down, as a short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code was usable and the call went out.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: In Territory
nodes.desc: Tells the HUD that the player is standing inside (or has just left) a faction's territory, which is how the game highlights the matching meter as you cross a border. Pair it with a trigger area to get the same border feedback the real map gives.
nodes.desc_short: Tells the HUD that the player is standing inside (or has just left) a faction's territory, which is how the...

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Whose territory it is, as a short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ.

params.name: bInside
params.desc: Tick when the player has entered the territory, untick when they leave. A blank socket counts as outside.

params.name: bInitialize
params.desc: Tick to snap the highlight on or off rather than easing it - what you want for the very first call, before the player has moved anywhere.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code was usable and the call went out.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Redefine Levels
nodes.desc: DESTRUCTIVE AND GLOBAL - read this before you use it. It does not label your meter: it rewrites the level bands and mood words shared by EVERY faction gauge in the game, including the game's own. A live test set custom names and Universal Petroleum's real meter then displayed one of them as its mood, so the player's faction standing is simply wrong from then on, for every faction, until the level reloads. There is no way to read the old values back, so always pair this with the Restore Levels node - and if you only wanted a countdown or a gauge, you do not need this at all.
