nodes.desc_short: DESTRUCTIVE AND GLOBAL - read this before you use it.

params.name: tThresholds
params.desc: The bottom value of each band, as a list of numbers going upwards. The FIRST ONE MUST BE EXACTLY 0 and each must be larger than the one before, or this node refuses and tells you which entry was wrong. That ascending check is Ess doing a job the engine forgot: the game's own check is broken and waves backwards or duplicate numbers through, which then leaves the gauge dividing by a negative or zero range.

params.name: tNames
params.desc: The mood word for each band, as a list of text exactly as long as the thresholds list. These replace the mood names on every faction meter in the game, not just yours. The stock values are not English words at all but localisation codes, which is precisely why substituting readable text is what breaks the real meters.

params.name: sPursuitName
params.desc: The label used for the pursuit state. The game's own value is recorded in Ess as Ess.Hud.Faction.STOCK_PURSUIT, and that is what the Restore Levels node puts back.

params.name: bShow
params.desc: Asks the game to display the result of the change straight away. The Ess source forwards it without documenting what it actually draws, so treat it as an experiment rather than something to rely on.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if your two lists passed the checks and the change was sent. A false always comes with a logged reason: mismatched lengths, an empty list, a first threshold that is not 0, a threshold that is not a number, a name that is not text, or thresholds that do not ascend.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Pursuit Gauge
nodes.desc: The red 'you are being hunted' gauge on a faction meter. It FILLS UP rather than draining down - confirmed on screen - so it reads as a threat closing in, which is the opposite of what the word 'duration' suggests. Give it zero or a negative time for an open-ended chase that ends on an event instead of a clock, which is what the game does for its own.
nodes.desc_short: The red 'you are being hunted' gauge on a faction meter.

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Which faction is doing the hunting, as a short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ.

params.name: nSeconds
params.desc: How long the gauge takes to FILL. Zero or a negative number - which is also what a blank socket gives you - means an open-ended pursuit instead. The meter is held on screen for this long plus about two seconds.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Your code, run once when the gauge finishes filling. An open-ended pursuit is documented as having no callback, so do not count on this firing when you pass zero or a negative time. Errors inside it are caught and logged.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code was usable and the pursuit was started. Remember that setting that meter's value above zero will stop it early.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Restore Levels
nodes.desc: Puts the game's own faction mood words and level bands back after Redefine Levels has replaced them - the cleanup half of that node, and the only way out short of reloading the level. It always works, because the stock values are written down inside Ess rather than read back from the game (there is nothing to read them from). One catch: meters do not repaint until something updates them, so a gauge still showing a custom mood keeps that text until its next value change, timer or pursuit - use the Set Value node on anything visible to force it through.
nodes.desc_short: Puts the game's own faction mood words and level bands back after Redefine Levels has replaced them - the...

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Set Value
nodes.desc: Moves a faction meter's needle on a 0 to 100 scale. Numbers outside that range are passed straight through rather than trimmed, deliberately, because the gauge's own band maths treats the two ends as open. One trap worth knowing: setting any value above zero CANCELS a pursuit running on that same meter, so do not nudge a value while the red gauge is up unless ending it is what you meant.
nodes.desc_short: Moves a faction meter's needle on a 0 to 100 scale.

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Which faction's meter to move, as a short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ.

params.name: nValue
params.desc: Where to put the needle, 0 to 100. This is a display number, not a relationship score - the game converts real faction standing onto this scale first, so a raw relations value wired straight in will not line up. Non-numbers are refused and logged.

params.name: bInitialize
params.desc: Tick to SNAP straight to the new value instead of sweeping to it. Use it for the first value you set, so the needle does not visibly climb up from zero.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code and the number were usable and the call went out.

nodes.title: HUD Faction: Countdown Timer
nodes.desc: The reason this whole group is worth knowing about: a real on-screen countdown with the game's own HUD chrome, which runs down and then calls your code. It is the ONLY countdown display the game exposes, so anything on a clock - defuse this, survive this, get there before the convoy - gets a native-looking presentation for almost nothing. Be aware it CANNOT BE STOPPED: there is no cancel, and starting another timer on the same faction is the only way to displace one that is running.
nodes.desc_short: The reason this whole group is worth knowing about: a real on-screen countdown with the game's own HUD...

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: Which faction's meter carries the countdown, as a short code: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ. It is just the slot the clock gets drawn in - it does not have to be a faction your mission is about.

params.name: nSeconds
params.desc: How long the countdown runs, in seconds. It must be above zero or the node refuses and logs why. The meter is held on screen for this long plus about five seconds, which is the supported way to keep a gauge up for a known period.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Your code, run the moment the clock hits zero. It fires exactly once and receives no information at all, so put whatever it needs to know in the code itself. An error inside it is caught and logged rather than breaking anything else.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the faction code and the time were usable and the timer was started. You get no handle back and there is no way to cancel it - see the description.

nodes.title: HUD: Banner
nodes.desc: Flash big plain text across the middle of the screen, like a mission announcement -- no icon, no gold header, just your words. It rides the game's own event-fanfare animation, so it plays once and clears itself; there is no hide call and nothing to clean up. Live-confirmed working.
nodes.desc_short: Flash big plain text across the middle of the screen, like a mission announcement -- no icon, no gold header,...

params.name: sMsg
params.desc: The text to flash across the screen.

nodes.title: HUD: Set Cash Readout
nodes.desc: Changes the CASH NUMBER SHOWN ON SCREEN and nothing else. This does not give the player any money - the save is untouched, and the next genuine cash change overwrites whatever you wrote. Use it for a faked readout in a scripted scene; if you actually want to pay the player, use the give-cash node instead.
nodes.desc_short: Changes the CASH NUMBER SHOWN ON SCREEN and nothing else.

params.name: nValue
params.desc: The cash figure to print on the HUD. Anything that is not a number is refused and logged. Worth repeating: this is the display only, the player is no richer.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Optional trimmings. sReason produces the game's own '+$500 (reason)' annotation beside the figure, and nIncrement drives the counting-up roll animation instead of the number just snapping to its new value.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the value was a number and the call went out. False means you passed something that is not a number, which is logged too.

nodes.title: HUD: Clear All Messages
nodes.desc: Wipes the message box completely - the line currently on screen and everything stacked up behind it. This is the only message node with no waiting-in-the-queue catch, so it is what to reach for when you need a visible notification gone right now.
nodes.desc_short: Wipes the message box completely - the line currently on screen and everything stacked up behind it.

nodes.title: HUD: Set Fuel Readout
nodes.desc: Changes the FUEL NUMBER SHOWN ON SCREEN and nothing else - the player's real fuel is untouched, and the next genuine change overwrites it. Display dressing only, exactly like the cash readout.
nodes.desc_short: Changes the FUEL NUMBER SHOWN ON SCREEN and nothing else - the player's real fuel is untouched, and the next...

params.name: nValue
params.desc: The fuel figure to print on the HUD. Anything that is not a number is refused and logged.

params.name: nMax
params.desc: An undocumented extra that none of the game's own scripts ever used: give it a number and the readout shows 'value/max' instead of a bare figure. Leave it blank for the normal display.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the value was a number and the call went out. False means you passed something that is not a number, which is logged too.

nodes.title: HUD: Hide Hint
nodes.desc: Take down a popup put up by HUD: Hint Popup. TRAP: the id must MATCH the one you showed it with -- a wrong or missing id leaves the hint sitting on screen, confirmed by live testing. That is deliberate, so two scripts showing messages at the same time can't wipe each other's.
nodes.desc_short: Take down a popup put up by HUD: Hint Popup.

params.name: sId
params.desc: The same id you passed to HUD: Hint Popup.

params.name: bBroadcast
params.desc: Leave false for your own screen only. True also hides it for other players in co-op (untested).

nodes.title: HUD: Hint Popup
nodes.desc: Show the game's own tutorial-style hint popup -- the little box with an icon and a notification sound that normally says things like "you're swimming" or "low on fuel" -- with any text you want. Confirmed reusable and live-tested with a screenshot. TRAP: it has no timer at all. It stays on screen forever until you take it down with HUD: Hide Hint using the SAME id, so always give it an id you can hide it by.
nodes.desc_short: Show the game's own tutorial-style hint popup -- the little box with an icon and a notification sound that...

params.name: sMsg
params.desc: The text to show in the popup.

params.name: sId
params.desc: A name for this hint. HUD: Hide Hint must be given the exact same one to clear it.

params.name: bBroadcast
params.desc: Leave false to show it only on your own screen. True opts into the game's co-op broadcast (its real network behaviour is untested).

nodes.title: HUD: Objective Tray Image
nodes.desc: Puts a picture in one of the objective tray's slots instead of text. It shares those slots with the Objective and Radio nodes, so an image on slot 1 replaces whatever objective text was there, and the next objective line replaces the image right back.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a picture in one of the objective tray's slots instead of text.

params.name: sTexture
params.desc: The name of a picture the game already has loaded. This node only checks that you typed something, so a name the game does not recognise is not reported back to you here. Blank is refused and logged.

params.name: nSlot
params.desc: Which tray line to draw on. 1 is the current-objective line (the default), 3 is the transient radio-chatter line - the same numbering the Objective and Radio nodes use, which is why they overwrite each other.

params.name: nW
params.desc: How wide to draw the picture. Leave it blank to let the game decide.

params.name: nH
params.desc: How tall to draw the picture. Leave it blank to let the game decide.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if a texture name was supplied and the call went out. False only means the name was blank or not text.

nodes.title: HUD: Location Banner
nodes.desc: The region-name card the game slides in when you cross into a named area, 'Playa del Este' style. It takes any text you like and changes nothing in the world, so it doubles nicely as a chapter or act card. Note it lingers for 10 seconds by default, much longer than the other text nodes.
nodes.desc_short: The region-name card the game slides in when you cross into a named area, 'Playa del Este' style.

params.name: sText
params.desc: The place name to print on the card. Any text works - this is pure decoration and does not move the player or touch the map. Blank text is refused and logged.

params.name: nDuration
params.desc: Seconds the card stays up. Defaults to 10.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the text was usable and the call went out. False only means you passed blank or non-text.

nodes.title: HUD: Show Message
nodes.desc: Adds a line to the message box - the notification stack the game itself uses for 'Checkpoint reached' and support denials - and hands back a ticket you can pass to the Update or Remove Message nodes. Watch the duration setting: a NEGATIVE number means PERMANENT. The game turns any negative time into a stay-forever flag, so the line sits there until you take it down by hand.
nodes.desc_short: Adds a line to the message box - the notification stack the game itself uses for 'Checkpoint reached' and...

params.name: sText
params.desc: The line of text to push onto the notification stack. Blank text is refused and logged.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Optional settings. nDuration is in seconds and defaults to 2 - a NEGATIVE value means permanent, and only a remove or a clear will take it down. nPriority runs 0 to 5 (default 5); anything outside that is quietly forced to 5, and 0 takes a separate high-priority path inside the widget. nFade is the fade time in seconds (0.25). bClearBuffer wipes everything else the moment this one appears. bAppends defaults to true. fCallback is your own code, run by the message widget, with an optional tCallbackData table handed along to it.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: A ticket identifying this message, to wire into the Update or Remove Message nodes. You get nothing back if the call failed - and the ticket is only useful while the line is still waiting in the queue.

nodes.title: HUD: Set Objective Line
nodes.desc: Write a line into the objective tray -- the mission-goal text that sits on the HUD and STAYS there until you change or clear it. Line 1 is the "current objective" line most missions use. Pass no text at all to wipe that line. Careful with line 3: that is the radio-chatter line, and HUD: Radio Line will overwrite anything you leave there.
nodes.desc_short: Write a line into the objective tray -- the mission-goal text that sits on the HUD and STAYS there until you...

params.name: sText
params.desc: The objective text. Leave it empty (nil) to clear that line instead.

params.name: nSlot
params.desc: Which tray line to write. 1 (the default) is the current objective; 3 is the radio line.

nodes.title: HUD: Radio Line
nodes.desc: Drop a one-off radio-chatter subtitle on the HUD (objective-tray line 3) -- the game's own mission-chatter line, and the natural home for cutscene dialogue and subtitles. It wipes ITSELF after the hold time, 5 seconds if you don't say otherwise, so never clear it by hand. Firing a newer line won't get cut short early by an older line's pending timer.
nodes.desc_short: Drop a one-off radio-chatter subtitle on the HUD (objective-tray line 3) -- the game's own mission-chatter...

params.name: sText
params.default: Bravo Six, we have eyes on the target.
params.desc: The subtitle line to show.

params.name: nHold
params.desc: Seconds it stays up before clearing itself. Defaults to 5.

nodes.title: HUD: Remove Queued Message
nodes.desc: Pulls a message back out of the message box before it ever appears. Same catch as Update Queued Message: it only searches the lines still waiting their turn, so this will NOT remove something already on screen. It also reports true just for having tried, not for having found anything - if you need a visible notification gone, use Clear All Messages.
nodes.desc_short: Pulls a message back out of the message box before it ever appears.

params.name: handle
params.desc: The ticket the Show Message node handed back for the line you want pulled. Only bites while that line is still queued.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the ticket looked valid and the removal was attempted - this is NOT proof a message was found and taken out. You only get false if you passed something that was not a ticket.

nodes.title: HUD: Show Or Hide Resources
nodes.desc: Shows or hides the cash and fuel readouts together. Showing is temporary - they slide back out after a few seconds - while hiding lasts indefinitely, until you show them again. Mind the switch: ONLY an explicit false hides them, so leaving that socket blank counts as 'show'.
nodes.desc_short: Shows or hides the cash and fuel readouts together.

params.name: bShow
params.desc: Tick to show the readouts, untick to hide them. Only an explicit false hides - a blank socket shows.

params.name: nDuration
params.desc: How many seconds they stay visible when showing. Defaults to 3, and is ignored when hiding, because hiding has no timer.

nodes.title: HUD: Suppress Resources
nodes.desc: The game's own 'hide these during a cutscene' switch for the cash and fuel counters, settable separately for each. It is a different mechanism from the show/hide node, so the two do not know about each other. Both sockets left blank counts as 'suppress nothing', which is how you turn it back off.
nodes.desc_short: The game's own 'hide these during a cutscene' switch for the cash and fuel counters, settable separately for...

params.name: bCash
params.desc: Tick to suppress the cash counter the way the game does during a cutscene. Blank counts as off - this node always writes both switches, it never leaves one as it found it.

params.name: bFuel
params.desc: Same for the fuel counter, set independently of cash.

nodes.title: HUD: Big Title Card
nodes.desc: The nicest-looking text the game can put on screen - a big stylised title that animates in and out, driven by the same Flash movie the game uses for its own cards. Good for 'MISSION COMPLETE' or an act title. You cannot move it left or right: the game overwrites any sideways position with a centred one, so the only placement you really control is how far down the screen it sits.
nodes.desc_short: The nicest-looking text the game can put on screen - a big stylised title that animates in and out, driven by...

params.name: sText
params.desc: The words to show. Blank text is refused and written to the log rather than drawn.

params.name: nDuration
params.desc: How many seconds it stays up, animation included. Defaults to 3.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Extra positioning, all optional. nY is a height on the game's own 640x480 grid - not screen pixels and not a percentage - so 0 is the top, 240 the middle, and it is pulled back to 450 at the lowest. sJustify is 'left', 'center' (the default) or 'right' and only shifts the text INSIDE a fixed centred box, because the sideways position is not yours to set. sVertAnchor ('center', 'bottom', or anything else for top) decides what nY is measuring to, and bExpand is handed straight through to the Flash animation.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the text was usable and the call went out. False only means you passed blank or non-text.

nodes.title: HUD: Tutorial Strip
nodes.desc: Writes the bare tutorial text strip - the plain instruction line, with none of the popup box, icon or notification sound the Hint node gets. It is STICKY: there is no duration on it at all, so whatever you write stays on screen through everything else that happens until something clears it. Leave the text empty to clear it, which is the game's own way of doing it.
nodes.desc_short: Writes the bare tutorial text strip - the plain instruction line, with none of the popup box, icon or...

params.name: sText
params.desc: The instruction line to display. Leave this EMPTY to clear the strip - that is the only way it ever goes away, since nothing times it out.

nodes.title: HUD: Update Queued Message
nodes.desc: Rewrites a message that has not appeared yet. Read this before relying on it: the game only searches messages still WAITING IN THE QUEUE, so a line already visible on screen simply cannot be found and you get a plain false with no other signal. Adding a message to an empty box displays it immediately, which means updating it straight afterwards always fails - to change a visible line, remove it and add a new one.
nodes.desc_short: Rewrites a message that has not appeared yet.

params.name: handle
params.desc: The ticket the Show Message node handed back for the line you want to edit. Wire it in - a ticket is a small table, not a number, and anything else is refused and logged.

params.name: sText
params.desc: The replacement wording for that queued line.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True only if the message was still in the queue and was changed. False means it had already gone on screen - which is the ordinary case here, not a malfunction.

nodes.title: Human: All Weapons
nodes.desc: Lists every weapon a character is carrying, so you can loop over them to refill ammo, count a loadout, or check what changed after giving them something.
nodes.desc_short: Lists every weapon a character is carrying, so you can loop over them to refill ammo, count a loadout, or...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person whose kit you want.

returns.name: tWeapons
returns.desc: A list of weapon handles. Always a real list, empty rather than nil when they carry nothing or cannot be read.

nodes.title: Human: Allow Corpse Cleanup
nodes.desc: Decides whether the game is allowed to quietly remove this body. The engine reclaims corpses on its own to save memory, so when you need one to keep lying there - a body the player has to find, or set dressing for a scripted scene - switch cleanup off or it can vanish halfway through.
nodes.desc_short: Decides whether the game is allowed to quietly remove this body.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The character, or the body, in question.

params.name: bAllow
params.desc: False keeps the body around for as long as you need it. True hands it back to the game to clear away whenever it likes, which is the normal behaviour.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. False means no character was passed in, or the game refused it.

nodes.title: Human: Weapon Ammo
nodes.desc: Reads how much SPARE ammo a weapon has left in reserve - not the rounds in the magazine it is currently firing.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how much SPARE ammo a weapon has left in reserve - not the rounds in the magazine it is currently firing.

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: A weapon handle, normally wired in from the Primary Weapon or All Weapons node - this takes the WEAPON, not the person holding it.

returns.name: n
returns.desc: Reserve rounds remaining. Comes back as 0 rather than nil if the weapon cannot be read, so a 0 does not always mean empty.

nodes.title: Human: Is Carrying Something
nodes.desc: Tells you whether a character has their hands full, hauling a body or a crate. Worth checking whenever an order mysteriously does nothing: carrying blocks climbing, swimming and most weapon use, so it is the usual explanation for a character appearing to ignore you.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether a character has their hands full, hauling a body or a crate.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to check. Ess.Player.character(0) is you; wire in any character instead.

returns.name: carrying
returns.desc: True when they are carrying something. Live-checked to be a real true/false with no nil surprises, and a character that cannot be read simply comes back false.

nodes.title: Human: Disable Weapons
nodes.desc: Stops a character being able to use their guns without taking them away - for a cutscene, a truce, or a non-combat stretch.
nodes.desc_short: Stops a character being able to use their guns without taking them away - for a cutscene, a truce, or a...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to disarm. Pair every use with Enable Weapons or they stay unable to shoot.

nodes.title: Human: Do Action
nodes.desc: Plays a named animation or behaviour on a character - how you make a civilian cower, stand back up, or react.
nodes.desc_short: Plays a named animation or behaviour on a character - how you make a civilian cower, stand back up, or react.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person who should perform it.

params.name: sActionName
params.desc: The action name, spelled the way the game spells it - known-good examples are "Cower", "Stand" and "Proximity". A blank name is quietly ignored rather than erroring, so a typo just means nothing visibly happens.

nodes.title: Human: Drop What They Are Carrying
nodes.desc: Makes a character put down the body or crate they are hauling. Unlike most nodes here the answer is genuinely useful - a false means there was nothing in their hands to begin with, so this doubles as a "were they carrying anything?" test as well as an action.
nodes.desc_short: Makes a character put down the body or crate they are hauling.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person whose hands you want emptied.

returns.name: dropped
returns.desc: True if something was actually put down. False means they were carrying nothing (confirmed on an NPC with empty hands), or no character was passed in.

nodes.title: Human: Drop Weapon
nodes.desc: Makes a character throw a weapon on the ground - disarming an enemy, or leaving a gun for the player to pick up.
nodes.desc_short: Makes a character throw a weapon on the ground - disarming an enemy, or leaving a gun for the player to pick...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person dropping it.

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: Which of their weapons to drop - usually wired in from the Primary Weapon or All Weapons node.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through.

nodes.title: Human: Enable Weapons
nodes.desc: Gives a character the use of their weapons back after they were disabled.
nodes.desc_short: Gives a character the use of their weapons back after they were disabled.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to re-arm.

nodes.title: Human: Equip Weapon
nodes.desc: Puts a weapon in a character's hands - either switching them to one they already carry, or genuinely adding a brand-new gun if you hand it a weapon looked up by template name.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a weapon in a character's hands - either switching them to one they already carry, or genuinely adding a...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to arm.

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: The weapon handle. Looking a weapon TEMPLATE up by name and passing that was live-confirmed to actually ADD a new weapon (their weapon count went 2 to 3), not just re-select one they already had.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through.

nodes.title: Human: Force Out Of Seat
nodes.desc: Yanks a character straight out of a vehicle seat - no door animation, no shuffling them onto a tidy patch of ground. Deliberately abrupt, and the right tool when the vehicle is about to be removed and a normal exit would strand them mid-animation. For the polite version that plays the get-out properly, use Vehicle: Exit.
nodes.desc_short: Yanks a character straight out of a vehicle seat - no door animation, no shuffling them onto a tidy patch of...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person sitting in the vehicle. This takes the PERSON, not the vehicle they are riding in.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. False means no character was passed in.

nodes.title: Human: Is Grappling
nodes.desc: Tells you whether a character is locked in a grapple right now - the close-in hold used by hijacks and takedowns. Useful as a guard before you order them to do anything else, because a grapple in progress swallows most other commands.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether a character is locked in a grapple right now - the close-in hold used by hijacks and...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to check.

returns.name: grappling
returns.desc: True while the hold is happening. Live-checked to be a real true/false, and a character that cannot be read comes back false.

nodes.title: Human: Knock Down
nodes.desc: Knocks a character off their feet for a moment - a stun, a shockwave reaction, or a scripted takedown.
nodes.desc_short: Knocks a character off their feet for a moment - a stun, a shockwave reaction, or a scripted takedown.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to floor.

params.name: nDuration
params.desc: How long they stay down, in seconds. Leave blank for the built-in 0.5.

nodes.title: Human: Weapon Max Ammo
nodes.desc: Reads the biggest reserve a weapon can hold, which is what you compare against to show an ammo bar or decide whether a resupply is worth it.
nodes.desc_short: Reads the biggest reserve a weapon can hold, which is what you compare against to show an ammo bar or decide...

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: The weapon handle to ask about.

returns.name: n
returns.desc: The maximum reserve rounds. Comes back as 0 rather than nil if it cannot be read.

nodes.title: Human: Pin Position
nodes.desc: Freezes where a character currently stands - both their spot and the way they are facing - so the game stops working it out for them again. The shipped scripts use this around vehicle exits and hand-placed characters, where the engine would otherwise shunt someone back to where it thinks they ought to be.
nodes.desc_short: Freezes where a character currently stands - both their spot and the way they are facing - so the game stops...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to pin exactly where they are.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. False means no character was passed in, or the game refused it.

nodes.title: Human: Ragdoll Early
nodes.desc: Makes a character go limp right now, BEFORE the thing that would knock them down actually happens. That order is the whole trick: the shipped hijack code goes limp first so the takedown flows smoothly, whereas ragdolling afterwards makes the body snap into place.
nodes.desc_short: Makes a character go limp right now, BEFORE the thing that would knock them down actually happens.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to go limp - usually the victim of a takedown or a hijack, a moment before it lands.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. False means no character was passed in.

nodes.title: Human: Primary Weapon
nodes.desc: Gets the handle of a character's main gun, which is what the ammo and refill nodes need as their input.
nodes.desc_short: Gets the handle of a character's main gun, which is what the ammo and refill nodes need as their input.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to look at.

returns.name: uWeapon
returns.desc: The weapon handle, or nil if they have no primary.

nodes.title: Human: Refill Weapon Ammo
nodes.desc: Fills a single weapon's spare ammo right back up to its maximum - the same one-liner the shipped game's own contract scripts use for a resupply.
nodes.desc_short: Fills a single weapon's spare ammo right back up to its maximum - the same one-liner the shipped game's own...

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: The weapon to top up. This fills the SPARE pool - follow it with Reload All if you also want the loaded magazine full right now.

nodes.title: Human: Reload All Weapons
nodes.desc: Tops up the loaded magazines on every weapon a character carries, from their spare ammo.
nodes.desc_short: Tops up the loaded magazines on every weapon a character carries, from their spare ammo.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to reload.

nodes.title: Human: Secondary Weapon
nodes.desc: Gets the handle of a character's sidearm or second weapon slot.
nodes.desc_short: Gets the handle of a character's sidearm or second weapon slot.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to look at.

returns.name: uWeapon
returns.desc: The weapon handle, or nil if that slot is empty.

nodes.title: Human: Set All Weapons
nodes.desc: Replaces a character's entire weapon loadout in one call, instead of equipping guns one at a time.
nodes.desc_short: Replaces a character's entire weapon loadout in one call, instead of equipping guns one at a time.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person whose loadout is being replaced.

params.name: tWeaponGuids
params.desc: The full list of weapon handles they should end up with. This REPLACES what they carry, so anything missing from the list is gone - the default here just hands back their current list, which changes nothing and is a safe starting point to edit.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through.

nodes.title: Human: Set Weapon Ammo
nodes.desc: Sets a weapon's spare ammo to an exact number - for a low-ammo challenge, a scripted resupply, or emptying a reserve.
nodes.desc_short: Sets a weapon's spare ammo to an exact number - for a low-ammo challenge, a scripted resupply, or emptying a...

params.name: uWeapon
params.desc: The weapon handle to change - the WEAPON, not the person.

params.name: n
params.desc: The new reserve count. This is the spare pool only; the magazine already loaded is untouched.

nodes.title: Human: Hold Fire
nodes.desc: Stops a character pulling the trigger while leaving the gun in their hands - for a standoff, a ceasefire, or a bodyguard who should look armed but never shoot. Different from Human: Disable Weapons, which takes the use of the weapon away entirely; this is a safety catch you flip on and off.
nodes.desc_short: Stops a character pulling the trigger while leaving the gun in their hands - for a standoff, a ceasefire, or...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to put on hold-fire. Ess.Player.character(0) is you; wire in any character instead.

params.name: bLocked
params.desc: True clamps the trigger shut, false lets them shoot again. Nothing clears this for you - a character left locked stays unable to fire for the rest of the session.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. False means no character was passed in, or the game refused it.

nodes.title: Human: Infinite Ammo
nodes.desc: Switches endless ammo on or off for a character, so their spare ammo never runs down.
nodes.desc_short: Switches endless ammo on or off for a character, so their spare ammo never runs down.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to give endless ammo to. Note this one takes the PERSON, unlike the other ammo nodes which take a weapon.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to switch it on, false to switch it back off. Live-tested behaviour: it keeps the RESERVE topped up forever, but the magazine being fired still empties and still needs a reload - and grenades still get thrown one at a time.

nodes.title: Human: Crowd Shoving
nodes.desc: Controls whether passers-by can bump this character out of the way. Switch it off for anyone you placed by hand for a scene - a crowd walking into them nudges them a little further each time, which is the usual reason a carefully-positioned NPC has drifted somewhere else by the time the player arrives.
nodes.desc_short: Controls whether passers-by can bump this character out of the way.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person who should stop being shoved around.

params.name: bEnabled
params.desc: False means nobody can push them and they stay exactly where you put them. True is the normal game behaviour, where they get jostled like anyone else.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. It confirms the request was accepted, not that you would see any difference.

nodes.title: Human: Set State
nodes.desc: Puts a character into one of the game's four body states - standing normally, sitting in a vehicle, subdued, or cowering - and plays an animation while they hold it. Upright plus Idle is the shipped way to snap someone back to normal after a cutscene or a cower, and this is the most-used control in the whole Human group. WARNING: it cannot tell you whether it worked. The game answers exactly the same nothing for a real state and for total gibberish (tested with "NotAReal"), so a misspelled state fails silently forever while this node still reports success.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a character into one of the game's four body states - standing normally, sitting in a vehicle, subdued,...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to change. Ess.Player.character(0) is you - but wire in a spawned throwaway character while you experiment, because a bad state can leave whoever you aim this at stuck.

params.name: sPosture
params.desc: The body state. Only these four are known to work: Upright, InVehicle, Subdued, Cower. Spelling and capitals matter and are NOT checked - a typo is accepted in silence and simply never happens, so copy one of the four exactly.

params.name: sAnim
params.desc: Which animation they play while in that state. "Idle" means just behave normally and is what nearly every shipped script passes; anything else is the name of a specific animation clip, e.g. "lifestylejobPlayerArmwrestlingWinningloop01". Leave it alone to get Idle.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True only means the call did not error - it does NOT mean the state was applied, because the game reports nothing either way. False means you left the person or the state name blank. Check the character in-game rather than trusting this.

nodes.title: Human: Break Out Of Grapple
nodes.desc: Ends the close-quarters hold a character is locked in - the melee grab used by hijacks and takedowns - and hands them back to normal movement. Check Human: Is Grappling first so you only break a hold that is really happening.
nodes.desc_short: Ends the close-quarters hold a character is locked in - the melee grab used by hijacks and takedowns - and...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to free from the hold.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through. It does NOT tell you whether they were grappling at all - use Human: Is Grappling for that.

nodes.title: Human: Is Swimming
nodes.desc: Tells you whether a character is out in deep water and genuinely swimming, rather than wading or standing on dry land. Good for drowning timers, river-crossing objectives, or refusing to drop a vehicle on someone mid-swim.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether a character is out in deep water and genuinely swimming, rather than wading or standing on...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to check.

returns.name: swimming
returns.desc: True while they are swimming. The game's own scripts check whether this ability exists before using it, which hints that some versions of the game lack it - it is confirmed present here, and even if it were missing this node would answer false rather than break your mod.

nodes.title: Impulse: Mass
nodes.desc: Reads how heavy something is - useful for telling a car from a tank, and it is the same number the push nodes scale their force by.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how heavy something is - useful for telling a car from a tank, and it is the same number the push nodes...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to weigh.

returns.name: n
returns.desc: The mass, or nil when it cannot be read. The push nodes fall back to 1000 in that case so a shove still does something.

nodes.title: Impulse: Push
nodes.desc: Shoves an object with a physics kick, handling the mass maths and axis order for you so a boost feels the same on a light bike as on a heavy tank.
nodes.desc_short: Shoves an object with a physics kick, handling the mass maths and axis order for you so a boost feels the...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to shove - a vehicle, a prop, a person.

params.name: opts
params.desc: How to shove it. Either the object-relative form - forward (the way it is facing), up, side, any of which you can leave out - or dir = {x,y,z} for a WORLD direction instead, with strength to scale it (default 1). scaleByMass defaults to true and is what makes the same numbers feel the same on any weight; set it false only if you want to supply the raw force yourself. A forward of about 8 is a strong speed boost.

nodes.title: Impulse: Spin
nodes.desc: Shoves an object OFF-CENTRE so it rolls or flips instead of just moving - this is how the barrel-roll style stunt is done.
nodes.desc_short: Shoves an object OFF-CENTRE so it rolls or flips instead of just moving - this is how the barrel-roll style...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to spin.

params.name: opts
params.desc: forward / up / side are the kick itself, relative to the object. at = {x,y,z} is where on the object the kick lands, measured from its centre - that offset is the lever arm, so further out means more spin. scaleByMass works as it does on Push.

nodes.title: Input: Key To Character
nodes.desc: Turns a key code into the character that key types on a US keyboard, which is what a text box needs to build up what the player is typing. Letters, digits, space and the usual punctuation are covered.
nodes.desc_short: Turns a key code into the character that key types on a US keyboard, which is what a text box needs to build...

params.name: vk
params.desc: The Windows key code, usually one taken straight from Input: Poll Keyboard's pressed list. 65 is A.

params.name: bShift
params.desc: Was Shift held - the difference between a and A, and between 1 and !. Read the live Shift state with Input: Key Held rather than guessing.

returns.name: char
returns.desc: The character, or nothing at all for keys that do not type anything (F5, arrows, Enter). Always allow for nothing before adding it to a buffer.

nodes.title: Input: Clear Pending Keys
nodes.desc:
Throws away every key press waiting in the buffer.

The classic use: a script that was LAUNCHED by a key press flushes the buffer as it starts, so its own trigger key - and anything the player mashed while it was loading - does not immediately fire an action on the very first tick. If your menu opens and instantly selects something, this is the fix.
nodes.desc_short: Throws away every key press waiting in the buffer.

nodes.title: Input: Key Held
nodes.desc:
Is this key down at this exact moment.

Safe to call from as many loops as you like: it only reads the keyboard's current state and never touches the press buffer, so it cannot steal presses from a menu or another script. This is the right node for 'hold Shift to boost'; for a one-shot press use Keys: On Key Press instead, or it will fire on every single tick the key is down.
nodes.desc_short: Is this key down at this exact moment.

params.name: vk
params.desc: The Windows key code. 16 is Shift, 17 is Ctrl, 32 is Space. Rather than memorise numbers, use the Keys: Key Code node to turn a name like 'F5' into one.

returns.name: held
returns.desc: True while the key is physically down. It stays true tick after tick, which is exactly what you want for a hold and exactly what you do not want for a press.

nodes.title: Input: Hijack Controller
nodes.desc:
NICHE, AND UNVERIFIED IN THIS BUILD - most mods never need it, and it is put together from documentation rather than a confirmed live test.

What it is for: while the world is paused there is no per-frame callback at all on this engine, so a PDA-style pause menu cannot animate or read a stick. Controller input is the one thing that still comes through, so this hides the PDA widget and takes over its controller callback to ride it.

Two catches. The PDA underneath still claims the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, so any keyboard interface you layer on top must use letter keys. And an idle stick sends NOTHING - not even a final zero - so if 'the stick just went back to centre' matters, you have to decide that yourself.

ALWAYS call the release it hands back, or the PDA stays hidden.
nodes.desc_short: NICHE, AND UNVERIFIED IN THIS BUILD - most mods never need it, and it is put together from documentation...

params.name: onInput
params.desc: Runs on every scrap of controller activity while hijacked. It does not run at all when the player is not touching the controller.

returns.name: release
returns.desc: Keep this and call it (or feed it to an Ess.stop node) to give the PDA back. Nothing else will do it for you. You still get one back even if the hijack failed - calling it is then harmless.

nodes.title: Input: Poll Keyboard
nodes.desc:
The one correct way to read the keyboard: call it ONCE per tick and read both halves off the result - which keys were just pressed, and which are held right now.

IT DRAINS THE PRESS BUFFER. The presses it hands you are gone for everyone else, so if a menu is also reading keys this will eat the presses that menu needed. When you only care whether a key is held, use Input: Key Held instead and leave the presses alone.

Never check keys one at a time in a loop - that is where every framerate bug in this project's menus came from.
nodes.desc_short: The one correct way to read the keyboard: call it ONCE per tick and read both halves off the result - which...

returns.name: input
returns.desc: Read it in a Lua field. input.pressed is the list of key codes that went down since your last poll (usually empty). input.down(vk) answers whether a key is held right now. Use pressed for one-shot actions and down for hold-to-do-something.

nodes.title: Input: Using Controller
nodes.desc:
Is the player on a controller right now. The everyday use is wording a hint correctly - 'Press A' against 'Press E' - without keeping a setting of your own.

Carefully written: not every build of the game exposes this, and the engine sometimes answers with a 1 or a 0 rather than a real yes/no, so this checks properly instead of being fooled by a 0 (which Lua would otherwise treat as true).
nodes.desc_short: Is the player on a controller right now.

returns.name: usingController
returns.desc: True if a controller is in use. Comes back false when the game cannot tell, so keyboard wording is the safe fallback.

nodes.title: Keys: Unbind All
nodes.desc: Drops every key binding at once. A good first action in a script that re-runs and rebinds its keys, so old bindings from a previous run cannot linger with stale actions attached.
nodes.desc_short: Drops every key binding at once.

nodes.title: Keys: Is Key Bound
nodes.desc: Is anything currently handling this key. Useful before binding, so you do not silently replace another part of your own mod's hotkey.
nodes.desc_short: Is anything currently handling this key.

params.name: key
params.desc: A key name like 'F5', or a raw key code number.

returns.name: bound
returns.desc: True if something is bound to that key right now. It only knows about keys bound through Keys nodes, not the game's own controls.

nodes.title: Keys: Unbind Key
nodes.desc: Stops handling one key. If it was the last binding, the shared poll loop notices on its next check and shuts itself down, so nothing keeps running in the background.
nodes.desc_short: Stops handling one key.

params.name: key
params.desc: The same key name or code you bound. Unbinding a key that was never bound is harmless.

nodes.title: Keys: On Key Press
nodes.desc:
Binds a key to an action, so ONE script can own a whole panel of hotkeys - the game's own loader only gives a script a single key.

Edge-triggered: holding the key down fires your action ONCE, not every tick. Binding the same key again REPLACES the old action rather than stacking a second one, so a script that re-runs cannot end up firing twice per press.

It quietly runs one shared poll loop behind the scenes, which shuts itself off when nothing is bound. Careful: it reads the same key presses that a focused Ess.UI menu reads, so do not run both on the same keys.
nodes.desc_short: Binds a key to an action, so ONE script can own a whole panel of hotkeys - the game's own loader only gives a...

params.name: key
params.desc: A key name - 'F5', 'space', 'a', '1', 'up', 'escape' - or a raw key code number. An unrecognised name is not an error: it is logged and simply not bound, so nothing at all happens when you press it.

params.name: fn
params.desc: What to run on each press. It is told whether Shift was held, so one key can do two things. Errors inside it are swallowed, so it cannot take the poll loop down with it.

nodes.title: Keys: Key Code
nodes.desc: Turns a friendly key name into the Windows key code number, for nodes that want the number rather than the name - Input: Key Held, for one. Numbers pass straight through unchanged, so it is safe to send anything through it.
nodes.desc_short: Turns a friendly key name into the Windows key code number, for nodes that want the number rather than the...

params.name: key
params.desc: The name: 'f1' to 'f12', 'a' to 'z', '0' to '9', 'space', 'enter', 'escape', 'tab', 'backspace', 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right', 'shift', 'ctrl', 'insert', 'delete', 'home', 'end', 'pageup', 'pagedown'. Capitals do not matter.

returns.name: vk
returns.desc: The key code, or nothing at all if the name is not in that list - which is the usual reason a binding silently does nothing.

nodes.title: Layers: Add
nodes.desc: Streams extra layer(s) into the level. The single most common reason this appears to do nothing: it is ignored outright unless a mode is already open, so put a Layers: Begin node before it. Layers already loaded are skipped, and STATIC layers - terrain and geometry - are refused and logged, because pulling those around mid-session is not survivable.
nodes.desc_short: Streams extra layer(s) into the level.

params.name: vLayers
params.desc: The layer name(s) to load, as a Lua list (a single name on its own also works). Names are the vz_state_* pieces of the level; 'vz_state_mer_oilrig_pristine' is one confirmed working example. Capitalisation does not matter.

params.name: fCb
params.desc: Optional. Runs once the loading finishes. It still runs immediately if every name you gave was skipped or refused.

nodes.title: Layers: Begin Mode
nodes.desc: Opens a layer mode. Layers are the chunks of the level the game streams in and out - an alternate, undamaged version of a building, an extra set of props - and this node writes down exactly which ones are loaded right now so the Layers: Finish node can put the world back precisely. Saving is switched off for the duration, so a crash mid-mode leaves the player's ordinary save on disk. Nothing else in this group does anything until a mode is open.
nodes.desc_short: Opens a layer mode. Layers are the chunks of the level the game streams in and out - an alternate, undamaged...

params.name: sId
params.desc: A name for this mode, used in the log to tell modes apart.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the mode opened. False if a mode is already open - only one layer mode runs at a time, and the second call is ignored rather than nesting.

nodes.title: Layers: Force Recomposite
nodes.desc: Optional extra step that forces the engine to visibly rebuild the scene after layers were added or removed. Many modes never need it - one that teleports or fast-travels the player recomposites for free - but a change made while the player stands still may not appear until you call this. Run it AFTER the add/remove work has finished. If the engine's state manager is unavailable it is skipped with a log line rather than failing.
nodes.desc_short: Optional extra step that forces the engine to visibly rebuild the scene after layers were added or removed.

params.name: fCb
params.desc: Optional. Runs once the rebuild is done.

nodes.title: Layers: Currently Loaded
nodes.desc: Lists the layers loaded in the level right now. Compare it against the baseline snapshot to see exactly what your mode has changed so far. Only streamed layers appear here; static terrain and geometry are not part of this list.
nodes.desc_short: Lists the layers loaded in the level right now.

returns.name: layers
returns.desc: A list of the layer names currently loaded.

nodes.title: Layers: Expect State
nodes.desc: Declares what the world should look like and makes it so, issuing only the missing loads and unloads. This is the fix for drift: instead of tracking what you changed, you state what must be present and what must be gone, and anything already correct is left alone. Ignored unless a mode is open.
nodes.desc_short: Declares what the world should look like and makes it so, issuing only the missing loads and unloads.

params.name: spec
params.desc: present = the layers that must be loaded, absent = the layers that must not be, cb = optional code to run once the world has converged. Static terrain layers named in either list are refused and logged.

nodes.title: Layers: Finish Mode
nodes.desc: Closes the layer mode and puts the world back. It compares what is loaded now against the picture taken at Begin and issues exactly the loads and unloads needed to match it, whatever happened in between - so it still restores correctly even if something else changed layers behind your back. Saving is allowed again afterwards (once no sandbox is still holding it). Static terrain layers are never unloaded on the way back.
nodes.desc_short: Closes the layer mode and puts the world back.

params.name: fCb
params.desc: Optional. Runs once the world is back to its pre-mode state. It still runs if there was no mode open or if the restore could not be issued, so it is a safe place to continue from.

nodes.title: Layers: Is Mode Open
nodes.desc: Checks whether a layer mode is currently open. Worth testing before Add or Remove, since those quietly do nothing when no mode is running.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether a layer mode is currently open.

returns.name: active
returns.desc: True while a mode is open.

nodes.title: Layers: Is Layer Loaded
nodes.desc: Checks whether one named layer is loaded in the level right now. This is the honest way to confirm a layer change actually took effect, rather than assuming it did because nothing errored.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether one named layer is loaded in the level right now.

params.name: name
params.desc: The layer name to check. Capitalisation does not matter.

returns.name: loaded
returns.desc: True if that layer is currently loaded.

nodes.title: Layers: Remove
nodes.desc: Unloads layer(s) from the level - how you make a set of props or an alternate version of a building disappear for your encounter. Like Add, it is ignored entirely unless a mode is open, and it flatly refuses to unload STATIC terrain and geometry layers.
nodes.desc_short: Unloads layer(s) from the level - how you make a set of props or an alternate version of a building disappear...

params.name: vLayers
params.desc: The layer name(s) to unload, as a Lua list (a single name on its own also works).

params.name: fCb
params.desc: Optional. Runs once the unloading finishes.

nodes.title: Layers: Baseline Snapshot
nodes.desc: Lists the layers that were loaded at the moment the mode opened - the state Finish will restore the world to. Useful for checking what you started from while a mode is running.
nodes.desc_short: Lists the layers that were loaded at the moment the mode opened - the state Finish will restore the world to.

returns.name: layers
returns.desc: A list of layer names. Empty when no mode is open, since there is no baseline to report.

nodes.title: Layers: Swap
nodes.desc: Unloads one set of layers and then loads another, properly sequenced - the everyday 'switch this area over to its arena version' move. Doing it with separate Remove and Add nodes lets the two overlap; this one waits for the removal to finish first. Ignored unless a mode is open.
nodes.desc_short: Unloads one set of layers and then loads another, properly sequenced - the everyday 'switch this area over to...

params.name: vRemove
params.desc: The layer name(s) to unload first.

params.name: vAdd
params.desc: The layer name(s) to load once the removal is done.

params.name: fCb
params.desc: Optional. Runs once both halves have finished.

nodes.title: Log Message
nodes.desc: Writes one line into the game's log file (scripts/lua_loader_printf.log), tagged [Ess] so it is easy to find among everything else. This is the simplest 'did my mod get this far' check there is: drop it between two nodes and see whether the line shows up.
nodes.desc_short: Writes one line into the game's log file (scripts/lua_loader_printf.log), tagged [Ess] so it is easy to find...

params.name: msg
params.desc: The line to write. Wire a value in if you want to print something the graph produced.

nodes.title: Loop: Is Running
nodes.desc: Is a loop with this name alive right now. The usual use is a toggle: if it is running, stop it; if not, start it - so one key turns your feature on and off.
nodes.desc_short: Is a loop with this name alive right now.

params.name: id
params.desc: The name used when the loop was started.

returns.name: running
returns.desc: True while that loop exists. It becomes false the moment a tick returns false or Loop: Stop is called.

nodes.title: Loop: List All
nodes.desc: Every loop running right now, sorted by name. The first thing to look at when the game starts slowing down: a name you do not recognise, or several near-identical names, is what a leaked loop looks like.
nodes.desc_short: Every loop running right now, sorted by name.

returns.name: loops
returns.desc: A list of entries, each with .id plus the same fields as Loop: Stats. Walk it in a Lua field to print or draw a monitor.

nodes.title: Loop: Start
nodes.desc: Run something over and over on the one shared heartbeat - a HUD that redraws, a watcher that keeps checking, anything that must not be a one-shot. It runs until the tick returns false or until Loop: Stop is called with the same name; nothing stops it on its own.
nodes.desc_short: Run something over and over on the one shared heartbeat - a HUD that redraws, a watcher that keeps checking,...

params.name: id
params.desc: A name for this loop. Starting again with the SAME name REPLACES the old one instead of adding a second, so a script that re-runs on every key press cannot leak a duplicate loop. Two different names means two loops both running.

params.name: interval
params.desc: Seconds between ticks. 0.2 is five times a second, fine for a HUD or a watcher. Smaller is smoother and more expensive; there is no per-frame option on this engine.

params.name: tickFn
params.desc: What to do each tick. It MUST return true to keep going - returning false, or forgetting to return anything at all, stops the loop after that one tick. That is the number one reason a loop 'only runs once'.

nodes.title: Loop: Stats
nodes.desc: A snapshot of how one loop is behaving. This is how you answer 'is my loop what is making the game chug' - compare how long a tick takes against the interval it runs at.
nodes.desc_short: A snapshot of how one loop is behaving.

params.name: id
params.desc: The name of the loop to inspect.

returns.name: stats
returns.desc: Nothing if that loop is not running. Otherwise a frozen copy (it will not change under you) with .interval, .ticks, .lastDuration, .avgDuration and .lastError. If lastDuration is anywhere near interval, that tick is doing too much work for how often it runs. lastError holds the message from the last tick that errored.

nodes.title: Loop: Stop
nodes.desc: Cancels a running loop by name. The tick already scheduled just notices the loop is gone and quietly does not book another one, so there is no error and nothing left dangling. Stopping a name that was never running is harmless.
nodes.desc_short: Cancels a running loop by name.

params.name: id
params.desc: The exact same name you gave Loop: Start. A typo here silently stops nothing and leaves the real loop running.

nodes.title: Mark: Clear
nodes.desc:
Removes a marker: every surface that handle actually used, plus the invisible anchor prop if it came from Mark: Zone. This is the ONLY thing that takes a marker off the screen.

Safe on a half-built handle and safe to call on one you already cleared - anything missing is simply skipped.
nodes.desc_short: Removes a marker: every surface that handle actually used, plus the invisible anchor prop if it came from...

params.name: handle
params.desc: The handle from Mark: Object or Mark: Zone, wired in. An empty one does nothing at all - which is what 'my marker will not go away' usually turns out to be.

nodes.title: Mark: Object
nodes.desc:
Puts a marker on a thing: a round-radar blip, a PDA map blip and a floating in-world icon, each one an independent switch, plus an optional ring on the ground around it.

Keep the handle it gives back. Markers do NOT clean themselves up - not even when the thing they are stuck to dies - so a marker you drop the handle for is stuck on screen for the rest of the session.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a marker on a thing: a round-radar blip, a PDA map blip and a floating in-world icon, each one an...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to mark, wired in from whatever spawned or found it.

params.name: opts
params.default: { radar = true, pda = true, world = true }
params.desc: Which surfaces to use. radar, pda and world (the floating icon) are all ON unless you set one to false. Extras: disc = true adds a ring on the ground (radius = 15 by default, discAlpha sets its fill), kind picks the icon set out of 'destroy', 'verify', 'defend', 'action' or 'destination' (default 'action'), rgb = { 255, 0, 0 } colours it, size and dist tune the floating icon's size and how far off it stays visible.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: Keep this. It is the only way to remove the marker later - feed it to Mark: Clear, an Ess.stop node, or a tracker.

nodes.title: Mark: Zone
nodes.desc:
Marks a PLACE rather than a thing: a ring drawn on the ground plus radar and PDA blips, for a delivery point or an area objective.

There is nothing at a bare position to hang a blip on, so this quietly spawns an invisible anchor prop and marks that. The zone OWNS that prop, so Mark: Clear removes it for you - which is exactly why you must not throw the handle away.
nodes.desc_short: Marks a PLACE rather than a thing: a ring drawn on the ground plus radar and PDA blips, for a delivery point...

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west centre of the zone.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height of the centre. Put it near ground level or the ring hangs in the air.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south centre of the zone.

params.name: radius
params.desc: How wide the ground ring is drawn, in world units.

params.name: opts
params.default: { world = true, radar = true, pda = true }
params.desc: Which surfaces to use. world (the ground ring), radar and pda are all ON unless you set one to false. Extras: icon = true ALSO drops a floating icon on the anchor (off by default), kind picks the icon set (default 'destination'), rgb = { 0, 255, 0 } colours it, discAlpha sets the ring's fill, size and dist tune the floating icon.

returns.name: handle
returns.desc: Keep this for Mark: Clear. It comes back empty if the anchor prop could not be spawned, so a zone that never appears means the spawn failed, not the marking.

nodes.title: Math: Angle Toward Point
nodes.desc: Which way to point something so it faces a spot: gives the yaw, in degrees, that looks from one place toward another. Feed it into Ess.Object.setYaw to turn a thing to face a target. It uses the engine's own yaw convention (forward is +sin, +cos) and is the exact opposite of Math: Point Ahead. If the two points are identical you get 0.
nodes.desc_short: Which way to point something so it faces a spot: gives the yaw, in degrees, that looks from one place toward...

params.name: fromX
params.desc: X of the thing doing the facing.

params.name: fromZ
params.desc: Z of the thing doing the facing.

params.name: toX
params.desc: X of the spot to face.

params.name: toZ
params.desc: Z of the spot to face.

returns.name: yawDegrees
returns.desc: The facing angle in degrees, in the engine's yaw convention.

nodes.title: Math: Approach
nodes.desc: Moves a number toward a target by a limited step and never overshoots it. Run it every frame with maxStep = speed * deltaTime and you get smooth easing that behaves the same whatever the frame rate.
nodes.desc_short: Moves a number toward a target by a limited step and never overshoots it.

params.name: cur
params.desc: Where the value is right now.

params.name: target
params.desc: Where you want it to end up.

params.name: maxStep
params.desc: The biggest jump allowed this call.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The new value, one step closer to the target (or exactly the target if it was within reach).

nodes.title: Math: Clamp
nodes.desc: Keeps a number inside a low/high range. Anything below lo comes back as lo, anything above hi comes back as hi. Use it so health, ammo or a speed can never go out of bounds.
nodes.desc_short: Keeps a number inside a low/high range.

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to keep in range.

params.name: lo
params.desc: Lowest allowed value.

params.name: hi
params.desc: Highest allowed value.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The number, pulled back inside lo..hi.

nodes.title: Math: Clamp 0 to 1
nodes.desc: Squashes a number into the 0..1 range. The usual tidy-up before feeding a blend or ease amount into Math: Blend Numbers.
nodes.desc_short: Squashes a number into the 0..1 range.

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to squash into 0..1.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The number, never below 0 and never above 1.

nodes.title: Math: Distance 2D
nodes.desc: How far apart two points are on the ground, ignoring height. This is the one you normally want, so something on a rooftop right above you doesn't read as far away just because it is high up.
nodes.desc_short: How far apart two points are on the ground, ignoring height.

params.name: x1
params.desc: First point's X.

params.name: z1
params.desc: First point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: Second point's X.

params.name: z2
params.desc: Second point's Z.

returns.name: distance
returns.desc: Ground distance in world units.

nodes.title: Math: Distance 2D (Squared)
nodes.desc: Ground distance with the expensive square root skipped, so it is cheaper to run a lot. Only use it to COMPARE distances ("which one is closer") - the number itself is the distance multiplied by itself, not the distance.
nodes.desc_short: Ground distance with the expensive square root skipped, so it is cheaper to run a lot.

params.name: x1
params.desc: First point's X.

params.name: z1
params.desc: First point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: Second point's X.

params.name: z2
params.desc: Second point's Z.

returns.name: distanceSq
returns.desc: Ground distance squared. Comparable, but not a real distance.

nodes.title: Math: Distance 3D
nodes.desc: True straight-line distance between two points, height included. Use Distance 2D instead when a difference in height shouldn't count.
nodes.desc_short: True straight-line distance between two points, height included.

params.name: x1
params.desc: First point's X.

params.name: y1
params.desc: First point's Y (height).

params.name: z1
params.desc: First point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: Second point's X.

params.name: y2
params.desc: Second point's Y (height).

params.name: z2
params.desc: Second point's Z.

returns.name: distance
returns.desc: Straight-line distance in world units.

nodes.title: Math: Distance 3D (Squared)
nodes.desc: Straight-line distance including height, with the square root skipped for speed. Good for sorting or comparing only - the number is not a real distance.
nodes.desc_short: Straight-line distance including height, with the square root skipped for speed.

params.name: x1
params.desc: First point's X.

params.name: y1
params.desc: First point's Y (height).

params.name: z1
params.desc: First point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: Second point's X.

params.name: y2
params.desc: Second point's Y (height).

params.name: z2
params.desc: Second point's Z.

returns.name: distanceSq
returns.desc: 3D distance squared. Comparable, but not a real distance.

nodes.title: Math: Blend Numbers
nodes.desc: Blends smoothly between two numbers. t = 0 gives a, t = 1 gives b, 0.5 gives the halfway point. The workhorse behind fades, growing bars and easing a value over time.
nodes.desc_short: Blends smoothly between two numbers.

params.name: a
params.desc: The value at t = 0 (the start).

params.name: b
params.desc: The value at t = 1 (the end).

params.name: t
params.desc: How far along, usually 0 to 1.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The blended number.

nodes.title: Math: Blend Angles
nodes.desc: Blends between two facing angles the SHORT way round, so going from 350 to 10 eases forward 20 degrees through zero instead of spinning 340 the wrong way. This is the right blend for a turning yaw - plain number blending gets it wrong.
nodes.desc_short: Blends between two facing angles the SHORT way round, so going from 350 to 10 eases forward 20 degrees...

params.name: a
params.desc: Starting angle in degrees.

params.name: b
params.desc: Target angle in degrees.

params.name: t
params.desc: How far through the turn, 0 to 1.

returns.name: degrees
returns.desc: The in-between angle, between -180 and 180.

nodes.title: Math: Normalize Angle
nodes.desc: Folds any angle into the -180 to 180 range, so the gap between two facings reads as the SHORTEST turn: 350 and 10 come out 20 apart, not 340. Use it before asking "am I roughly facing this?" or easing a turn.
nodes.desc_short: Folds any angle into the -180 to 180 range, so the gap between two facings reads as the SHORTEST turn: 350...

params.name: deg
params.desc: Any angle in degrees.

returns.name: degrees
returns.desc: The same angle, expressed between -180 and 180.

nodes.title: Math: Point Ahead
nodes.desc: Finds the spot a set distance directly in front of something, given where it is and which way it faces. This is the "put it 10 units ahead of me" maths behind spawnAhead, so you never re-derive the sin/cos. Two things to know: it uses the engine's yaw convention (forward is +sin, +cos), and a character's yaw is its BODY facing, not where the player is looking - so this lands in front of the chest, not the crosshair. Height (Y) is left to you.
nodes.desc_short: Finds the spot a set distance directly in front of something, given where it is and which way it faces.

params.name: x
params.desc: Starting X.

params.name: z
params.desc: Starting Z.

params.name: yawDeg
params.desc: The facing angle in degrees. 0 means facing +Z.

params.name: dist
params.desc: How far ahead, in world units.

returns.name: x
returns.desc: X of the spot ahead.

returns.name: z
returns.desc: Z of the spot ahead.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Math: Remap Range
nodes.desc: Rescales a number from one range onto another - turn 0..maxHealth into 0..1 for a bar, or a distance into a fade amount. If the input range has no width you get outLo back instead of a divide-by-zero error.
nodes.desc_short: Rescales a number from one range onto another - turn 0..maxHealth into 0..1 for a bar, or a distance into a...

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to rescale.

params.name: inLo
params.desc: Bottom of the range it's currently in.

params.name: inHi
params.desc: Top of the range it's currently in.

params.name: outLo
params.desc: Bottom of the range you want.

params.name: outHi
params.desc: Top of the range you want.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The rescaled number.

nodes.title: Math: Rotate Offset To World
nodes.desc: Turns a "5 to my right and 10 ahead of me" offset into real world coordinates for something facing yawDeg. Use it for squad formations, grids and side-by-side placement instead of writing your own rotation maths - a hand-rolled one is exactly where this project got the signs wrong before. Point Ahead is just this with no sideways part.
nodes.desc_short: Turns a "5 to my right and 10 ahead of me" offset into real world coordinates for something facing yawDeg.

params.name: x
params.desc: X of the thing you're offsetting from.

params.name: z
params.desc: Z of the thing you're offsetting from.

params.name: yawDeg
params.desc: Which way that thing faces, in degrees.

params.name: localX
params.desc: Sideways offset - positive is to its right.

params.name: localZ
params.desc: Forward offset - positive is ahead of it.

returns.name: worldX
returns.desc: World X of the offset spot.

returns.name: worldZ
returns.desc: World Z of the offset spot.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Math: Round
nodes.desc: Rounds a number to the nearest whole number, or to however many decimal places you ask for. Use it so a HUD shows 13 or 12.99 instead of 12.9999997.
nodes.desc_short: Rounds a number to the nearest whole number, or to however many decimal places you ask for.

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to round.

params.name: decimals
params.desc: How many decimal places to keep. Leave at 0 for the nearest whole number.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The rounded number.

nodes.title: Math: Sign
nodes.desc: Tells you which way a number points: 1 if it is positive, -1 if negative, 0 if exactly zero. Handy for turning a difference into a simple left/right or up/down decision.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you which way a number points: 1 if it is positive, -1 if negative, 0 if exactly zero.

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to test.

nodes.title: Math: Smooth Ease
nodes.desc: Turns straight-line 0..1 progress into eased 0..1 progress that starts and ends gently. Feed the result into Math: Blend Numbers for smooth ease-in-out movement instead of something that snaps into motion. t is clamped for you.
nodes.desc_short: Turns straight-line 0..1 progress into eased 0..1 progress that starts and ends gently.

params.name: t
params.desc: Raw progress, 0 to 1.

returns.name: eased
returns.desc: Eased progress, 0 to 1.

nodes.title: Math: Within Range 2D
nodes.desc: Is the second point within r units of the first, measured on the ground? This is the proximity check every "has the player reached the zone yet" poll needs, already written correctly so you can't fumble the maths.
nodes.desc_short: Is the second point within r units of the first, measured on the ground?

params.name: x1
params.desc: Centre point's X.

params.name: z1
params.desc: Centre point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: The point you're testing, X.

params.name: z2
params.desc: The point you're testing, Z.

params.name: r
params.desc: The radius, in world units.

returns.name: inRange
returns.desc: True if the second point is inside the circle.

nodes.title: Math: Within Range 3D
nodes.desc: Is the second point within r units of the first, height included? The sphere version of Within Range 2D - use this when something being far above or below should push it out of range.
nodes.desc_short: Is the second point within r units of the first, height included?

params.name: x1
params.desc: Centre point's X.

params.name: y1
params.desc: Centre point's Y (height).

params.name: z1
params.desc: Centre point's Z.

params.name: x2
params.desc: The point you're testing, X.

params.name: y2
params.desc: The point you're testing, Y (height).

params.name: z2
params.desc: The point you're testing, Z.

params.name: r
params.desc: The radius, in world units.

returns.name: inRange
returns.desc: True if the second point is inside the sphere.

nodes.title: Math: Wrap Into Range
nodes.desc: Wraps a number back around whenever it runs off the end of a range - keeps a menu index, an angle or a scrolling cursor in bounds. The top end is excluded, so wrapping into 0..360 gives 0 up to 359.99, and 370 comes back as 10.
nodes.desc_short: Wraps a number back around whenever it runs off the end of a range - keeps a menu index, an angle or a...

params.name: v
params.desc: The number to wrap.

params.name: lo
params.desc: Bottom of the range (included).

params.name: hi
params.desc: Top of the range (excluded).

returns.name: value
returns.desc: The number wrapped into lo..hi.

nodes.title: Minimap: Auto-Zoom Curve
nodes.desc: Retunes the game's speed-based zoom rather than fighting it. You give it the two speeds to slide between and how much ground the map should show at each, and it keeps sliding smoothly as you drive - so the minimap still breathes with your speed, just on your numbers instead of the game's. Handing it no options puts the stock figures back, which makes this the reset as well. Like the lock, it is lost when a level loads and needs applying again.
nodes.desc_short: Retunes the game's speed-based zoom rather than fighting it.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: The four numbers of the curve, each one optional and each falling back to the game's own: nMinSpeed and nMaxSpeed are the speeds the zoom slides between (stock 10 and 50), and nMinRange and nMaxRange are how far the map sees at those two speeds (stock 150 and 400). nMaxSpeed has to be bigger than nMinSpeed - the maths divides by the gap between them - so an equal or backwards pair is refused outright.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the retuned curve is running. False means either the two speeds were the wrong way round, or there was no minimap update to wrap.

nodes.title: Minimap: Border Texture
nodes.desc: Swaps the frame drawn around the minimap for a different texture. Read the warning before you use it: the widget only does this if your build of the game has the underlying engine feature, and on a build without it the call is a SILENT do-nothing. So success here does not prove the frame changed - judge this one by looking at the screen, never by the result. The game's own scripts never make this call, so there is no known-good texture name to copy either.
nodes.desc_short: Swaps the frame drawn around the minimap for a different texture.

params.name: sTexture
params.desc: Name of the texture to draw as the frame. It must be actual text and must not be blank - an empty or non-text value is refused outright and noted in the log. You will need a name from the game's own art files; nothing in the game's scripts uses this call, so there is no worked example to copy from.

params.name: nWidth
params.desc: How wide the frame should be. This node lets you leave it out, but the engine call underneath expects the texture and both sizes together, so fill it in.

params.name: nHeight
params.desc: How tall the frame should be. Same story as the width - leaving it out is allowed here, but the engine call expects it.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True only means the texture name was valid and a minimap was found. On a build lacking the underlying feature you still get true and nothing changes at all.

nodes.title: Minimap: Lock Range
nodes.desc: Sets the minimap's zoom and MAKES IT STICK. It works by taking over the update that would otherwise recalculate the zoom from your speed, and re-forcing your number afterwards, so the view holds through turning and driving instead of snapping back. This is the node you want for a lasting zoom; the plain range node is the one that looks like it failed. One thing to remember: the minimap is rebuilt when a level loads and takes the lock with it, so apply it again after a load.
nodes.desc_short: Sets the minimap's zoom and MAKES IT STICK.

params.name: n
