params.desc: How far the minimap can see, in world units, held there for good. The game's own range only ever runs 150 (standing still) to 400 (fast), so anything above 400 is a wider view than the game will ever give you on its own. Must be a number.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the lock is in place. False means there was no minimap, or it had no update for this to wrap - and in that case the lock is thrown away cleanly rather than left half-applied.

nodes.title: Minimap: Set Range (One-Shot)
nodes.desc: Zooms the minimap in or out by setting how much ground it shows. Here is the catch that trips everyone up: the game recalculates this from how fast you are moving on every single minimap update, so your value applies instantly and is then wiped. Measured in game - a range of 1500 while standing still visibly zoomed the map out and held, then snapped straight back the moment the map turned. Use Minimap: Lock Range for anything meant to last; this one is for a momentary effect.
nodes.desc_short: Zooms the minimap in or out by setting how much ground it shows.

params.name: n
params.desc: How far the minimap can see, in world units - bigger numbers show more ground. For scale, the game's own value runs 150 when you are standing still up to 400 at speed. Must be a number; anything else is refused and noted in the log.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the number was valid and a minimap was there to receive it. It is NOT a promise the zoom stuck - the next map update almost certainly overwrote it.

nodes.title: Minimap: Rotation
nodes.desc: Spins the minimap to an angle. ONE-SHOT, and deliberately left that way: the game drives the map's rotation from the camera heading on every update, so your angle is overwritten almost at once - and even the lock node holds only the RANGE, never the rotation. Owning the rotation too would break the map's north-up behaviour, so it was left alone. Fine for a momentary flourish, not for a lasting change.
nodes.desc_short: Spins the minimap to an angle.

params.name: n
params.desc: The angle to turn the map to. The source does not record whether the widget wants degrees or radians, so try a value and watch what happens. Must be a number; anything else is refused and noted in the log.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the number was valid and a minimap was there to receive it, not that the spin lasted - it will not.

nodes.title: Minimap: Show Or Hide
nodes.desc: Hides the whole minimap, or brings it back. This is not a hack - it is exactly what the game's own clean-HUD demo mode does to the map, so it is a supported state rather than something forced. Good for a cutscene or a stripped-down screen.
nodes.desc_short: Hides the whole minimap, or brings it back.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to show the minimap, false to hide it. Only an explicit false hides it, so leaving this alone brings the map back.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if there was a minimap to show or hide. False only means the widget was missing - usually because the HUD has not been built yet.

nodes.title: Minimap: Unlock Range
nodes.desc: Undoes Minimap: Lock Range. It puts the game's original minimap update back exactly as it was, so the speed-based zoom takes over again. Safe to run when nothing was ever locked - it simply does nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Undoes Minimap: Lock Range.

nodes.title: Minimap: Widget
nodes.desc: Hands you the minimap's own widget object - the thing every other Minimap node drives - so you can reach features this framework does not already wrap. It is looked up fresh on every call and never remembered, because the game rebuilds the widget whenever a level loads and a saved copy would quietly stop working. You get nothing back if the HUD has not been built yet.
nodes.desc_short: Hands you the minimap's own widget object - the thing every other Minimap node drives - so you can reach...

returns.name: widget
returns.desc: The minimap widget itself, or nothing at all when the HUD is not up. Always check you actually got one before using it.

nodes.title: Name Of
nodes.desc: The other direction: give it a live handle and it gives back that object's name as text - useful for printing what you just picked up, spawned or aimed at. Safe on anything: the raw engine call behind it is confirmed to throw outright on at least one real object, and this one absorbs that instead of crashing your mod.
nodes.desc_short: The other direction: give it a live handle and it gives back that object's name as text - useful for printing...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing whose name you want. Wire one in, or leave it as the player.

returns.name: name
returns.desc: The object's name text, or nothing at all if it could not be read.

nodes.title: Co-op: Get Shared Value
nodes.desc: Reads back a value that either machine put into the shared store under that name. In single-player it simply reads back whatever you set locally, so the same graph works solo and in co-op.
nodes.desc_short: Reads back a value that either machine put into the shared store under that name.

params.name: key
params.desc: The same name that was used to set it.

returns.name: value
returns.desc: Whatever was stored under that name, or nothing at all if nobody has set it yet.

nodes.title: Co-op: Am I In Charge?
nodes.desc: True when playing alone, and true on the host in co-op. This is the check to put in front of anything that must happen exactly once no matter how many players there are: spawning a wave, paying out money, deciding the boss is dead. Almost always the one you want, because Am I The Host is false in single-player and would skip your logic entirely.
nodes.desc_short: True when playing alone, and true on the host in co-op.

returns.name: isAuthority
returns.desc: True if this machine should be the one running the logic.

nodes.title: Co-op: In A Co-op Game?
nodes.desc: True when you are actually in a live two-player session, false when you are playing alone. Check it before doing anything co-op-specific.
nodes.desc_short: True when you are actually in a live two-player session, false when you are playing alone.

returns.name: isCoop
returns.desc: True only in a live co-op session.

nodes.title: Co-op: Am I The Host?
nodes.desc: True only on the machine hosting a live co-op session. It is FALSE in single-player, which catches people out - if what you really mean is 'should this machine be the one running the logic', use Am I In Charge instead.
nodes.desc_short: True only on the machine hosting a live co-op session.

returns.name: isHost
returns.desc: True only on the co-op host. False when playing alone.

nodes.title: Co-op: My Player Id
nodes.desc: Which player this machine is, 0 or 1. Use it to tell the two sides apart - a different colour, a different spawn point, a different half of the job.
nodes.desc_short: Which player this machine is, 0 or 1.

returns.name: id
returns.desc: This machine's player id, 0 or 1.

nodes.title: Co-op: On Message
nodes.desc: Listens on a named channel and runs your code whenever the other player sends on it. Pair it with a Co-op: Send Message node using exactly the same channel name. One name has one listener - registering the same name again replaces the previous one rather than adding a second.
nodes.desc_short: Listens on a named channel and runs your code whenever the other player sends on it.

params.name: name
params.desc: The channel to listen on. Must match the sender's name character for character.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs when a message arrives. It is handed the sender's player id (0 or 1) and the value that was sent.

nodes.title: Co-op: Send Message
nodes.desc: Fires a one-off message to the other player on a named channel - 'the boss spawned', 'I picked up the case'. Use this for events; use Set Shared Value for state that should stay true. The other machine needs a Co-op: On Message node listening on the exact same channel name. Same honest limit as the rest of the co-op layer: two-machine delivery has not been re-verified since the port.
nodes.desc_short: Fires a one-off message to the other player on a named channel - 'the boss spawned', 'I picked up the case'.

params.name: name
params.desc: The channel name. It must match the listener's name character for character.

params.name: value
params.desc: The payload: text in quotes, a number, true/false, or a small table. Keep it small.

params.name: reliable
params.desc: Leave this on so the message is guaranteed to arrive. Turn it off only for chatter you can afford to lose.

nodes.title: Co-op: Set Shared Value
nodes.desc: Stores a value under a name and pushes it to the other player, so both machines agree on it - a score, a wave number, whether the boss is down. The most recent write wins. Honest limit: this wire is a faithful port of co-op code that was working in real sessions, but full two-machine delivery has not been re-verified (it needs a second machine), so co-op sync is the one part of Ess that has not been proven again. In single-player it still stores locally, so a mod built on these works either way.
nodes.desc_short: Stores a value under a name and pushes it to the other player, so both machines agree on it - a score, a wave...

params.name: key
params.desc: The name to store it under. Both machines use this same name to find it.

params.name: value
params.desc: What to store: a number, text in quotes, true/false, or a small table. Keep it small - this is a channel for state, not for moving files. Numbers stay exact up to about 16 million.

nodes.title: Object: Add Label
nodes.desc: Sticks a text tag onto an object so you (or the game) can find and identify it later - the simplest way to mark the things your script created.
nodes.desc_short: Sticks a text tag onto an object so you (or the game) can find and identify it later - the simplest way to...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to tag.

params.name: sLabel
params.desc: The tag text. Make up your own for your own bookkeeping; be careful reusing the game's own tags like 'PMC' or 'Disposable', as other systems act on those.

nodes.title: Object: Is Alive
nodes.desc: Checks whether something is still alive and in the world - this is the reliable 'is it gone yet' test, unlike Is Valid.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether something is still alive and in the world - this is the reliable 'is it gone yet' test, unlike...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check. Remember both Kill and Remove are deferred - this still reports true for roughly half a second afterwards, so give it a tick or two before you trust a false.

returns.name: alive
returns.desc: True if it is still alive. Safe to use in a plain if - the engine's 1/0 answers are converted to real true/false for you.

nodes.title: Object: Apply Spin
nodes.desc: Gives an object a sudden twist so it SPINS, where the Apply Impulse node shoves it in a straight line. The strength is scaled against the object's weight, so a heavy thing needs a proportionally bigger number than a light one - and see Set Mass if you happen to be tuning both at the same time.
nodes.desc_short: Gives an object a sudden twist so it SPINS, where the Apply Impulse node shoves it in a straight line.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to spin.

params.name: x
params.desc: Twist strength around one of the two tumbling axes. Only the up axis below is confirmed on this engine, so put a value in, watch which way it rolls, and swap if it wasn't the one you wanted.

params.name: y
params.desc: Twist strength around the UP axis - the confirmed one. This is a flat spin on the spot, like a turntable. 500 is a sensible number to try first, scaled up for heavier objects.

params.name: z
params.desc: Twist strength around the other tumbling axis. Same advice as the first one: try it and watch.

params.name: bLocal
params.desc: True spins around the object's OWN axes, false around the fixed world axes. Watch out: this socket defaults to FALSE when left alone, unlike the Apply Impulse node whose matching socket defaults to true.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the call. There is nothing to read a spin rate back from, so this confirms the call went through, not that anything visibly rotated.

nodes.title: Object: Attached Objects
nodes.desc: Lists everything currently stuck to an object - a person's held weapon, gear bolted onto a vehicle, and so on. It always hands back a real list, empty rather than nothing when it fails, so you can loop over the result without checking it first.
nodes.desc_short: Lists everything currently stuck to an object - a person's held weapon, gear bolted onto a vehicle, and so on.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to look at. The player's own character typically comes back with about 5 entries, the weapon they are holding among them.

returns.name: attached
returns.desc: The list of attached things. This is a genuine list you can walk through one entry at a time, unlike some similarly-named engine calls that hand back a sealed collection you cannot read. An empty list means either nothing is attached or the object couldn't be read - it never means an error.

nodes.title: Object: Is Awake
nodes.desc: Tells you whether an object's physics is actively running or has dozed off. The game stops simulating things that have settled, to save work. Careful right after spawning: something created this very instant can read as asleep for a tick before it settles, so give it a beat before you trust a false.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether an object's physics is actively running or has dozed off.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check.

returns.name: awake
returns.desc: True if its physics is simulating right now. False means asleep, which is normal for anything at rest - it is not an error.

nodes.title: Object: Close Gate
nodes.desc: Tells a gate or door object to close - the partner to Open Gate, and carrying the same warning. It has never been tested against a real gate, and the engine reports nothing either way, so a true only means the call did not blow up. Confirm by looking before you rely on it.
nodes.desc_short: Tells a gate or door object to close - the partner to Open Gate, and carrying the same warning.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The gate or door to close. Pointed at anything that is not a gate it fails silently rather than complaining.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the call survived, NOT that anything moved. 'Closed it' and 'that wasn't a gate' look identical from here.

nodes.title: Object: Damage
nodes.desc: Takes a chunk of health off something, and finishes it off properly if that would drop it to zero or below.
nodes.desc_short: Takes a chunk of health off something, and finishes it off properly if that would drop it to zero or below.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to hurt. Leaving this as the player will damage YOU - normally you wire in an enemy or a vehicle.

params.name: nAmount
params.desc: How much health to take off. There is no real 'damage' call in this engine, so this reads health, subtracts your amount and writes it back - and if the result would be zero or less it kills the object outright, because writing 0 health doesn't reliably count as death here.

returns.name: newHealth
returns.desc: The health it has left - 0 if this blow killed it, or nothing at all if its health couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Disable Physics
nodes.desc: Freezes an object's physics so it stops falling and reacting to collisions - useful for pinning a prop in mid-air or stopping a wreck sliding around.
nodes.desc_short: Freezes an object's physics so it stops falling and reacting to collisions - useful for pinning a prop in...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to freeze physics on.

nodes.title: Object: Display Name
nodes.desc: Gets the readable, translated name of something so you can print it on the HUD or in a message - 'Veyron' rather than an internal code.
nodes.desc_short: Gets the readable, translated name of something so you can print it on the HUD or in a message - 'Veyron'...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to name.

returns.name: name
returns.desc: The human-readable name. This is a completely different thing from the object's ID string - use this one for anything a player will read.

nodes.title: Object: Distance
nodes.desc: Measures how far apart two things are, or how far an object is from a fixed map point - one node instead of two different engine calls.
nodes.desc_short: Measures how far apart two things are, or how far an object is from a fixed map point - one node instead of...

params.name: uGuidA
params.desc: The object to measure FROM.

params.name: uGuidBOrX
params.desc: The other object to measure to. To measure to a fixed map point instead, type the X coordinate number here and fill in the next two slots as Y and Z.

params.name: yOrIgnoreY
params.desc: Object-to-object: leave as false, or set true to ignore height (a flat, map-view distance). Point mode: this is the Y (height) coordinate instead.

params.name: z
params.desc: Only used in point mode - the north/south coordinate. Leave alone when measuring to another object.

params.name: bIgnoreY
params.desc: Only used in point mode - true measures flat along the ground and ignores the height difference.

returns.name: distance
returns.desc: Distance in world units, or nothing at all if either object couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Enable Physics
nodes.desc: Turns physics back on for an object so it falls, collides and can be shoved around again.
nodes.desc_short: Turns physics back on for an object so it falls, collides and can be shoved around again.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to re-activate physics on.

nodes.title: Object: Face Another Object
nodes.desc: Turns one object to look at another one's position right now - a one-off snap, not a follow, so re-run it if the target moves.
nodes.desc_short: Turns one object to look at another one's position right now - a one-off snap, not a follow, so re-run it if...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing that should turn.

params.name: uTarget
params.desc: The thing to look at. If this object can't be read, nothing happens.

nodes.title: Object: Face A Point
nodes.desc: Turns an object so it looks at a spot on the map - the everyday 'make this NPC or prop look over there' for a cutscene or a scripted pose.
nodes.desc_short: Turns an object so it looks at a spot on the map - the everyday 'make this NPC or prop look over there' for a...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing that should turn.

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west coordinate of the spot to look at.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height of the spot. Accepted so you can pass a full position straight through, but it is IGNORED - objects only turn left/right, never tilt up or down.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south coordinate of the spot to look at.

nodes.title: Object: Fade Out
nodes.desc: Fades an object away over a few seconds and then DELETES it. This is a delete wearing the costume of a visual effect: unless you deliberately turn the removal off, the object really is gone at the end - confirmed the hard way by a test car that had no weight and no settings left minutes later. It is also delayed, so the object's handle keeps working for the whole fade and only goes stale afterwards.
nodes.desc_short: Fades an object away over a few seconds and then DELETES it.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to fade away. Bear in mind that by default this destroys it, so do not point it at something the mission still needs.

params.name: nDuration
params.desc: How many seconds the fade takes. 10 is the value the game's own scripts use. Leave it alone and you get 10.

params.name: bRemove
params.desc: True (what you get if you leave this alone) deletes the object once the fade finishes. Set it to false explicitly when you only want the visual disappearance and want the object to stay in the world.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the request - not that the fade has finished. Anything still holding this object's handle should re-check it with the Is Valid Handle node after the fade time is up, rather than assuming it survived.

nodes.title: Object: Has Label
nodes.desc: Checks whether an object carries a particular text tag - the way to tell 'is this one of mine' or 'is this a PMC unit' apart from a plain civilian.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether an object carries a particular text tag - the way to tell 'is this one of mine' or 'is this a...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check.

params.name: sLabel
params.desc: The tag to look for. Labels are free-form text that the game itself and other scripts read - real examples are 'PMC', 'Disposable' and 'garage'.

returns.name: hasLabel
returns.desc: True if the object carries that tag.

nodes.title: Object: Heal To Full
nodes.desc: Restores something to its maximum health in one go - the confirmed 'patch me up' move for the player, an ally or a beaten-up vehicle.
nodes.desc_short: Restores something to its maximum health in one go - the confirmed 'patch me up' move for the player, an ally...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to fully heal. Silently does nothing if its max health can't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Health
nodes.desc: Reads how much health something has left, so you can react when it drops - the read side of the health nodes.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how much health something has left, so you can react when it drops - the read side of the health nodes.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The character, vehicle or destructible to read.

returns.name: health
returns.desc: Current health, or nothing at all if the object is dead or invalid.

nodes.title: Object: Height Above Ground
nodes.desc: Reads how far an object is floating above the terrain - the check behind 'is this helicopter airborne' or 'did that prop spawn buried in a hill'.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how far an object is floating above the terrain - the check behind 'is this helicopter airborne' or...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to measure. A reading of exactly 0 is ambiguous - near the player it almost always means genuinely touching the ground, but far away or in a just-loaded area it can be the engine's placeholder for terrain that hasn't loaded yet.

returns.name: height
returns.desc: Distance above the terrain in world units, or nothing at all if it couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Is Hibernated
nodes.desc: Tells you whether the game has parked an object because the player wandered too far away. A hibernated thing still exists and its handle still works, it just stops simulating - so 'the car I spawned froze the moment I drove off' is almost always this and not a bug in your mod. The Set Hibernation Distance node raises the range at which it happens.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether the game has parked an object because the player wandered too far away.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check. The distance that triggers parking belongs to the object itself - a character's is 120 units.

returns.name: hibernated
returns.desc: True if the game has parked it. It has NOT been deleted and its handle is still good; it is simply not running.

nodes.title: Object: Apply Impulse
nodes.desc: Gives an object a sudden physical shove - the raw primitive behind launching cars into the air and knocking people back.
nodes.desc_short: Gives an object a sudden physical shove - the raw primitive behind launching cars into the air and knocking...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to shove.

params.name: x
params.desc: Sideways push strength.

params.name: y
params.desc: Upward push strength. Numbers here are big - real launch code uses values in the thousands, and heavier objects need a proportionally bigger push, so start around 10000 and tune.

params.name: z
params.desc: Forward/backward push strength.

params.name: bLocal
params.desc: True (the default) pushes along the object's OWN facing, so 'forward' means forward for that car. False pushes along fixed world directions.

nodes.title: Object: Is Invincible
nodes.desc: Checks whether something is currently immune to damage - lets you avoid stacking protection or clean it up afterwards.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether something is currently immune to damage - lets you avoid stacking protection or clean it up...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check.

returns.name: invincible
returns.desc: True if it currently can't be damaged. Safe in a plain if - a 1/0 answer from the engine is converted to a real true/false.

nodes.title: Object: Is Attached To
nodes.desc: Checks whether one particular thing is stuck to one other particular thing. The narrow yes/no version of the Attached Objects node, for when you already know both ends and just want confirmation.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether one particular thing is stuck to one other particular thing.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing that might be attached (the child).

params.name: uOther
params.desc: The thing it might be attached to (the parent). Leave either socket empty and you get a plain false back rather than an error.

returns.name: attached
returns.desc: True only if that first thing really is attached to that second thing. Safe to use in a plain yes/no test.

nodes.title: Object: Kill
nodes.desc: Destroys something where it stands, leaving a corpse or a burnt-out wreck behind - one-way, there is no undo beyond Revive.
nodes.desc_short: Destroys something where it stands, leaving a corpse or a burnt-out wreck behind - one-way, there is no undo...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to kill. Leaving this as the player kills YOU - usually you wire in an enemy or a vehicle. The kill is NOT instant: the Alive node still reports true in the same moment you call this and only flips to false a beat later, so check it a tick or two afterwards rather than immediately.

nodes.title: Object: Local Offset To World Point
nodes.desc: Turns an offset measured from an object ('two units to its left, one up') into an actual map position - the correct way to place something relative to a car or a person.
nodes.desc_short: Turns an offset measured from an object ('two units to its left, one up') into an actual map position - the...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object the offset is measured from.

params.name: lx
params.desc: Sideways offset from the object, in world units.

params.name: ly
params.desc: Upward offset from the object, in world units.

params.name: lz
params.desc: Forward offset from the object, in world units.

returns.name: x
returns.desc: Resulting east/west world coordinate.

returns.name: y
returns.desc: Resulting height. This uses the engine's full 3D transform including tilt, so prefer this node over the flat maths helper whenever the object can be leaning - a car on a slope, a listing boat.

returns.name: z
returns.desc: Resulting north/south world coordinate.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Object: Max Health
nodes.desc: Reads the full-health value for something, so you can work out a health percentage for a bar or a 'below half' check.
nodes.desc_short: Reads the full-health value for something, so you can work out a health percentage for a bar or a 'below...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to read the maximum health of.

returns.name: maxHealth
returns.desc: The object's full-health value, or nothing at all if it couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Move To Object
nodes.desc: Teleports one object straight onto another object's position in a single step. Doing it by hand means reading the target's position and then setting it, which is two trips and gives the target a chance to move in between; this does not. For moving the player themselves, the Player: Teleport node is the right tool instead.
nodes.desc_short: Teleports one object straight onto another object's position in a single step.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing that gets moved.

params.name: uTarget
params.desc: The thing to move it ONTO. It lands on exactly that spot, so the two end up overlapping - follow with the Teleport To Position node if you wanted it beside the target rather than inside it.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the move. Empty sockets give a plain false rather than an error.

nodes.title: Object: Open Gate
nodes.desc: Tells a gate or door object to open. TREAT WITH SUSPICION: this has never been tested against a real gate, and the engine says nothing back whether it worked or the object was not a gate at all, so a true here only means the call did not blow up. Watch the gate with your own eyes before you build a mission around it.
nodes.desc_short: Tells a gate or door object to open.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The gate or door to open. Wire in the gate object here - pointed at anything else (a car was tried) it fails silently rather than complaining.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the call survived, NOT that anything moved. This node cannot tell 'opened it' from 'that wasn't a gate' - only looking can.

nodes.title: Object: Parent
nodes.desc: Finds what an object is stuck TO - the opposite direction from the Attached Objects node. One trap worth knowing: the game hands out parent handles from a different number range than ordinary world objects, so what comes back does not necessarily behave like the handle of something you spawned. Run it through the Is Valid Handle node before you feed it anywhere else.
nodes.desc_short: Finds what an object is stuck TO - the opposite direction from the Attached Objects node.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing whose parent you want to know. A handle is just the game's way of pointing at one specific object in the world; you normally get one out of a spawn node or a find node rather than typing it.

returns.name: uParent
returns.desc: What it is attached to. You get nothing at all if it is attached to nothing, or if the object couldn't be read. Check it with Is Valid Handle before passing it on.

nodes.title: Object: Physics Type
nodes.desc: Asks the game what KIND of thing something is and gets a plain word back - a character reports 'human'. This is the honest way to tell a person from a vehicle from a prop, instead of guessing from a model name or from which other nodes happen to work on it.
nodes.desc_short: Asks the game what KIND of thing something is and gets a plain word back - a character reports 'human'.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to classify.

returns.name: sType
returns.desc: The game's own classification word, for example 'human' for a person. You get nothing at all if the object couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Play Material Animation
nodes.desc: Starts one of an object's built-in surface effects by name - the shipped game uses these for things like 'energy_wave' and 'global_weapon_beacon'. This is one of the few nodes whose answer is genuinely worth reading: a name the object does not have comes back FALSE instead of erroring, so it tells you when nothing happened rather than failing silently.
nodes.desc_short: Starts one of an object's built-in surface effects by name - the shipped game uses these for things like...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to run the effect on. Which names work depends entirely on this object's own artwork.

params.name: sName
params.desc: The name of the effect, spelled exactly as the artwork spells it. There is NO way to list an object's valid names from a mod, so take them from the game's own scripts - guessing just gets you a false. A car asked for 'energy_wave', for instance, says no.

params.name: bLoop
params.desc: True repeats the effect over and over until the Stop Material Animation node stops it. Left alone it plays through once.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the effect started. A FALSE here is real information: it means this object has no effect by that name, which is the mistake you most want reported.

nodes.title: Object: Is Player Controlled
nodes.desc: Checks whether a person or vehicle is being driven by a real player rather than the AI - the guard you want before applying an effect meant only for NPCs.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether a person or vehicle is being driven by a real player rather than the AI - the guard you want...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The character or vehicle to check.

returns.name: playerControlled
returns.desc: True if a player is controlling it. Underneath, the engine actually hands back the controlling player's handle rather than a true/false, which would fool a naive check - this node converts it to a proper true/false for you.

nodes.title: Object: Watch For Vehicle Change
nodes.desc: Keeps an eye on someone and runs your code the moment they get into or out of any vehicle - the only workable way to catch this, since the game has no 'entered a vehicle' event for a vehicle you don't already know about.
nodes.desc_short: Keeps an eye on someone and runs your code the moment they get into or out of any vehicle - the only workable...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to watch.

params.name: onChange
params.default: function(uVehicle, uPrevVehicle) Ess.Log(uVehicle and "got in" or "got out") end
params.desc: Your code, run only when they get in or out. It receives the vehicle they're in now (nothing if they just got out) and the one they were in before. If your code errors it is caught and logged, and the watch carries on.

params.name: interval
params.desc: How often to check, in seconds. 0.5 is the default and is responsive enough for getting in and out of cars; smaller numbers react faster but do more work.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Call this to end the watch early - otherwise it keeps running on the framework's normal heartbeat.

nodes.title: Object: Position
nodes.desc: Reads where something is in the world, as three numbers you can feed into teleports, distance checks or spawn points.
nodes.desc_short: Reads where something is in the world, as three numbers you can feed into teleports, distance checks or spawn...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to read the position of - a character, vehicle or prop. Wire one in, or leave it as the player.

returns.name: x
returns.desc: East/west world coordinate.

returns.name: y
returns.desc: Height (up) world coordinate.

returns.name: z
returns.desc: North/south world coordinate.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Object: Remove
nodes.desc: Deletes an object from the world entirely - no corpse, no wreck, just gone. Use this for cleaning up things your script spawned.
nodes.desc_short: Deletes an object from the world entirely - no corpse, no wreck, just gone.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to delete. Removal is DEFERRED: right after this the Alive node still reports true and only reads false about half a second later, so never check for removal in the same breath - and the Valid node stays true even after that, so it is not a usable 'is it gone yet' test at all.

nodes.title: Object: Remove Label
nodes.desc: Takes a text tag back off an object - the undo for Add Label.
nodes.desc_short: Takes a text tag back off an object - the undo for Add Label.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to untag.

params.name: sLabel
params.desc: The exact tag text to remove.

nodes.title: Object: Revert Hibernation Distance
nodes.desc: Puts an object's parking distance back to whatever it originally was, undoing the Set Hibernation Distance node. Verified working (200 raised to 999, reverted, back to 200). Prefer this over noting the old number and writing it back by hand: the game restores that particular object's own built-in default, which depends on what kind of thing it is and may not match whatever you happened to read a moment earlier.
nodes.desc_short: Puts an object's parking distance back to whatever it originally was, undoing the Set Hibernation Distance...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to restore. Safe to run on something you never changed - it just puts back the value that was already there.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the reset.

nodes.title: Object: Revive
nodes.desc: Brings a killed character back, optionally after a short pause - the undo for the Kill node.
nodes.desc_short: Brings a killed character back, optionally after a short pause - the undo for the Kill node.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The dead thing to bring back.

params.name: nDelay
params.desc: Seconds to wait before it stands back up. Leave at 0 for immediate; small values like 0.5 give a beat of drama.

nodes.title: Object: Set Health
nodes.desc: Writes a health value directly onto something - use it to soften a boss or top someone up to an exact number.
nodes.desc_short: Writes a health value directly onto something - use it to soften a boss or top someone up to an exact number.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing whose health you're setting.

params.name: n
params.desc: The exact health value to write. Do NOT use this to kill something - setting health to 0 does not reliably register as a death on this engine; use the Kill node or the Damage node, which kills properly.

nodes.title: Object: Set Hibernation Distance
nodes.desc: Sets how far the player can get before the game parks this object and it stops simulating. Raise it to stop something you spawned freezing the instant you drive away. The shipped game scripts also use it the other way round, with a near-zero value (0.000001) to make a thing park immediately.
nodes.desc_short: Sets how far the player can get before the game parks this object and it stops simulating.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing whose parking range you are changing.

params.name: n
params.desc: The new distance in world units. For scale, a character's built-in value is 120. It must be a number - text is refused and nothing happens. To put it back, use the Revert Hibernation Distance node rather than writing the old figure back yourself.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the change took. Confirmed live by raising 200 to 999 and reading it back.

nodes.title: Object: Set Invincible
nodes.desc: Makes something immune to damage (or takes that immunity away) - the usual way to protect the player during a scripted sequence or keep a mission-critical vehicle alive.
nodes.desc_short: Makes something immune to damage (or takes that immunity away) - the usual way to protect the player during a...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to protect.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to make it invincible, false to make it vulnerable again.

params.name: sReason
params.desc: A short tag saying WHY, like 'Survival' or 'Hijack' or 'HQ'. This framework insists on it so another system can later work out who turned invincibility on; leave it blank and it logs a warning and files it under 'Ess'.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the change.

nodes.title: Object: Set Mass
nodes.desc: Changes how heavy the game believes an object is, in kilograms. Verified live by taking a car from 1800 up to 5000. Remember this quietly changes how every push and every spin affects that object, so if you are tuning impulse strengths, check you have not moved the weight underneath them at the same time.
nodes.desc_short: Changes how heavy the game believes an object is, in kilograms.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to re-weigh.

params.name: nKg
params.desc: The new weight in kilograms. For scale, a car starts around 1800, so 5000 makes it distinctly harder to shove around. It must be a number - text is refused and nothing happens.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the change took. This is one you can genuinely confirm: the Impulse: Mass node reads the weight straight back out.

nodes.title: Object: Set Name
nodes.desc: Gives an object a name of your own choosing, which is what makes it findable afterwards by the Find By Name and Probe: All By Name nodes. Verified end to end: a spawned car was named, then looked up by that exact string, and the right car came back. Note the one-way street though - you can SET a name and you can look one UP, but this engine gives you no way to READ a name back off an object.
nodes.desc_short: Gives an object a name of your own choosing, which is what makes it findable afterwards by the Find By Name...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to name. Naming things you spawn is the easiest way to get hold of them again later from another part of your mod.

params.name: sName
params.desc: The name to give it. Pick something distinctive that the game itself is unlikely to have used, or your lookups will find its objects as well as yours. It has to be text - anything else is refused and nothing happens.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the name was accepted. The real test is to look the name up afterwards and see whether your object comes back.

nodes.title: Object: Teleport To Position
nodes.desc: Instantly moves an object to a world position - solid for props, vehicles and a just-spawned object, but unreliable on freshly-spawned or AI people, who streaming and physics can snap straight back.
nodes.desc_short: Instantly moves an object to a world position - solid for props, vehicles and a just-spawned object, but...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to move. To move the PLAYER use the Player Teleport node instead - this one is unreliable on humans.

params.name: x
params.desc: Destination east/west coordinate. Usually wired in from an Object Position node rather than typed.

params.name: y
params.desc: Destination height. Too low buries it in terrain, too high drops it - add a few units if unsure.

params.name: z
params.desc: Destination north/south coordinate.

nodes.title: Object: Set Unkillable
nodes.desc: Stops something from DYING, which is not the same thing as stopping it being hurt. Set Invincible blocks the damage; this lets the damage land but refuses the death. A mission that wants an NPC shot to pieces and still standing wants this one, not that one.
nodes.desc_short: Stops something from DYING, which is not the same thing as stopping it being hurt.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing that should refuse to die.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to make it unkillable, false to let it die normally again.

params.name: sReason
params.desc: A short tag saying WHY, like 'Mission' or 'Escort'. The game counts these per tag, so two different systems can each switch it on and each switch it off again without cancelling one another - which is exactly why you want your own tag rather than the shared default. Left blank, it is filed under 'Ess'.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the engine accepted the change.

nodes.title: Object: Set Visible
nodes.desc: Shows or hides an object without deleting it - it stays in the world and keeps working, it just stops being drawn.
nodes.desc_short: Shows or hides an object without deleting it - it stays in the world and keeps working, it just stops being...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to show or hide.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True to show it, false to make it invisible.

nodes.title: Object: Set Facing Angle
nodes.desc: Spins an object to a given heading on the spot - handy for lining up a spawned vehicle or posing a prop.
nodes.desc_short: Spins an object to a given heading on the spot - handy for lining up a spawned vehicle or posing a prop.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to turn.

params.name: n
params.desc: The new facing angle. Degrees vs radians is unconfirmed on this engine, so the safe habit is to take a value from the Facing Angle node and add to it rather than typing a raw number.

nodes.title: Object: Size
nodes.desc: Reads how big an object's model is in each direction - use it to space spawns out so they don't overlap, size a camera orbit, or work out where to attach something.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how big an object's model is in each direction - use it to space spawns out so they don't overlap, size...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: A LIVE object to measure - this takes a real spawned thing, not a template name, even though it's asking about a model. On an object spawned this very instant it reports zeros; wait a beat and read it again.

returns.name: ex
returns.desc: Width of the model's bounding box.

returns.name: ey
returns.desc: Height of the model's bounding box.

returns.name: ez
returns.desc: Length of the model's bounding box.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Object: Snap To Ground
nodes.desc: Drops (or lifts) an object so it sits neatly on the terrain - the tidy-up for anything you spawned that ended up floating or half-buried.
nodes.desc_short: Drops (or lifts) an object so it sits neatly on the terrain - the tidy-up for anything you spawned that ended...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to place on the ground.

params.name: nOffset
params.desc: How far ABOVE the ground to leave it, in world units. 0 sets it right down; a small number like 1 gives a little clearance so it doesn't clip in.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if it moved. False means it was left alone - either its position couldn't be read, or its ground height read exactly 0, which is either already-grounded or unloaded terrain, and skipping is safe either way.

nodes.title: Object: Spawn At Position
nodes.desc: Creates a new vehicle, person or prop at an exact map position - the one node in this group that makes something out of nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Creates a new vehicle, person or prop at an exact map position - the one node in this group that makes...

params.name: sTemplate
params.desc: The name of the thing to create, e.g. 'Veyron' for a car or 'VZ Soldier' for an enemy. Never leave this blank or all-spaces: a blank name hard-crashes the game outright, so this node refuses it and logs a warning instead.

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west coordinate to place it at. Usually wired from an Object Position node - if you just want it in front of the player, use the Spawn Ahead node instead and skip the coordinates.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height to place it at. Follow with a Snap To Ground node if you aren't sure of the terrain height.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south coordinate to place it at.

params.name: yaw
params.desc: Which way it should face once created. Leave this out entirely to keep whatever orientation the game gives it.

returns.name: uGuid
returns.desc: The thing that was created - wire this into other nodes. You get nothing back if the name was blank or the game refused to create it.

nodes.title: Object: Spawn Ahead Of Player
nodes.desc: Creates something a set distance in front of the player, already facing the same way - saves you working out the 'in front of me' maths by hand.
nodes.desc_short: Creates something a set distance in front of the player, already facing the same way - saves you working out...

params.name: sTemplate
params.desc: The name of the thing to create, e.g. 'Veyron' for a car or 'VZ Soldier' for an enemy. A blank name would hard-crash the game, so it is refused before anything happens.

params.name: nDist
params.desc: How far in front to place it, in world units. 18 is the default and leaves comfortable room for a car.

params.name: nHeight
params.desc: How far above the player's feet to place it, in world units. Leave at 0 for ground level; raise it for aircraft or a mid-air drop.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player to spawn in front of. 0 is you; 1 is the co-op partner, which does not exist in single-player, in which case nothing is spawned and a warning is logged.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Extra settings. By default 'in front of' means in front of the character's BODY - stand still and swing the camera and your view turns but your chest doesn't, so it can appear off to one side. Set useView = true to place it where you are LOOKING instead, which is what usually feels right; that safely falls back to body facing if you're aiming at open sky.

returns.name: uGuid
returns.desc: The thing that was created - wire this into other nodes. You get nothing back if the player has no character yet or the game refused to create it.

nodes.title: Object: Speed
nodes.desc: Reads how fast something is going as a single number, ignoring direction - the easy 'is this car moving' check.
nodes.desc_short: Reads how fast something is going as a single number, ignoring direction - the easy 'is this car moving' check.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to read. On an object spawned this very instant this comes back empty - wait a beat after spawning and read it again.

returns.name: speed
returns.desc: Speed in world units per second, or nothing at all if it couldn't be read.

nodes.title: Object: Speed Squared
nodes.desc: The cheaper cousin of Speed for 'is it faster than X' tests that run every frame - compare against your threshold multiplied by itself instead of the plain number.
nodes.desc_short: The cheaper cousin of Speed for 'is it faster than X' tests that run every frame - compare against your...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to read. On an object spawned this very instant this comes back empty - wait a beat after spawning and read it again.

returns.name: speedSq
returns.desc: Speed multiplied by itself. It skips the square root, so it's the cheapest option - but it is NOT a real speed, so only ever compare it against another squared number.

nodes.title: Object: Stop All Animation
nodes.desc: Stops every animation running on an object at once, instead of naming them one at a time - useful for tidying up after effects you started and lost track of. True here only means the call went through, not that anything was actually playing.
nodes.desc_short: Stops every animation running on an object at once, instead of naming them one at a time - useful for tidying...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to silence. This clears every channel, so anything the game itself was animating on that object stops too.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the call went through.

nodes.title: Object: Stop Material Animation
nodes.desc: Stops one named surface effect that the Play Material Animation node started. Unlike that node, this one does NOT catch a wrong name: it answers true as long as the call went through, so a typo here fails quietly and the effect keeps running. If you just want everything off, the Stop All Animation node is the surer bet.
nodes.desc_short: Stops one named surface effect that the Play Material Animation node started.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The object to stop the effect on.

params.name: sName
params.desc: The name of the effect to stop, spelled exactly as you spelled it when starting it. It has to be text - anything else is refused and nothing happens.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the call went through. It says nothing about whether that effect was playing or has actually stopped.

nodes.title: Object: Is Valid Handle
nodes.desc: Checks that a handle still points at something the engine recognises - a guard against passing junk into other nodes, NOT a check that the thing still exists.
nodes.desc_short: Checks that a handle still points at something the engine recognises - a guard against passing junk into...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The handle to sanity-check. Warning: this stays true even after an object has been removed and Is Alive has already flipped to false - the handle outlives the object, so use Is Alive to ask whether something is gone.

returns.name: valid
returns.desc: True if the engine still recognises this handle.

nodes.title: Object: Vehicle Of Character
nodes.desc: Finds the vehicle a person is currently sitting in, whether they're driving or just riding along - the reliable way to grab 'the car the player is in'.
nodes.desc_short: Finds the vehicle a person is currently sitting in, whether they're driving or just riding along - the...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to check.

returns.name: uVehicle
returns.desc: The vehicle they're in, counting passenger seats as well as the driver's, or nothing at all if they're on foot.

nodes.title: Object: Velocity
nodes.desc: Reads which way and how fast something is moving, split into three directions - the basis for chase cameras, race checks and 'has it stopped yet'.
nodes.desc_short: Reads which way and how fast something is moving, split into three directions - the basis for chase cameras,...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to read. On an object spawned this very instant this comes back empty - wait a beat after spawning and read it again.

returns.name: vx
returns.desc: Sideways component of the movement.

returns.name: vy
returns.desc: Upward component of the movement.

returns.name: vz
returns.desc: Forward/backward component of the movement.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Object: Is Visible
nodes.desc: Checks whether an object is currently drawn on screen rather than hidden.
nodes.desc_short: Checks whether an object is currently drawn on screen rather than hidden.

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing to check.

returns.name: visible
returns.desc: True if the object is being drawn. This is a genuine true/false from the engine, unlike the visibility check on UI widgets.

nodes.title: Object: Facing Angle
nodes.desc: Reads which way an object is turned, so you can copy that heading onto something else or nudge it by a fixed amount.
nodes.desc_short: Reads which way an object is turned, so you can copy that heading onto something else or nudge it by a fixed...

params.name: uGuid
params.desc: The thing whose facing you want to read.

returns.name: yaw
returns.desc: The facing angle. Whether this is degrees or radians is NOT confirmed on this engine, so read a yaw, change it, and write it back - that stays self-consistent either way.

nodes.title: Objective: Counted Goal
nodes.desc: The lightest of the three mission tools: ONE counted goal on the HUD objective line, with no mission engine behind it. It shows 'Collect intel 2/5', ticks up each time you advance it, and fires your completion callback when the count reaches the target. Use it when you want a real, stateful goal but a whole Contract would be overkill. Give it an id and it becomes reload-safe: creating another one with the same id silently cancels the old one first, so re-running your script never leaves a stale goal stuck on screen.
nodes.desc_short: The lightest of the three mission tools: ONE counted goal on the HUD objective line, with no mission engine...

params.name: opts
params.default: { label = 'Collect intel', target = 5, id = 'collect_intel', onComplete = function() Ess.Easy.Toast('Intel secured!') end }
params.desc: The goal spec. `label` is the text on the HUD; `target` is how many are needed (default 1 - the counter is only shown when it is above 1). `id` makes it reload-safe. `onComplete` fires when the count is reached, `onProgress(count, target)` on every step, `onFail` if you fail it. `slot` picks which HUD objective line to use (default 1) and `show = false` hides it entirely while still counting.

returns.name: objective
returns.desc: The live goal. Call `:advance(n)` to add to the count, `:set(n)` to set it outright, `:progress()` for count and target, `:isDone()`, `:label(s)` to change the wording, or `:complete()` / `:fail()` / `:cancel()` to end it early. The HUD line clears itself when it ends.

nodes.title: On: Object Dies
nodes.desc: Do something when one specific thing you already have a handle for is killed or destroyed. This is a real engine event, not a poll, so it costs nothing while it waits. Something only dies once, so it fires once - call the stop if you armed it and no longer care.
nodes.desc_short: Do something when one specific thing you already have a handle for is killed or destroyed.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The thing to watch, wired in from whatever spawned or found it. If this is empty the hook is NOT armed and will never fire - silently, unless Ess.DEBUG is on. A hook that never fires is the quietest failure here, so check this first when nothing happens.

params.name: fn
params.desc: What to do when it dies. It gets no information about who killed it - this engine has no 'who shot me' event.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it (or feed it to an Ess.stop node) to release the hook early.

nodes.title: On: Player Enters Area
nodes.desc:
Fires the moment a player walks into a circle on the map, then stops itself - it is a ONCE hook, so it will not nag every tick. It works by checking four times a second, comparing flat map distance only, so height is ignored: a player on a rooftop directly above the spot counts as inside.

Arming it twice gives you two independent watchers, so keep the stop for each.
nodes.desc_short: Fires the moment a player walks into a circle on the map, then stops itself - it is a ONCE hook, so it will...

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west centre of the circle. Usually wired from an Object Position node rather than typed.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height of the centre. Only passed back to your callback - it is NOT used to decide who is inside.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south centre of the circle.

params.name: r
params.desc: Radius in world units. Too small and a player can run through the gap between two checks a quarter-second apart.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs once on entry. It is handed the player's east/west and north/south position, but the MIDDLE value is the height you passed in above, not the player's own height.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player: 0 is you. 1 is the co-op partner, who usually does not exist in single-player.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it to cancel the watcher if the player never turns up. After it fires, it has already cleaned itself up.

nodes.title: On: Player Leaves Area
nodes.desc: Fires the moment a player leaves a circle, then stops itself. It only counts as leaving once they have actually BEEN inside, so arming this while the player is on the other side of the map will not fire straight away - it waits for them to come in and go out again. Flat map distance, checked four times a second.
nodes.desc_short: Fires the moment a player leaves a circle, then stops itself.

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west centre of the circle.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height of the centre. Passed back to your callback but NOT used to decide who is inside.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south centre of the circle.

params.name: r
params.desc: Radius in world units.

params.name: fn
params.default: function(px, py, pz) Ess.Easy.Toast('left the area') end
params.desc: Runs once on the way out. It is handed the player's east/west and north/south position, but the MIDDLE value is the height you passed in above, not the player's own height.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player: 0 is you.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it to cancel the watcher before it ever fires.

nodes.title: On: Health Drops Below
nodes.desc:
Fires once when something has lost enough health, then stops itself. Good for a scripted 'the boss is nearly down' beat.

The percentage is measured against the health it had when you ARMED this, not its maximum - arm it on an already wounded enemy and 50% means half of what was left. It checks a bit over twice a second.
nodes.desc_short: Fires once when something has lost enough health, then stops itself.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The thing to watch.

params.name: pct
params.desc: The threshold as a percentage of its health at arm time. Leaving it empty means 50.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs once when the threshold is crossed, given the health value that tripped it.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it to cancel the watch if it becomes irrelevant - otherwise it keeps polling until the threshold is crossed.

nodes.title: On: While Player Inside Area
nodes.desc:
Runs your action AGAIN AND AGAIN, four times a second, the whole time a player is standing in the circle - a live zone, for draining health, holding a capture point or keeping a prompt on screen.

This one NEVER stops itself. It keeps polling forever even when the player is nowhere near, so you must keep the stop and call it, or it is a leak that outlives your feature.
nodes.desc_short: Runs your action AGAIN AND AGAIN, four times a second, the whole time a player is standing in the circle - a...

params.name: x
params.desc: East/west centre of the circle.

params.name: y
params.desc: Height of the centre. Passed back to your callback but NOT used to decide who is inside.

params.name: z
params.desc: North/south centre of the circle.

params.name: r
params.desc: Radius in world units.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs on EVERY check while they are inside - four times a second. Keep it cheap, and do not leave a toast in the real version or you will bury the screen. The middle value it is handed is the height you passed in above, not the player's own.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player: 0 is you.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: You MUST keep this - it is the only thing that ends the zone. Call it, or feed it to an Ess.stop node or a tracker.

nodes.title: On: Labeled Object Found
nodes.desc:
The way to FIND things by the label the map designers gave them - collectible boxes, scripted props - which you cannot simply ask the engine for. It fires once for each matching object as it comes near a player and streams into memory.

Each object is remembered and excluded after its first hit, so it never fires twice for the same one. Distant objects do not exist yet, so streaming, not your radius, is the real limit on what you can find. If the label is empty or that player has no character, the hook is NOT armed and nothing will ever fire.
nodes.desc_short: The way to FIND things by the label the map designers gave them - collectible boxes, scripted props - which...

params.name: sLabel
params.desc: The world label objects carry, spelled exactly. A wrong label is not an error - you just never get a single hit.

params.name: nRadius
params.desc: How near a player they have to come, in world units. Leaving it empty means 300.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs once per object as it is discovered, given that object's handle - mark it, count it, or hold on to it.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player things have to come near: 0 is you.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it to stop discovering. Without it the search stays armed for the rest of the session.

nodes.title: On: Player Takes Damage
nodes.desc:
Runs every time a player's health goes DOWN, and keeps repeating for as long as you let it - the feasible version of 'I got hit' on this engine, since there is no real damage event and no way to know who hit you.

It polls five times a second, so several quick hits can read as one bigger drop. It never stops itself: keep the stop.
nodes.desc_short: Runs every time a player's health goes DOWN, and keeps repeating for as long as you let it - the feasible...

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs on each drop, given the new health and how much was just lost. Healing does not fire it - only drops.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player: 0 is you.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this - it is the only way to end the watcher. Call it, or feed it to an Ess.stop node or a tracker.

nodes.title: On: Game Announcement
nodes.desc: Listens for the GAME's own announcements and runs your work when one arrives. Every other On node watches the world by checking it over and over; this one is told directly by the shipped game, so it costs nothing while it waits and it knows things you could not otherwise detect - the moment the PDA is opened, a GPS beacon dropped, an airstrike called. The names are fixed strings you cannot guess, so copy one from the list on the event name socket.
nodes.desc_short: Listens for the GAME's own announcements and runs your work when one arrives.

params.name: sName
params.desc: Which announcement to listen for, spelled EXACTLY as the game posts it - spaces and capitals included. Real ones: "PDA Open", "PDA Close", "GPS Beacon Set", "GPS Beacon Cleared", "Support Menu Open", "SupportUsed", "Airstrike", "MunitionsPickup", "RecruitAvailable", "MedevacComplete", "oilrigDestroyed". A name the game never posts is not an error - you simply never fire, which is the quietest way for this node to disappoint you. If the box is left blank the hook is NOT armed at all.

params.name: fn
params.desc: What to do when the announcement arrives. It is handed the extra details the game sent along, as a table - for a GPS beacon that includes the coordinates. Some announcements send nothing, so check before reading anything out of it. If this is empty the hook is NOT armed and will never fire.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it (or feed it to an Ess.stop node) to stop listening. Without it the hook stays armed for the rest of the session.

nodes.title: On: Every Few Seconds
nodes.desc:
The simplest repeater: do this every so often, forever, until you stop it. It never stops itself.

WATCH OUT: unlike Loop: Start this names itself a new name every time, so arming it twice gives you TWO loops doing the same work - there is no name to replace. In a script that re-runs on a key press, use Loop: Start with a fixed name instead.
nodes.desc_short: The simplest repeater: do this every so often, forever, until you stop it.

params.name: interval
params.desc: Seconds between runs. Leaving it empty means one second.

params.name: fn
params.desc: What to do each time. Unlike Loop: Start you do NOT return anything here - it always keeps going.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this. Calling it (or feeding it to an Ess.stop node, or a tracker) is the only way to end this repeater.

nodes.title: On: Player Enters Or Exits Vehicle
nodes.desc:
Runs whenever a player gets into or out of a vehicle, and keeps repeating. Your action is handed what they are in now and what they were in before, so you can tell the two apart: nothing now means they just got out.

If that player has no character - asking for the co-op partner in single-player does exactly this - the hook is NOT armed, and the stop it hands back does nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Runs whenever a player gets into or out of a vehicle, and keeps repeating.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Runs on each change, given the vehicle now and the one before. On foot, the first is nothing.

params.name: i
params.desc: Which player: 0 is you. Player 1 usually does not exist in single-player, and asking for them leaves this hook unarmed.

returns.name: stop
returns.desc: Keep this and call it to end the watcher. It never stops itself.

nodes.title: PDA: Allow Mission Change
nodes.desc: Controls whether the player may change which mission they are tracking from inside the PDA - turn it off during a scripted stretch where switching objectives would break your mod. Note that the engine ignores a 'true' on a network client, so a joined player always has it disallowed no matter what you set.
nodes.desc_short: Controls whether the player may change which mission they are tracking from inside the PDA - turn it off...

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True lets the player pick a different mission to track, false locks them to whatever is tracked now.

nodes.title: PDA: Set Faction Attitude
nodes.desc: Sets how a faction's stance towards the player is shown on the PDA's database screen. This is DISPLAY ONLY - it changes the readout and nothing else. Who actually shoots at whom lives in the Ess.Relations nodes, so change both if you want the screen and the world to agree.
nodes.desc_short: Sets how a faction's stance towards the player is shown on the PDA's database screen.

params.name: sFaction
params.desc: The faction's code in capitals: PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR or VZ. Anything outside that list is not recognised and shows no faction at all. Cannot be blank.

params.name: nAttitude
params.desc: The attitude value the database screen displays. The scale it uses is not documented anywhere in the Ess source, so try a number and look at the screen rather than assuming - it is display-only, so a wrong value cannot break anything.

params.name: sTexture
params.desc: Optional picture to show alongside the attitude. Leave it empty for the default.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the change was handed to the PDA. False only when the faction code was left blank.

nodes.title: PDA: Beacon Tutorial Mode
nodes.desc: Switches the map into the mode that prompts the player to drop a GPS beacon - the same nudge the game's own GPS tutorial uses. Pair it with the Ess.Gps nodes if you want to react to where they actually put it.
nodes.desc_short: Switches the map into the mode that prompts the player to drop a GPS beacon - the same nudge the game's own...

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True shows the place-a-beacon prompt on the map, false returns the map to normal.

nodes.title: PDA: Add Map Blip
nodes.desc:
Puts a marker on the PDA's big map, including the one thing the Mark nodes cannot do: a blip at a FIXED PLACE with nothing behind it, for a destination, a search area, or where something used to be.

It also closes two traps that make a blip look like it never happened. A blip with no drawable icon is INVISIBLE - placed and hoverable, but nothing on screen until the cursor is over it, because the engine's own last-resort icon ('icon_yellow_mc') is a registered name that draws no art at all. And a blip with NO LABEL displays its texture name instead - a real unlabelled blip read 'icon_verify_1_mc' on the map. So this node fills in a working icon and uses the blip's own name as its label. Those two defaults are deliberately skipped when the blip belongs to a mission, so the mission's icon and label can come through instead. Blips are never tidied up for you - remove one with PDA: Remove Map Blip, or hand it to a tracker.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a marker on the PDA's big map, including the one thing the Mark nodes cannot do: a blip at a FIXED PLACE...

params.name: sName
params.desc: The blip's private id - what you pass to PDA: Remove Map Blip later, and (unless you set sLabel) the text the player sees on the map. Cannot be blank.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Where the blip sits and how it looks. nX/nY place it at a fixed spot, and read these carefully: they are WORLD coordinates, nY is world Z (north/south), NOT height - a top-down map has nowhere to show height - and THE X AXIS IS MIRRORED, so increasing world X moves the blip LEFT across the PDA. That was measured with four blips in a known cross; nothing in the scripts says so, the flip happens inside the map's Flash movie. Use uGuid instead of nX/nY to stick the blip to an object. The rest: sLabel and sDesc name and describe it in the PDA's own list; sTexture picks the icon from Ess.Pda.ICONS (never 'icon_yellow_mc' - it is a real name that draws nothing), and sTexture = false genuinely opts out of an icon; sMission ties the blip to a registered mission, which makes it inherit that mission's icon and label, turn sticky while that mission is tracked, and become selectable as the tracked objective; nMeter, bSticky, bTodoList, sFaction (defaults to 'PMC') and nSortOrder (defaults to 5) round it out.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the blip was handed to the PDA. False only when the name was left blank.

nodes.title: PDA: Add Or Edit Dossier Entry
nodes.desc: Adds an entry to the PDA's reference database - the section the player reads to learn who somebody is or what something means. Writing to a title that already exists EDITS that entry instead of adding a duplicate, so this is also how you update a dossier as the story moves on.
nodes.desc_short: Adds an entry to the PDA's reference database - the section the player reads to learn who somebody is or what...

params.name: sTitle
params.desc: The entry's heading, and also its identity: use the same title again and you overwrite the existing entry rather than creating a second one. Cannot be blank.

params.name: sText
params.default: Everything known about them so far.
params.desc: The body the player reads when they open the entry. Anything you pass is turned into text for you; leave it out and the entry exists but says nothing, which is rarely what you want.

params.name: sIcon
params.desc: Optional picture shown beside the entry. Leave it empty and the entry simply renders without one.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the entry was handed to the PDA. False only when the title was left blank.

nodes.title: PDA: Fake Player Location
nodes.desc: Draws the 'you are here' marker somewhere other than where the player actually is. The game itself does this inside the PMC base, where the real position means nothing on a world map. Leave all three sockets empty to put the marker back where it belongs - and note the engine ignores the call unless all three coordinates are real numbers, which is why this node refuses a half-filled set instead of letting it vanish.
nodes.desc_short: Draws the 'you are here' marker somewhere other than where the player actually is.

params.name: x
params.desc: World east/west of the spot to draw the marker at.

params.name: y
params.desc: World height. Fill it in even though a flat map has nowhere to show height - the engine drops the whole call if any one of the three is missing.

params.name: z
params.desc: World north/south of the spot.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the marker was moved, or cleared when all three were left empty. False if you filled in some coordinates but not all three.

nodes.title: PDA: Add Log Line
nodes.desc: Writes a permanent line into the player's PDA journal - the running record of what happened, which they can pause and scroll back through. This is the one way a mod leaves a lasting trace instead of a message that flashes for a few seconds and is gone, and it is what makes a mission read like part of the game.
nodes.desc_short: Writes a permanent line into the player's PDA journal - the running record of what happened, which they can...

params.name: sMessage
params.desc: The line to write. Try not to start it with a square bracket: the PDA reads '[Something]' as a lookup into the game's own text database and '[red]' as a colour tag, so a leading bracket either recolours your line or prints the brackets on screen. Cannot be blank - this node refuses an empty message rather than writing nothing.

params.name: tOpts
params.desc: Extras, all optional. sType picks which section of the log the line lands in - 'objective', 'event' or 'dialog', the three the shipped game uses and all three confirmed to display live. sName is a short label beside the line (the game always passes an empty one, so that is the default). sColor is a BARE hex colour with no '#' and no '0x', e.g. '3399FF', which is the game's own event blue and the default here.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the line was handed to the PDA. False only when the message was left blank.

nodes.title: PDA: Add Or Update Mission
nodes.desc:
Registers a mission with the PDA so the game treats it as a real objective: blips can belong to it, it shows up in the mission list, and the player can track it. Using a name that already exists updates that mission instead of adding a second one, and any field you leave out keeps its old value.

The trap that catches everyone: a BRAND NEW mission is rejected outright unless sLabel, sDesc AND sFaction are all supplied - the engine does nothing at all and says nothing about why, so this node checks up front and explains instead. And it cannot tell you whether the mission was really created, because the engine throws that answer away - so it always reports true, and PDA: Mission Exists is the only honest check.
nodes.desc_short: Registers a mission with the PDA so the game treats it as a real objective: blips can belong to it, it shows...

params.name: sName
params.desc: The mission's private id - what a blip's sMission points at, and what every other PDA mission node takes. This is not what the player reads; that is sLabel. Cannot be blank.

params.name: tOpts
params.default: { sLabel = "Blow The Bridge", sDesc = "Destroy the river crossing.", sFaction = "PMC" }
params.desc: The mission's details. sLabel (its name in the PDA list), sDesc (its description) and sFaction (one of PMC, AN, CH, GR, OC, PR, VZ - anything else resolves to no faction at all) are ALL THREE REQUIRED for a new mission; miss one and the entire call is thrown out. When updating a mission that already exists you can pass only the fields you want changed. The rest: sIcon is the default icon for blips that belong to this mission and sBlipLabel their default label - leave sBlipLabel out and the map literally prints 'DESIGNER ERROR', which is the game's own placeholder, not a fault in your mod. bTrackable starts true for a new mission; to change it afterwards use PDA: Set Mission Trackable, which is the route that actually works. bSuppress hides the mission and forces it untrackable, and nSortOrder is its place in the list.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the call was MADE, not that the mission exists - the engine discards the real answer, so nothing here can promise more than that. False means this node refused the call: a blank name, or a new mission missing sLabel, sDesc or sFaction.

nodes.title: PDA: Mission Exists
nodes.desc: Asks whether a mission name is really registered with the PDA - the only existence test there is, because every other PDA call throws its success away. It works by briefly selecting the mission and reading back what stuck (the engine only stores a name it recognises), then putting the player's previous selection back, so it is safe to run at any time. It is not free, though: every check writes a debug line and, in multiplayer, fires a network event - ask once, do not poll it every frame.
nodes.desc_short: Asks whether a mission name is really registered with the PDA - the only existence test there is, because...

params.name: sName
params.desc: The mission id you registered with PDA: Add Or Update Mission. Cannot be blank.

returns.name: bExists
returns.desc: True if the PDA knows this mission. False if it was never registered, or if its registration was quietly rejected for missing a required field.

nodes.title: PDA: On Mission Tracked
nodes.desc: Runs your code whenever the player tracks or untracks a mission in their PDA. One handler covers both, and you tell them apart by what arrives: tracking hands you the mission's id, untracking hands you nothing at all. Unlike the Ess.On events there is no stop handle, because the game keeps only ONE handler here - registering a second one replaces the first.
nodes.desc_short: Runs your code whenever the player tracks or untracks a mission in their PDA.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Your handler. It receives the newly tracked mission's id as its one argument, and is called with NOTHING when the player untracks - so 'if sMission then ... else ... end' is how you branch between the two. Leave it empty to unregister the current handler.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True once the handler was registered (or cleared). False if what you passed was not a function.

nodes.title: PDA: Shade Map Region
