returns.desc: Y of the resulting point.

returns.name: z
returns.desc: Z of the resulting point.

nodes.promoted_from_getter: multi-value return cannot be spliced inline as an expression

nodes.title: Vehicle: Clear Controls
nodes.desc: Releases whatever inputs are currently being held down on a vehicle - throttle, steering and the rest. The shipped game scripts call it at the end of a scripted drive when handing control back, so the vehicle does not carry on pressing the accelerator by itself.
nodes.desc_short: Releases whatever inputs are currently being held down on a vehicle - throttle, steering and the rest.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to let go of.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Close Door
nodes.desc: Shuts a named door or hatch again - the partner to Vehicle: Open Door, and it takes the same door names. Same caution about the result: it tells you the call did not error, not that the vehicle has that door or that it closed.
nodes.desc_short: Shuts a named door or hatch again - the partner to Vehicle: Open Door, and it takes the same door names.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle whose door should close.

params.name: sDoor
params.desc: The door's name, as text - the same two known names as the open node: "DriverHatch" and "pivot". Use the name you opened with.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True only means the call ran without erroring, not that a door closed.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Driver
nodes.desc: Gets whoever is behind the wheel or at the controls of a vehicle - also the way you get a helicopter's PILOT handle, which is what the flight and landing orders want.
nodes.desc_short: Gets whoever is behind the wheel or at the controls of a vehicle - also the way you get a helicopter's PILOT...

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to look inside.

returns.name: uChar
returns.desc: The driver's character handle, or nil if the seat is empty. A freshly spawned vehicle has no driver for a moment, so an immediate read can come back nil.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Enable Turret
nodes.desc: Switches a vehicle's turret on or off by name. Turning it off does not remove the gun, it just stops it responding - which is what the shipped hijack scripts do to freeze a tank's turret while someone is climbing onto it.
nodes.desc_short: Switches a vehicle's turret on or off by name.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle carrying the turret.

params.name: sTurret
params.desc: Which turret, by name. The names that appear in the game's own scripts are "main_turret" (a tank's big gun) and "head" (the smaller traversing head).

params.name: bEnable
params.desc: False freezes the turret, true wakes it up again.

params.name: sAxis
params.desc: Optional - limits the change to one axis of movement instead of the whole turret. The only values seen in the game's scripts are "all" and "pitch" (the up/down axis). Leave it empty to get the engine's own default; the node quietly picks between the engine's short and long forms depending on whether you filled this in.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the call ran without erroring. It cannot tell you whether this vehicle actually has a turret by that name.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Enter Best Seat
nodes.desc: Puts a character into a vehicle, taking the best free seat automatically in driver, gunner, passenger, cargo order - the everyday 'get in' node.
nodes.desc_short: Puts a character into a vehicle, taking the best free seat automatically in driver, gunner, passenger, cargo...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person who should board.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to board. CAUTION from live testing: spawning a vehicle and immediately boarding it from INSIDE the PMC HQ interior stalled the whole Lua tick for 30+ seconds, and needed the game killed. Do this out in the open world, and do not chain another query on the very next line - leave a beat.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the boarding call went through.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Enter Seat (Excluding)
nodes.desc: Boards a vehicle but skips seats you name - built for 'get in but never take the wheel', such as a co-op partner boarding a car the other player is already driving.
nodes.desc_short: Boards a vehicle but skips seats you name - built for 'get in but never take the wheel', such as a co-op...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person who should board.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to board.

params.name: excludeSeats
params.desc: A list of seat codes to refuse: "d" driver, "g" gunner, "p" passenger, "c" cargo. The remaining types are tried in that same priority order. Blocking the driver seat is the usual case: { "d" }.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the character actually got into a seat.

returns.name: sSeatTypeUsed
returns.desc: Which seat code they ended up in ("d"/"g"/"p"/"c"), or nil when every allowed seat was full or missing.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Evict Everyone
nodes.desc: Forces every occupant out of a vehicle at once - the bulk version of the exit node, for clearing an enemy truck or emptying a heli before you take it.
nodes.desc_short: Forces every occupant out of a vehicle at once - the bulk version of the exit node, for clearing an enemy...

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to empty. This one wants the VEHICLE's own handle, not a rider's or a pilot's - confirmed live, the driver read as real before the call and nil after.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the call went through.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Exit
nodes.desc: Gets one named character back out of a vehicle - the missing other half of the boarding nodes.
nodes.desc_short: Gets one named character back out of a vehicle - the missing other half of the boarding nodes.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to get out of. Note the order here: the VEHICLE comes first, the person second.

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person getting out.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the exit went through.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Fly Helicopter To Point
nodes.desc: Sends an AI helicopter to a spot in the sky, handling the two things that trip people up: a plain move-to order does not fly a helicopter, and a freshly spawned one has no pilot for a moment.
nodes.desc_short: Sends an AI helicopter to a spot in the sky, handling the two things that trip people up: a plain move-to...

params.name: uHeli
params.desc: The helicopter to send. It needs a pilot - a crewed '(Driver)' or '(Full)' template. This node keeps checking every 0.15s until the pilot exists and only then issues the order, so it is safe to call the instant you spawn one.

params.name: x
params.desc: Destination east/west coordinate.

params.name: y
params.desc: Destination height. Y is up; give it real altitude or it will try to fly into the ground.

params.name: z
params.desc: Destination north/south coordinate.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Extra settings: height = the drop height (default 0.5), careless = true for a less cautious approach, onReady = a function run once the order is actually issued, handy for hanging a camera on the pilot.

returns.name: cancel
returns.desc: Call this to abort the wait-for-pilot loop early if you change your mind before the order goes out.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Follow Ghost
nodes.desc: Spawns a stand-in object you can keep moving around - a live preview marker for placement tools - and hands back a little object with the controls to move or delete it.
nodes.desc_short: Spawns a stand-in object you can keep moving around - a live preview marker for placement tools - and hands...

params.name: template
params.desc: The template name to spawn, exactly as the game spells it. A blank name is refused on purpose because an empty spawn crashes the game to desktop.

params.name: x
params.desc: Where to first place it: east/west coordinate.

params.name: y
params.desc: Starting height.

params.name: z
params.desc: Starting north/south coordinate.

returns.name: ghost
returns.desc: An object with ghost.guid (the CURRENT handle), ghost:update(x,y,z) to move it and ghost:remove() to delete it - or nil if the spawn failed. IMPORTANT: moving a spawned HUMAN by position silently does nothing on this engine, so update() detects that and quietly despawns and re-spawns instead, which CHANGES the handle. Always read ghost.guid fresh off the object, never cache it.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Is Flipped
nodes.desc: Tells you whether a vehicle has rolled onto its roof or side, so you can offer a respawn or a nudge.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether a vehicle has rolled onto its roof or side, so you can offer a respawn or a nudge.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to check.

returns.name: bFlipped
returns.desc: True when it is upside down. There is deliberately NO unflip node - no reliable way to right a vehicle has been verified on this engine, so the usual answer is an upward Impulse Push or a fresh spawn.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Is Flying
nodes.desc: Tells you whether a vehicle is airborne under power right now - helicopters and planes. It also fixes a genuine engine trap on the way: the raw engine call returns NOTHING (not false) for a vehicle that cannot fly at all, confirmed live on a ground car, so the natural-looking test "is flying equals false" is never true for a car and silently never fires. This node always gives you a proper true or false.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you whether a vehicle is airborne under power right now - helicopters and planes.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to check. Anything can be asked - a car simply answers false rather than misbehaving.

returns.name: bFlying
returns.desc: True when it is in the air. Always a real true or false, including for ground vehicles, so it is safe to compare against either.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Land Helicopter
nodes.desc: Orders an AI helicopter to descend and set down on the ground.
nodes.desc_short: Orders an AI helicopter to descend and set down on the ground.

params.name: uHeliOrPilot
params.desc: The helicopter, or its pilot directly - either works. BIG TRAP confirmed live: a heli still running its own combat AI simply IGNORES this and keeps flying. Send it somewhere with Vehicle Fly To first, then land it - that pattern gave a real measured descent.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when the order was issued. That is not a promise it actually descended - see the trap above.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Open Door
nodes.desc: Opens a named door or hatch on a vehicle. Read the result carefully: unlike Set Part, a failure here does NOT mean "no such door" - on a test car with neither known door, both door calls came back empty, and no confirmed success case was ever measured to compare against. Treat the answer as "the call did not error" and confirm with your own eyes.
nodes.desc_short: Opens a named door or hatch on a vehicle.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle whose door should open.

params.name: sDoor
params.desc: The door's name, as text. Only two names show up in the whole game script corpus: "DriverHatch" and "pivot". Ordinary cars have neither - this is for vehicles that actually have a modelled hatch, like armour.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True only means the call ran without erroring. It is not proof the door exists on this vehicle or that anything visibly moved.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Orbit Flight
nodes.desc: Flies a crewed helicopter a few circular laps around a point - the 'victory lap' flight - by chaining a ring of timed waypoints for you.
nodes.desc_short: Flies a crewed helicopter a few circular laps around a point - the 'victory lap' flight - by chaining a ring...

params.name: uHeli
params.desc: The helicopter to fly. It must already have a pilot - a '(Driver)' or '(Full)' template - an empty airframe will not move.

params.name: cx
params.desc: East/west coordinate of the point to circle.

params.name: cy
params.desc: Ground height at the centre point. The orbit height below is added on top of this, and because the first leg is already up in the air the heli climbs into the circle by itself - no separate takeoff order needed.

params.name: cz
params.desc: North/south coordinate of the point to circle.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Flight shape: radius (90), height above the centre (45), orbits (2), points per lap (6), secPerLeg (2.2), startAngle in degrees, tracker to register the timers for cleanup, onDone = a function run after the last leg.

returns.name: totalSeconds
returns.desc: How long the whole flight will take, so you can time a camera move or the next beat to match it.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Repair And Rearm
nodes.desc: Fully heals a vehicle and refills its weapons in one go - the between-round fixup for a wave defence, an escort patch-up, or mercy on a smoking ride.
nodes.desc_short: Fully heals a vehicle and refills its weapons in one go - the between-round fixup for a wave defence, an...

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to fix up.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if the heal went through. The rearm is best-effort and is not reported separately.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Rider In Seat
nodes.desc: Tells you exactly who is sitting in one specific seat, or nothing if it is empty. This is the precise version of the riders list, which only says who is aboard somewhere - use this when you care about the gunner's chair in particular.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you exactly who is sitting in one specific seat, or nothing if it is empty.

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: The seat handle to look inside - one particular chair, not the vehicle. Get one with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "g", true), where the letter picks the kind of seat: "d" driver, "g" gunner, "p" passenger, "c" cargo.

returns.name: uChar
returns.desc: The character sitting in that seat, or nothing at all if it is empty.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Riders
nodes.desc: Lists everyone currently aboard a vehicle so you can count occupants, heal a whole crew, or check whether it is worth blowing up.
nodes.desc_short: Lists everyone currently aboard a vehicle so you can count occupants, heal a whole crew, or check whether it...

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to look inside.

returns.name: tRiders
returns.desc: A list of character handles. Always a real list, empty rather than nil when there is nobody aboard or the vehicle cannot be read.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Is Seat Blocked
nodes.desc: Asks whether a seat is unusable right now - something in the way, or somebody already in it. Worth checking before you order a character to board or transfer, so you are not issuing a move that quietly does nothing.
nodes.desc_short: Asks whether a seat is unusable right now - something in the way, or somebody already in it.

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: The seat handle to test - one particular chair, not the vehicle. Get one with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "d", true) using "d"/"g"/"p"/"c" for driver/gunner/passenger/cargo, or take one from the Vehicle: Seat Transfers node.

returns.name: bBlocked
returns.desc: True when the seat cannot be used at the moment. Note that a handle which is not a seat at all also reads false, so a false is not by itself proof the seat is fine.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Seat Info
nodes.desc: Hands back everything the engine knows about one seat, as a table of yes/no flags: what the seat is for (IsDriver, IsGunner, IsCargo), whether the hijack system can target it (IsHijackable, IsHijackBlocker), how exposed whoever sits there is (IsRiderVulnerable, IsRiderBashable, IsRiderInvisible), and its stow-away pairing (IsStowable, StowSeatGuid). Always check you got something back: a handle that is not really a seat gives you nothing at all rather than an empty table.
nodes.desc_short: Hands back everything the engine knows about one seat, as a table of yes/no flags: what the seat is for...

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: A seat handle - the game's reference to one particular chair inside a vehicle, NOT the vehicle itself. Pass the vehicle by mistake and you get nothing back. Get a real one with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "d", true), where the letter picks the kind of seat: "d" driver, "g" gunner, "p" passenger, "c" cargo.

returns.name: tParams
returns.desc: The engine's own table of seat flags, passed through untouched so the key names match exactly what the engine calls them. Nothing at all if the handle was not a seat.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Is Seat A Ladder
nodes.desc: Ladder "seats" are climbing points, not places to ride - but the engine hands them back from exactly the same seat lookups as real seats. If you loop over a vehicle's seats looking for somewhere to put a character, use this to skip them, or you will end up assigning someone to a rung.
nodes.desc_short: Ladder "seats" are climbing points, not places to ride - but the engine hands them back from exactly the same...

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: The seat handle to test - one particular chair, not the vehicle. Get one with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "d", true) using "d"/"g"/"p"/"c" for driver/gunner/passenger/cargo.

returns.name: bLadder
returns.desc: True when this "seat" is really a ladder or climb-over point rather than somewhere to sit.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Seat Of Character
nodes.desc: Tells you which seat a character is sitting in, if any - the quick way to check 'are they driving or just along for the ride'.
nodes.desc_short: Tells you which seat a character is sitting in, if any - the quick way to check 'are they driving or just...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to ask about.

returns.name: sSeat
returns.desc: The seat they occupy, or nil if they are not in a vehicle.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Seat Transfers
nodes.desc: Lists the seats a rider can slide across to from this one without getting out - feed one of them straight into the Vehicle: Transfer To Seat node. Do not be thrown by an empty list: that is the common case, and a plain car's driver seat gives back zero entries.
nodes.desc_short: Lists the seats a rider can slide across to from this one without getting out - feed one of them straight...

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: The seat to start from - one particular chair, not the vehicle. Get one with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "d", true) using "d"/"g"/"p"/"c" for driver/gunner/passenger/cargo.

params.name: bIncludeAll
params.desc: False asks for the everyday reachable seats; true asks the engine for its wider set. Exactly what the wider set adds has never been pinned down, so if you need it, run both on your vehicle and compare the lists.

returns.name: tSeats
returns.desc: A list of seat handles. Always a real list and never nothing, so it is safe to loop over straight away - an empty one simply means there is nowhere to slide to.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Set Player Can Use Seat
nodes.desc: Lets you allow or forbid the player getting into one particular kind of seat. The game's own scripts use it to reserve a helicopter's pilot seat so you have to ride along instead of flying it yourself. Trap: what it hands back is ambiguous - denying the driver seat on a live car reported false, and nobody has pinned down whether that is the new state, the old state, or a refusal - so judge it by trying to board, not by the result.
nodes.desc_short: Lets you allow or forbid the player getting into one particular kind of seat.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to lock or unlock a seat on.

params.name: sSeatType
params.desc: Which kind of seat, as a single letter in quotes: "d" driver, "g" gunner, "p" passenger, "c" cargo. This is a seat TYPE, not a particular chair - it covers every seat of that kind on the vehicle.

params.name: bCan
params.desc: False locks the player out of that seat type; true gives it back.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: Do not trust this one - see the warning above. Verify by actually trying to get in.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Set Part On Or Off
nodes.desc: Switches a named part of a vehicle on or off - in practice this is nearly always lights. It is the one node in this group whose answer you can actually trust: a real part reports true and a name the vehicle does not have reports false (checked live with a made-up name), so a typo is caught instead of silently doing nothing. That makes it safe to try a part name you are unsure about.
nodes.desc_short: Switches a named part of a vehicle on or off - in practice this is nearly always lights.

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle to change. A guid is just the game's handle for a thing that exists in the world - wire in whatever a spawn or lookup node gave you, or leave this as the vehicle the player is currently in.

params.name: sPart
params.desc: Which part, by name. These are the only names that appear anywhere in the game's own scripts: "LightFront" (headlights, by far the most used), "LightBrake" (brake lights), "CtrlRotation" (rotation control). Nothing can list a vehicle's parts for you, so guessing is the only option - but a wrong guess just comes back false, it does not break anything.

params.name: bOn
params.desc: True switches the part on, false switches it off.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True when this vehicle really has that part and the switch went through. False means a bad handle or no such part on this vehicle - unusually for this namespace, that answer is genuinely worth checking.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Aim Turret
nodes.desc: Points a turret up/down and left/right from one node - the engine keeps those on two separate calls and you almost always want both. Leave an angle empty to leave that axis exactly where it is. Trap: this reported success on a car with no turret at all, so a true here means "nothing errored", not "the gun moved".
nodes.desc_short: Points a turret up/down and left/right from one node - the engine keeps those on two separate calls and you...

params.name: uVeh
params.desc: The vehicle carrying the turret.

params.name: sTurret
params.desc: Which turret to point, by name - the same names as the enable node: "main_turret" and "head".

params.name: nPitch
params.desc: The up/down angle. Leave this empty and the up/down aim is left untouched. The scale is not pinned down - the only value seen in the game's own scripts is 0, which recentres the axis, so expect to try a few numbers and watch what the barrel does.

params.name: nYaw
params.desc: The left/right angle. Leave this empty and the left/right aim is left untouched. Same caveat about the scale as the up/down angle.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True if at least one of the two aim calls ran. Leave BOTH angles empty and you get false, because nothing was actually asked for.

nodes.title: Vehicle: Transfer To Seat
nodes.desc: Slides someone already aboard into a different seat without them climbing out and walking round - a gunner taking over the driving, say. Find out where they are allowed to move first with the Vehicle: Seat Transfers node; a plain car's driver seat has nowhere to slide to, so this is really for multi-seat vehicles like helicopters and armour.
nodes.desc_short: Slides someone already aboard into a different seat without them climbing out and walking round - a gunner...

params.name: uChar
params.desc: The person to move. They have to be in the vehicle already - this shuffles seats, it does not board anyone.

params.name: uSeat
params.desc: The seat to move them INTO - a handle for one particular chair, not the vehicle. Take one straight out of the Vehicle: Seat Transfers node, or ask for one by kind with Vehicle.GetSeatByType(vehicle, "d", true), where the letter is "d" driver, "g" gunner, "p" passenger or "c" cargo.

params.name: bForce
params.desc: True pushes the move through, false is the polite version that can be refused. The game's own scripts pass false.

returns.name: ok
returns.desc: True means the call ran without erroring - it is not a promise the character ended up in that seat. Confirm with Vehicle: Rider In Seat.

nodes.title: Last Error
nodes.desc: This is how you find out why nothing happened. Ess fails silently on purpose - a stale handle or a missing argument gives you nothing back rather than crashing the game - so the last swallowed failure gets parked here. The routine: notice nothing happened, turn debug on with a Lua line reading Ess.DEBUG = true, do the thing again, then read this. Only failures recorded while debug was on carry a label saying which call it was.
nodes.desc_short: This is how you find out why nothing happened.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: A small record: .msg is what went wrong, .label is which call (only filled in while debug was on), .count is how many failures there have been this session. Nothing at all if nothing has failed yet.

nodes.title: Stop
nodes.desc: Turns off anything Ess handed you - a hook, a marker, a running loop's name, a tracker, an objective. Ess ended up with 27 different words for 'turn this off', one per namespace, so 'how do I stop this' had no learnable answer. This is the one node that takes any of them. Every namespace's own stop still works; this is the one to reach for when you are just holding a handle and want it gone.
nodes.desc_short: Turns off anything Ess handed you - a hook, a marker, a running loop's name, a tracker, an objective.

params.name: x
params.desc: Whatever the node that started the thing handed back - a stop function, a marker handle, a loop name in quotes, a tracker. Wire it straight in. Leaving it empty is harmless, it just does nothing.

returns.name: stopped
returns.desc: True if something was really torn down. False means it was empty or Ess did not recognise it - with debug on it logs exactly which.

nodes.title: Stop All
nodes.desc: Stops every handle in a list, working backwards from the end. Backwards is deliberate: things you set up later usually lean on things you set up earlier, so tearing down in reverse is the order that does not surprise. Use it when your mod keeps a list of everything it started.
nodes.desc_short: Stops every handle in a list, working backwards from the end.

params.name: tHandles
params.desc: A plain list of handles, e.g. { h1, h2, h3 }. It must have no gaps: if you emptied slots out by setting them to nil, Lua cannot be trusted to report the list's length and some entries may be left running without telling you.

returns.name: count
returns.desc: How many of them actually stopped.

skipped.reason: A programmer's helper for hand-built freecam controls - it hands back an object whose update method must be called from inside every controller-input event, which a node graph has no way to do.

Hands back the running scene's internal bookkeeping object, which nothing else in a node graph can use - Is A Cutscene Playing answers the real question, and Stop already targets whichever scene is running.
Internal teardown of a running mission's spawns, events and markers - happens automatically when a contract ends.
Internal - faction stances are declared with the mission's `relations` list, not applied by hand.
Internal end-of-mission routine (payout, fanfare, cleanup); use Cancel Mission, or let the objectives resolve.
Internal bookkeeping bucket the engine uses to track and clean up one objective's spawns and events.
Internal counterpart to the relations setup - runs automatically when the mission ends.
Internal single-objective runner; it needs a live mission instance no mod author ever holds.
Internal objective-list runner - the mission's `objectives` list and the Objective Group node express this already.
Internal - mission units are declared with the definition's `units` list, which this spawns for you.
Internal - started automatically from the definition's `timeLimit` and `fail` entries.
Internal - started automatically from the definition's `support`, `triggers` and `waypoints` entries.
Internal event-bus trigger the framework uses to fire follower events; it takes open-ended extra arguments, and beginners subscribe with the On Event node instead.
Internal raw order primitive with no markers and no automatic return to following - the Order Everyone and Order Team nodes are the ones to use.
Internal core shared by Order Everyone and Order Team; exposed only so ordering one team cannot clash with another team's order.
the expert raw-numbers channel; Co-op: On Message receives the same traffic as ordinary Lua values instead of hand-packed numbers.
sends a hand-packed array of raw numbers on the expert channel; Co-op: Send Message covers the same wire with ordinary values.
returns a magic proxy table whose whole point is `S.field = x` assignment syntax, which a graph cannot express; Co-op Set/Get reach the same store.
needs a hand-written closure that re-reads a live variable on every heartbeat; Co-op: Set Shared Value covers pushing a value you already have.
the namespaced form of Co-op: Get Shared Value; a second near-identical node only invites picking the wrong one.
replaces a live engine callback and takes two hand-written functions plus a module table that must be import()ed in the same file first.
the namespaced form of Co-op: Set Shared Value; a second near-identical node only invites picking the wrong one.
targets an engine module table that only exists after an import() in the same file, which an emitted graph cannot do, and each table's row shape is its own recipe.
replaces a live engine function with a hand-written wrapper that has to invoke callOriginal itself; not expressible from a graph.
resolves a vehicle to its driver so AI orders land; the AI Orders nodes already do this internally and Vehicle Driver reads the same thing.
the raw engine order call, whose args table (AIGuid/Goal/Target/Priority) must be hand-assembled; the AI Orders nodes assemble it correctly.
sets the movement speed of an order already in flight; on its own there is nothing to speed up - it belongs to the AI Orders node's speed option.
a pure string lookup that turns 'hi' into 'HiPri'; it touches nothing in the game.
the raw unscaled shove in the engine's side/up/forward axis order; Impulse Push does the same thing with the mass scaling that makes it feel the same on a bike and a tank.
the raw off-centre shove behind Impulse Spin, with the lever-arm offset and mass scaling left for you to work out.
reads an object's mass, which the tier above already exposes as Impulse Mass.
places only the PDA blip and hands back a name you must store yourself; Mark Object covers it as one opt-out of a single marker.
